findings.name: Agentforce Life Sciences
findings.detail: Agentforce Life Sciences brings customer, clinical, and patient engagement together on a single, connected platform. As a Salesforce admin or implementer, use this guide to help you set up your organization for success with Agentforce Life Sciences.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. Note Life Sciences Cloud is now Agentforce Life Sciences. You may see references to Life Sciences Cloud in your org and in this guide. Agentforce Life Sciences supports three integrated domains: Customer Engagement drives compliant, orchestrated provider interactions, with visibility into territory alignment, brand messaging, and medical insights. Clinical Engagement supports intelligent clinical operations, simplifies site selection and patient recruitment, and connects patients, sites, sponsors, and contract research organizations (CROs). Patient Engagement powers benefit verification, eligibility coordination, and program tracking, with real-time insight into outcomes and adherence risks. We've divided this guide into sections that cover the setup for each domain. Set Up Customer Engagement explains how to get your org ready to install the Customer Engagement managed package, which contains Customer Engagement features. You can then set up the features for Account Management, Engagement Planning, Engagement Execution, and so on. This section also explains how to set up the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app for iOS (iPad only), which is available in the Apple App Store . Set Up Clinical Engagement explains how to set up clinical engagement features, such as Participant Management and Site Management. Set Up Patient Engagement explains how to set up patient engagement features such as Financial Assistance Programs, Patient Program Outcomes, and Pharmacy Benefits Verification.

findings.name: Set Up a Field Rep’s First Visit with AI Skills
findings.detail: Configure a new Life Sciences org for field sales representatives through a guided conversation with an AI coding assistant, such as Claude Code or Agentforce Vibes, and Salesforce CLI. When you ask the assistant to set up Life Sciences, the Customer Engagement set up skill validates prerequisites, deploys the starter configuration, creates a three-level territory hierarchy, assigns the representative and admin to the territory, provisions a field sales representative, creates test visit data, and summarizes the results. You can validate the test visit created by the skill in the Life Sciences Cloud Mobile. Note Built-in Guardrails: The agent always verifies your org's record data first and prompts for your approval before performing any org-wide actions.

findings.name: Scenario
findings.detail: Maya, a Life Sciences admin has a supported Salesforce org with the Agentforce Life Sciences for Customer Engagement managed package installed and needs to prepare it for a field sales representative. Instead of completing the setup steps individually, Maya asks the AI coding assistant to set up Life Sciences for field sales representatives. The Customer Engagement set up skill checks if the org is ready for set up, deploys the selected starter configuration, proposes and creates a territory hierarchy, provisions the representative, creates test visit data, and provides a summary for review. Maya then validates the test visit data using the mobile experience on an iPad.

findings.name: Requirements
findings.detail: Permissions Available to users with the Health Cloud Starter permission set and the Life Sciences Commercial Admin permission set. Editions and Licenses Available in Lightning Experience in Enterprise and Unlimited editions with the Life Sciences Cloud license and the Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement add-on license, and where the Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement managed package is installed. Prerequisites A blank Life Sciences Cloud org. A supported AI coding assistant, such as Claude Code or Agentforce Vibes Salesforce CLI Git jq Salesforce Skills installed from https://github.com/forcedotcom/sf-skills . Applicable only for Claude. For Agentforce Vibes, the skills are automatically installed. Note The Life Sciences skills don’t install the managed package. If the package isn’t available in your org, contact your Salesforce account team or provisioning admin. Suggested Technology and Experience Recommended for Salesforce admins who are comfortable navigating Salesforce Setup and running AI coding tools. Use a supported AI coding assistant in an org connected through Salesforce CLI. You must be able to install and run Salesforce CLI, Git, and jq. Note No prior experience for managing territory is required to run this setup.

findings.name: Available AI Skills
findings.detail: Automate the setup of a new Life Sciences Cloud org using these AI skills: Life Sciences Skills | Skill Type | Exact Skill Name | What the Skill Does Field Sales Coordinator | Coordinating skill | life-sciences-fieldsalesrep-coordinate | Runs the complete field sales setup. It validates prerequisites, deploys the starter configuration, configures territories, provisions a field sales representative, and creates test visit data. Prerequisites Validator | Subskill | life-sciences-prerequisites-validate | Checks whether the connected org meets the Life Sciences prerequisites. It reports passes, failures, and warnings and provides steps to resolve issues. It doesn’t change org settings. Territory Configurator | Subskill | life-sciences-territory-configure | Creates a territory type, a territory model, and a three-level hierarchy consisting of a region, district, and territory. It asks for approval before activating the territory model.

findings.name: Agentic Tips
findings.detail: Connect Salesforce CLI to the org that you want to configure and run the assistant with admin access and the required permission sets. Review each summary and confirm each change before continuing. If a required step fails, the coordinating skill stops before it begins dependent configuration and explains how to resolve the issue. Choose the page layouts and Lightning pages to deploy when prompted. Review the territory hierarchy and warning before approving territory-model activation. Review changes to Multiple Currencies, State and Country/Territory Picklists, and Person Accounts with your implementation team. You can’t reverse these actions after completing them. Validate the mobile experience manually on an iPad.

findings.name: Design Considerations
findings.detail: Keep these design considerations in mind when you set up Customer Engagement with an AI coding assistant. The required managed package must already be installed. The Life Sciences skills don’t install it. The setup skill can’t complete a secure browser sign-in or respond to authentication prompts. The prerequisite skill performs read-only checks. It identifies passes, failures, and warnings and provides remediation steps, but it doesn’t change failed org settings. Differences from recommended Account and Case sharing defaults produce warnings because the appropriate access model depends on your implementation. The territory skill asks for approval before activating the model. An activated territory model can be deactivated but can’t be deleted. The standalone territory skill creates the hierarchy but doesn’t assign users. The source provides Claude Code installation and skill-management commands and identifies Agentforce Vibes as an alternative supported AI client. findings.name: Configure Customer Engagement
findings.detail: Accelerate time to market and reduce setup complexity for field sales representatives by using an AI assistant to automatically deploy starter configurations, establish territory hierarchies, and provision test visit data in a new Life Sciences Cloud org. These steps require certain editions and permissions. See Requirements for details. Connect the assistant to the target org and install Salesforce Skills. Connect the assistant to the target org through Salesforce CLI as an admin with the required access. Create a Salesforce DX project. Install Salesforce Skills in the project. If you use Claude Code, from the project directory run this command. ! npx skills add forcedotcom/sf-skills --agent claude-code --skill '*' --project --copy Reload the skills registry with /reload-skills , and verify the registered skills with /skills . If you use Agentforce Vibes, skip the install. Skills are installed and updated automatically. Ask the assistant to check that the org is ready for Life Sciences setup. For example, enter “Set up Life Sciences for a field sales representative in my connected org.” Review the read-only prerequisite checks that the assistant runs for admin access, required permission sets, Life Sciences settings, sharing recommendations, and supporting Salesforce features. Review each category marked Pass, Fail, or Warning. Follow the remediation steps for each failure, and review each warning with your implementation team. Before the assistant deploys or creates configuration, confirm the setup plan. Tell the assistant to deploy the Life Sciences starter configuration. The deployment includes objects, profiles, configuration records, layouts, and FlexiPages. When the assistant asks which page layouts and Lightning pages to include, select the pages you want. When the assistant asks for approval to deploy, approve the deployment. Review the deployment summary, and resolve any failure before you continue. Review the territory hierarchy, and tell the assistant to create it. Review the proposed names for the territory type, territory model, region, district, and territory. Accept the names or provide replacements. Review the proposed three-level hierarchy and record-access settings. Accounts have Read access, Contacts have Edit access, and Cases and Opportunities have no access. Tell the assistant to create the territory type, territory model, region, district, and territory. Review the activation warning, and approve activation only when the hierarchy and access settings are correct. Create the field sales representative user and assign the required access. Review the user details that the assistant fills in, and update them if needed. The assistant fills in the first name, last name, email, username, and alias. The email address is required so the representative can receive notifications and the password link. After the assistant creates the user, open the email inbox and copy the temporary password. Sign in with the representative’s credentials, and create a new password when prompted. Tell the assistant to assign the required permission set, and then verify the permission sets and territory assignment. Review the provisioning summary, and confirm that the representative is active and has the required access and territory assignment. Ask the assistant to create test visit data, and then confirm the visit in the iPad app. Tell the assistant to create a test provider visit. Tell the assistant to generate the mobile metadata required to validate the field sales experience in the Life Sciences Cloud iPad app. Install the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app on your iPad. Sign in to the Life Sciences Cloud iPad app with the representative’s credentials, and confirm that the visit appears. Note The initial sync downloads org data and the mobile metadata cache. The first sign-in can take 3 to 5 minutes. From the Home page, go to the Visits tab, and then tap the visit name to open the details page. Confirm that the target visit appears in the list and opens without errors. For example, confirm that Visit 00000001 for Dr. Aaron Morita appears. You can ask the assistant, “Do you see Visit 00000001 for Account Dr. Aaron Morita in the iPad app?” Confirm that the assistant created the test records in this order. Step | Object / Entity | Required Parent / Lookup | Key Fields & Configuration | Verification Criteria 1 | Account | None (Root) | Account Name, Owner | Record exists (e.g., Dr. Aaron Morita) and is owned by the field sales rep. 2 | Healthcare Provider | Account (AccountId) | Provider Details | Linked directly to the created Account record. 3 | Visit | Account (AccountId) & Territory (Territory2Id) | Visit Name, Owner, Territory | Record exists (e.g., Visit 00000001), owned by the rep, and mapped to the Level-3 Territory. 4 | Provider Visit | Visit & Healthcare Provider | Junction Details | Correctly links the Visit record to the target Healthcare Provider. 5 | Product Detailing | Visit | Product & Discussion Details | Sample and discussion records are populated and attached to the Visit. Review the Life Sciences Cloud setup summary. When setup finishes, check each area in the Life Sciences Cloud Setup Complete summary. Prerequisites: Confirm every org prerequisite. Deployments: Verify that objects, profiles, configuration records, <N> layouts, <N> FlexiPages, and 28 trigger handlers are deployed and active. Territory structure: Confirm that territory model is active and includes level-3 territory. User and permissions: Verify that user <firstName> <lastName> (<username>) has the LSC Custom Profile and these permission sets. Life Sciences Core Life Sciences Field Sales Representative Health Cloud Starter Life Sciences Key Account Management Confirm that both the user and the admin are assigned to the right territory name. Records and cache: Check that the account, healthcare provider, and visit under the created territory are present, along with product detailing records and the generated mobile metadata cache. Confirm that the summary displays this message: “The org is ready for Life Sciences Cloud field sales workflows.”

findings.name: Supported Platform Features and Components in Agentforce Life Sciences
findings.detail: Learn which automation features the Agentforce Life Sciences desktop (Lightning web) experience supports and which automation features the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app supports. Also, learn which Salesforce Platform features, Lightning templates, and standard Lightning page components the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app supports.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. This page documents the Salesforce Platform features, automations, and Lightning components that the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app supports, and how and when they run compared to the desktop (Lightning web) experience. For a feature-by-feature comparison of the mobile app and desktop UI, see Compare the Life Sciences Cloud Mobile App and Desktop Site .

findings.name: Supported Automation Features in Agentforce Life Sciences
findings.detail: Learn which automation features the desktop (Lightning web) experience supports, and which automation features the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app supports when users are online or offline. The Life Sciences Cloud mobile app uses an offline-first architecture with a local database on the device. Field reps can create and edit records without a connection, so server-side automations don't run at the moment a record is saved on the device. Instead, the app defers server-side execution until it syncs with the Salesforce platform. At sync, automations such as Apex triggers, flows, and platform events run on the server. Plan your automation design around this behavior, because logic that a user expects to run at save time on the desktop site runs only after a sync on the mobile app. Feature / Automation Type | Desktop (Lightning Web) | Mobile App (Online) | Mobile App (Offline) Agentforce (Note summarization using a prompt feature that runs on the server side and updates the record in Salesforce, which syncs to the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app) | Supported | Supported. Agents require the Salesforce Server connectivity. | Not supported. Agentforce Life Sciences Trigger Handlers | Supported | Supported. Agentforce Life Sciences triggers on the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app are not native Apex triggers. However, the logic is simulated in the iOS framework to work on local devices. | Supported. Agentforce Life Sciences triggers on the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app are not native Apex triggers. However, the logic is simulated in the iOS framework to work on local devices. Apex Trigger (Insert, After, Delete, Undelete) | Supported | Not supported. Triggers don’t execute locally in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. Instead, they fire on the Salesforce platform server-side when the mobile app initiates a sync. | Not supported. Triggers don’t execute locally in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. Instead, they fire on the Salesforce platform server-side when the mobile app initiates a sync. Flow - Before Save & After Save (Automations) | Supported | Not supported. Flows don’t execute locally in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. Instead, they run on the Salesforce platform and are triggered server-side when the mobile app synchronizes its data. | Not supported. Flows don’t execute locally in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. Instead, they run on the Salesforce platform and are triggered server-side when the mobile app synchronizes its data. Lightning Web Components (LWC) | Supported | Limited connectivity support. LWCs requiring server data only function with an active internet connection. Offline use causes load failures or errors. | Custom LWCs lack native SQLite access in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app because they run in an isolated JavaScript context. Without a built-in bridge API, developers must create a custom Swift-based iOS bridge to query or modify local data, as this functionality is not provided out-of-the-box. Mulesoft-based Automation | Supported | Not supported. Mulesoft -based automation executes on the Salesforce platform server-side when the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app initiates a sync. | Not supported. Mulesoft -based automation on the Salesforce platform server-side when the mobile app initiates a sync. Platform Events & Change Data Capture | Supported | Not supported. Platform Events execute on the Salesforce platform server-side when the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app initiates a sync. | Not supported. Platform Events execute on the Salesforce platform server-side when the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app initiates a sync. Screen Flows | Supported | Not supported. | Not supported. Transaction Boundaries | Supported | Supported. Transaction boundaries occur on the Salesforce platform server-side when the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app initiates a sync. This deferred transaction model explains why server-side automations (triggers, flows, platform events) don't execute locally on the device. | Supported. Transaction boundaries occur on the Salesforce platform server-side when the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app initiates a sync. This deferred transaction model explains why server-side automations (triggers, flows, platform events) don't execute locally on the device. Validation Rules | Supported | Supported. Validation messages are shown before the record is saved. No sync required. | Supported. Validation messages are shown before the record is saved. No sync required.

findings.name: Supported Platform Features in Agentforce Life Sciences
findings.detail: Learn which Salesforce Platform features are supported in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. Platform Features | Supported? | Comments Account Hierarchy | No | Use Dynamic Tree View Components for Life Sciences as a replacement. Bulk Update on List View | Partially Supported | The Life Sciences Cloud mobile app supports simultaneous updates for up to 100 account or account-related records only. This feature is unavailable for non-account parent objects, such as Account Plans or other Life Sciences Cloud-specific objects. Chatter | No | Chatter is not supported as a comprehensive collaboration tool within the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app, meaning features like feeds, groups, posts, and comments are unavailable. Furthermore, the application lacks a native user interface for engaging with Chatter groups or feeds. Console App Navigation | No | The Salesforce Console framework isn’t supported within the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. Therefore, features such as utility bars, subtabs, workspace tab navigation, and split-view workspaces are unavailable. Einstein Activity Capture (EAC) for Calendar Sync | No | EAC calendar sync partially supports Life Sciences Cloud via standard events, email and tasks but lacks native ProviderVisit (Visit) support. Evaluate AppExchange products/vendors if you’re looking for Visit specific sync features. Permission Set Groups | No | Permission Set Groups aren’t supported on the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. Instead, use profiles or individual permission sets to assign user permissions. Recently Viewed List View on Objects | No | Across all objects, the standard Recently Viewed filter and list view functionality is unsupported within the Life Sciences Cloud mobile application.

findings.name: Mobile Support for Lightning Page Templates
findings.detail: In the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app, Lightning page templates support the mobile form factor, allowing organizations to design pages tailored specifically for field rep workflows on handheld devices. When you build Agentforce Life Sciences pages for mobile app deployment, select a phone form factor template in the Lightning App Builder to ensure the layout and components render correctly within the mobile runtime. Template Type | Supported Layout App Page | One Region Home Page | Standard Home Page Record page | Header and One Region

findings.name: Mobile Support for Standard Lightning Page Components
findings.detail: Salesforce designs standard Lightning components, many of which are available for use on Lightning pages. This section outlines which components the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app supports or doesn't support. Also, learn about the custom Lightning page components available in Agentforce Life Sciences. Component Name | Supported? | Comments Accordion | Yes | The Life Sciences Cloud mobile app fully supports the Accordion component. Activities | No | The standard Salesforce Activity Timeline component isn't compatible with the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. Instead, the app uses a custom Activity Timeline designed to support a specific range of objects. The app doesn’t natively show standard events, tasks, or other objects. However, it includes out-of-the-box support for the these features: Assessment Task Email Transaction Medical Inquiry Survey Response Visit App Launcher | No | The Life Sciences Cloud mobile app doesn't support the App Launcher component. Blank Space | No | The Life Sciences Cloud mobile app doesn't support the Blank Space component, which is a layout utility. CRM Analytics Collection, CRM Analytics Dashboard (Aura), CRM Analytics Dashboard (LWC) | No | The Life Sciences Cloud mobile app doesn't support CRM Analytics. For mobile data visualization, use Salesforce Reports, dashboards, and Tableau Next instead. Dynamic Related List–Single | No | The Life Sciences Cloud mobile app doesn't support the Dynamic Related List–Single component. Instead, use the Related List – Life Sciences component, which is purpose-built for the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. The Related List – Life Sciences component supports filtering (restricted to simple WHERE clauses that use {recordId}), and supports customizable columns and headers. Dynamic Record Forms | Yes | The Life Sciences Cloud mobile app supports Dynamic Record Forms when Dynamic Forms for Mobile is turned on at the organizational level. Before implementation, confirm object compatibility by verifying the availability of the Fields tab within the Lightning App Builder. To ensure app stability, avoid these configuration conflicts: Component Redundancy: Avoid placing both a Record Detail component and Dynamic Forms on a single page, as this redundancy disrupts visibility logic and causes action bar overlaps. Legacy Conflicts: Make sure that Dynamic Forms aren't paired with legacy Aura components. These configurations can cause infinite refresh loops and UI flickering on mobile record pages. Highlights panel | Yes | The Highlights Panel is supported from the compact layout and actions pulled from the Salesforce Mobile and Lightning Experience section of the page layout. List View | No | The standard Salesforce List View component is unsupported within the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. Instead, use the Life Sciences Lists and Filters features, which you configure via the Admin Console. Recent items | Partially supported | Across all objects, the standard Recently Viewed filter and list view functionality, and the Salesforce Recent Records Lightning component, are unsupported within the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. The Life Sciences Cloud mobile app provides a native Recent Items capability. However, it's restricted to a predefined set of objects and you can’t configure it through the Lightning App Builder. Users can navigate back to recently accessed records—including Accounts, Visits, Medical Inquiries, Presentations, or Time Off Territory—directly from primary pages like the Home page. Record Detail | Yes | The Record Detail component renders fields and sections derived from the object's assigned page layout. Within the Lightning record page environment, the specific fields and sections presented to users are governed by their unique profile settings and page layout assignments. Related List – Life Sciences | Yes | The Related List – Life Sciences component, also known as the Generic Related List or, is a purpose-built custom component optimized for the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. It’s designed to replace standard Salesforce related list components to ensure native compatibility and functionality within mobile workflows. Related list – Single | Partially supported | The Related List – Single component is supported within the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. However, use the Related List – Life Sciences component for mobile workflows. Related List Quick Links | No | The Related List Quick Links component enables hoverable previews and mass actions within the desktop interface. The component is unsupported within the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. Related Lists | Yes | Use the Related Lists component to incorporate all pertinent child records within your Lightning page layout. To ensure visibility, confirm that the assigned user page layouts are configured with the specific related lists intended for mobile or desktop deployment. Related Record | No Report Chart & Dashboard | Partially supported | When you finalize the report and dashboard configuration, you can integrate these assets into Lightning page components to facilitate data visualization across both the Customer Engagement home page and record detail pages. These standard components are available for deployment via the Lightning App Builder. Dashboard: Supported on the home page Report Chart: Supported on the home page and Lightning record pages Furthermore, users can access reports and dashboards through dedicated navigation tabs within the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. Limitations for Bar and Column Charts Within the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app, standard bar and column charts are automatically rendered as stacked charts. Unsupported Chart Types These chart types are currently unsupported within the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app: Funnel charts Scatter charts Rich Text | Partially supported | The Life Sciences Cloud mobile app supports the Rich Text Area (RTA) component. However, the integration of images requires specific configuration for proper rendering. The Salesforce Platform documentation doesn't explicitly categorize Rich Text as a standalone Lightning component. However, technical guidance confirms its compatibility with the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. To ensure images render within the Rich Text Area, use Files with Public Distribution enabled. Avoid standard copy and paste actions. Instead, drag images directly from the browser into the component. Key Considerations: iPad Rendering: When configured using the drag method, the RTA component shows correctly within the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. Image Restrictions: Because the RTA servlet restricts mobile client access, standard copy and paste methods are unsupported. The mandatory workaround requires the use of Public Distribution files and drag functionality. Search Limitations: Rich Text fields are excluded from Global Search results within the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app, regardless of search layout configurations. Height Configuration: The Lightning App Builder lacks a native option to manually adjust the height of the Rich Text area specifically for iPad layouts. In short, while Rich Text is operational on the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app, successful image management relies on using publicly distributed files via the drag technique. Salesforce Surveys | Yes Tabs | Yes | The Tabs component is fully supported within the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. Visualforce Page | No | Custom actions enable the invocation of Lightning components, flows, Visualforce pages, or canvas apps to run business-specific logic. Use these actions to streamline repetitive workflows and make sure that processes remain tailored to unique organizational requirements.

findings.name: Custom Agentforce Life Sciences Lightning Page Components
findings.detail: Agentforce Life Sciences offers a collection of purpose-built custom components optimized for the platform's primary workflows. Any custom Lightning components developed for the Lightning App Builder are available within the components pane. This enables streamlined integration and advanced layout personalization to meet specific organizational requirements. Display Name | Description Account Affiliations | Shows account relationships and affiliations, such as hospital networks and parent organizations. Account Management Dashboard | Shows account health, activities, and key performance indicators. Account Map Display | Shows account locations and geographic distribution in an interactive map. Account Summary | Shows key metrics activities and insights specific to Life Sciences Customer Engagement. Account Team View | Shows account team members and their roles. Account Territory Fields | Shows territory assignment and alignment information for the account. Expenses List View | Shows expenses associated with visits, meetings, or activities. Generic Related List | Shows child records with Agentforce Life Sciences-specific functionality. Highlights Panel | Shows key fields and compact layout at the top of a record page for quick access to important information. Manage Visitors | Shows meeting attendees and participants for a visit. Multi-Entity Record View | Shows information from multiple related records simultaneously. Next Best Actions | Shows AI-driven recommendations for the next best actions to take with the account. Next Best Action Score Details | Shows details of Next Best Action (NBA) scores and recommendations. OPTS Web View | Embedded web view component (purpose specific to org configuration) Ratings | Shows account or contact ratings and classifications. Record Signature View | Shows captured signatures or provides signature capture functionality. Related List | Shows a single related list showing child records related to the current record. Survey List View | Shows a list of surveys associated with the current record. Video Call Recording List | Shows a list of recorded video calls and remote engagement sessions. Visit Survey List View | Shows a list of surveys completed during visits.

title: Add Life Sciences Users
summary: You can add internal Life Sciences users one at a time or in batches of up to 10

findings.name: Add Life Sciences Users
findings.detail: You can add internal Life Sciences users one at a time or in batches of up to 10 users.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud From Setup, use the Quick Find box to search for and select Users . Click New User to add a single user. Enter a first name, last name, email, and a unique username in the form of a email address. Your username must be unique across all Salesforce orgs, including trial and Sandbox orgs. Select a user license and a profile. For example, select Salesforce as the user license and Standard User as the profile. The user license determines the available profiles. A profile specifies the user’s minimum permissions and access settings. To email a login name and temporary password to each new user, ensure Generate new password and notify user immediately is selected. Specify more details for the user as needed. Save your changes.

findings.name: Filter Admin Console Tiles by User Permissions
findings.detail: Show users only the tiles they need in the Admin Console by turning on the Filter Admin Console Tiles Based On User Permissions setting. The setting is available on the Life Sciences Customer Engagement Setup page. The setting currently doesn't impact all tiles in the Admin Console.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. When the Filter Admin Console Tiles Based On User Permissions setting is off, all users who can access the Admin Console can also access all tiles. When this setting is turned on, only the users assigned with specific user permissions can access the respective tiles.

findings.name: Customize the Life Sciences Cloud Mobile App
findings.detail: Help your field teams manage their daily tasks efficiently using the Life Sciences Cloud Mobile app. Configure object metadata cache settings, application settings, profile-based configurations, and UI customizations to control data access, feature behavior, and the overall mobile app experience for your organization.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. Because Life Sciences Cloud is built on the core Salesforce platform, you can configure much of the mobile app experience using familiar Salesforce features, such as data access controls, Lightning record pages, and page layouts. Use the Life Sciences Cloud Admin Console to apply mobile-specific settings and sync your changes so they are available to users in the mobile app. Create Object Metadata Cache Configuration The Life Sciences Cloud Mobile app doesn’t automatically load all Salesforce objects and related data. Configure the object metadata cache to define which objects the mobile app stores locally and whether data syncs one-way or two-way between your Salesforce org and the mobile app. This configuration makes sure your sales reps have access to the data they need in the mobile app. Assign Profiles to Object Metadata Cache Configurations Assign profiles to a new object metadata cache configuration to make the configuration available to users with that specific profiles. Generate Metadata Cache Sync your configuration changes to the Life Sciences Cloud Mobile app by generating a metadata cache. This generated metadata cache includes object schemas and metadata definitions that the mobile app stores locally to support both online and offline modes. Generate a new metadata cache whenever you update Lightning record pages, page layouts, object or schema changes, new or modified feature settings, or permission updates. Configure Application Settings Configure essential Life Sciences Cloud mobile app settings, including default browser behavior, security controls such as password type, and user access to supported features. By using these settings, you can also control notifications, search capabilities, and the overall UI to customize the app to your needs. Set Up Profile-Based App Settings Use profile-based application settings to configure parameters to customize Life Sciences Cloud Mobile app settings for specific profiles. Configure UI Settings Configure custom UI components for the Life Sciences Cloud Mobile app. Create and manage records that define how tabs and static resources are shown in the Life Sciences Cloud Mobile app. Manage Translations for the Life Sciences Cloud Mobile App The Life Sciences Cloud Mobile app uses native Salesforce translation functionality. If multiple languages are enabled in your Salesforce org, configure translations so that your global users can access the app in their preferred language. Configure translations in Translation Workbench, then generate a translation file for mobile users to download to their devices.

title: Next Best Customer

findings.name: Next Best Customer
findings.detail: With the Next Best Customer scores, your field reps can identify the highest priority accounts for their next engagement. Next Best Customer leverages user-configured data, such as engagement history and territory alignment, to rank the accounts that are most likely to respond, so your reps can maximize the impact of each interaction. Show your users a prioritized set of accounts in the Next Best Customer component on the Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement home page. Users can also easily see the recommended accounts by filtering with Next Best Customer in the Account list view and on the Calendar tab. Set Up Next Best Customer To help your sales reps understand and work with the top accounts in their territory, set up the Next Best Customer component, quick actions, and scores. Account Scores and Rationales for Next Best Customer Use the Score Explainability Information field on Territory Account Score records to define how rationales appear in the Next Best Customer component. The Score Explainability Information field stores a JSON containing the store explainability details for a Next Best Customer (NBC) score. The JSON structure allows you to show multiple reasons per category and optionally include a Salesforce chart for a visual representation of the data.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. User Permissions Needed To configure a next best customer card: | Life Science Commercial Admin permission set From Setup, in the Quick Find box, find and select Actionable Relationship Center . Create a relationship graph. Click New Relationship Graph . Create a graph from scratch or select the NBC Card template, and then click Create Graph . In the properties pane, enter a unique label for the graph. The API name is automatically populated. Add or modify source objects in the graph view, if required. For Graph Type, ensure that Card View is selected. Configure the card layout. From the top left corner of the page, select Switch to Card . If you're creating the graph using the NBC card template, a default section with three preconfigured elements appears. You can customize these elements and apply visibility conditions as needed. To display additional information on the Next Best Customer card, create a section and enter a section display text. To display record details in the section, click Add Element . You can add up to three elements in a section. To control the space an element occupies in a row, use the Column Span field. Each row in a section is divided into 12 columns. If the column span is set to 12, the element occupies the entire row. If the combined column span of multiple elements equals 12, those elements appear in the same row. Select the alignment for item group elements. You can align item groups vertically or horizontally. Use the Item Alignment field to control how items in an element are aligned relative to other elements in the same row. For example, selecting Top aligns the element to the top of the row when displayed alongside other elements. Note Item alignment can’t be previewed in the card builder. Customize the font size and choose whether you want to apply bold style for each item in an element. Save your changes. Note Distance information is included in the NBC Card template by default but it can’t be previewed in the card view. If you’re creating the graph from scratch, you can’t add distance information to the Next Best Customer card. Note In addition to these customizations, you can also apply all other customizations described in Customizing a Provider Card because the next best customer card and provider card use the same card customization framework. Consequently, you can apply the configurations explained in this topic to Provider Card.

findings.name: Configure Sorting and Rationale Display Settings
findings.detail: Customize the sorting and rationale display settings for the Next Best Customer components in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile App. From the App Launcher, find and select Admin Console . Select Next Best Customer , and then select Next Best Customer Setting . For Apply Settings To, select whether you want to apply the settings to all the profiles in your org or to a specific profile. To apply the settings to all the profiles in your org, select SOrg Default . To apply the settings to a specific profile in your org, select Profile . Configure the Next Best Customer Sorting settings. Select whether you want to allow sorting of top customers by distance. Enter the account score threshold value that determines the number of top customers shown on the component. This value defines the number of accounts available for distance-based sorting, so that only this subset of top-scored accounts is sorted by proximity to ensure low-priority accounts don't surface just because they are nearby. Distance-based sorting applies only to accounts with geolocation data. Select whether you want to show the rationale as a standard Salesforce chart on the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. To ensure accounts are accurately sorted by distance, geolocation data must be captured for primary address or preferred address. Distance is calculated from an account’s preferred contact point address to the user’s real-time location. If the account doesn't have a preferred address, the distance is calculated from its primary contact point address. To update the geolocation data, activate data integration rules on the Contact Point Address object, which uses the Google Maps API to determine latitude, longitude, and accuracy. Alternatively, you can manually update the data by selecting Check for New Data from the record’s action menu. For accurate distance calculations, ensure users have their device’s location services enabled.

From Setup, click Object Manager and then select Territory Account Score . Select Fields & Relationships , and then select Set History Tracking . In the Track old and new values section, enable Total Score. Save your changes.

findings.detail: From Setup, in the Quick Find box enter Batch Management ,and then select Batch Management . Open the Process Accounts for Territory Planning batch job by clicking the batch job label. Verify that the batch job is active, uses the Account object, and is of the AccountTerritoryPlanning type. Ensure that batch sizes and filters are correctly configured. The standard definition has no filters and processes all accounts in segments. Note To process a filtered set of accounts, create and activate a batch definition that uses the Account object and the AccountTerritoryPlanning type instance. Configure its batch job name, batch definition name, process type, executor process, batch size, start time, entry criteria, and retry strategy. In the flow, replace the existing batch action with an action that uses the new batch API name.

findings.name: (Optional) Customize the Scheduled Flow
findings.detail: If you're using a batch definition to process a filtered set of accounts, update the scheduled flow to use the batch job you created. Open the Execute Territory Planning Rules action element in the flow. Set Sales Plan Id to the ID of the plan that you created. Get the ID from a Segment Builder URL or run this query in Developer Console. SELECT Id, Name FROM sfsp__SalesPlan__c WHERE Name = '<sales plan name>' Set Territory Model Id to the ID that you recorded from the active Sales Plan model. To verify the ID, run this query in Developer Console and select the intended active model. SELECT Id, Name FROM Territory2Model WHERE Name = '<territory model name>' Process selected alignments. Edit the existing Text resource for alignment IDs. If the flow doesn't contain this resource, create it. Enter the IDs as comma-separated values. Map the resource to TPAlignmentIds. Process selected segments. Edit the existing Text resource for segment IDs. If the flow doesn't contain this resource, create it. Enter the IDs as comma-separated values. Map the resource to SegmentIds. Retrieve IDs with this query and select only records that represent the intended segments. SELECT Id, Name FROM sfsp__SalesNode__c Set the Should Replace Existing Territory Associations flag. To delete existing manual object-to-territory and user-to-territory associations and rebuild associations from Territory Planning, set the value to True . To preserve manual associations and insert or update associations generated from Territory Planning, set the value to False .

Note If the frequency is once and the start date and time are in the past, the flow doesn't run. For other frequencies, the flow runs at the next scheduled time.

title: How Briefings Work
summary: Briefings helps you transform complex account data into personalized audio briefings through a two-stage process. Configure a scheduled flow that runs daily to convert account summaries into human-readable, natural language text. Sync this data into the Life Sciences Cloud Mobile app by creating...

findings.name: How Briefings Work
findings.detail: Briefings helps you transform complex account data into personalized audio briefings through a two-stage process. Configure a scheduled flow that runs daily to convert account summaries into human-readable, natural language text. Sync this data into the Life Sciences Cloud Mobile app by creating object metadata cache configurations for Briefings objects. The mobile app then converts this data into audio using Kokoro, an on-device text-to-speech model, delivering the latest audio briefings before every scheduled visit.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement, Agentforce for LifeSciences Cloud, Einstein GPT Prompt Builder, and Einstein GPT Platform Add-on licenses, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. Use the guided setup to configure Briefings for your users. The guided setup, available in Life Sciences for Customer Engagement Setup in your Salesforce org, walks you through the setup steps.

findings.name: Key Considerations
findings.detail: Briefings currently supports English only. If the podcast text contains non-English content, Kokoro Text to Speech (TTS) will attempt to read it using English phonetics, resulting in incorrect or unintelligible pronunciation. Briefings generates audio briefings only for visits scheduled on the current day. Briefings for future visits become available on the visit day, when the scheduled flow runs. Ask your field users to keep their calendars updated with upcoming visits to ensure the daily Briefings schedule captures all visit data. If you and your users are in different time zones, ask them to log their visits at least two days in advance. The daily Briefings schedule runs on the org's time zone, so logging in advance ensures all visit data is captured accurately. The Briefings icon appears in the top-right corner of the Life Sciences Cloud Mobile app once two conditions are met. Make sure the user's profile is associated with a Presentation Content Definition Assignment entry. The user also requires read access to the Presentation Content object. The icon remains hidden until both conditions are fulfilled. Each audio briefing is limited to 3,000 characters. Content exceeding this limit is truncated in the generated audio file. If you create a new visit, or cancel or reschedule an existing visit on the go, your playlist is not dynamically updated to reflect the changes. The audio briefings playlist is based on the Presentation Content data generated by the Briefings Daily scheduled flow. If you configure the flow to include all visit changes, the playlist updates automatically after the data syncs to the Life Sciences Cloud Mobile app.

summary: Use the Presentation Content Definition Assignments to control which user profiles can access and receive audio briefings in your org. This configuration helps ensure the right users get timely, relevant updates. Only one Presentation Content Definition record is required for

In the new Manage Presentation Content Definition Assignments window, select the user profiles as needed. Note Profile assignments determine which user profiles receive daily audio briefings; users not assigned to a profile won't receive any briefings. Save your changes. Note Daily audio briefings are only generated for the assigned profiles.

title: Mobile App Configuration for Briefings
summary: Configure the object schema for supported Briefings objects and generate a metadata cache to make the relevant objects available in the Life Sciences Cloud Mobile app. The mobile app uses on-device text-to-speech capability, powered by Kokoro, to generate personalized, up-to-date audio briefings...

findings.name: Mobile App Configuration for Briefings
findings.detail: Configure the object schema for supported Briefings objects and generate a metadata cache to make the relevant objects available in the Life Sciences Cloud Mobile app. The mobile app uses on-device text-to-speech capability, powered by Kokoro, to generate personalized, up-to-date audio briefings for your users.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement, Agentforce for LifeSciences Cloud, Einstein GPT Prompt Builder, and Einstein GPT Platform Add-on licenses, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. Audio files are created and stored on the device, organized as a playlist in the same order as the field user's visit schedule for the day. Field users can listen to these briefings via the built-in audio player in the mobile app. The playlist is updated during the next sync when new audio files are available. Each audio file has an effective end date, after which it is automatically removed. This date is defined in the object metadata cache configuration for the associated Presentation Content record. Configure the object metadata cache for these objects: Object | Type | Sync | where Clause Presentation Content | Data | Unidirectional | (EffectiveStartDate = NULL OR EffectiveStartDate <= TODAY) AND EffectiveEndDate >= TODAY AND (TargetUserId = '{USER.ID}' OR TargetUserId = NULL) AND (TerritoryId = '{USER.TERRITORYID}' OR TerritoryId = NULL) Presentation Content Usage Summary | Data | Bidirectional | UserId = '{USER.ID}' AND PresentationContentId IN ( SELECT Id FROM PresentationContent WHERE (EffectiveStartDate = NULL OR EffectiveStartDate <= TODAY) AND (EffectiveEndDate >= TODAY OR EffectiveEndDate = NULL) AND (TargetUserId = '{USER.ID}' OR TargetUserId = NULL) AND (TerritoryId = '{USER.TERRITORYID}' OR TerritoryId = NULL) ) Presentation Content Definition Assignment | Configuration | Unidirectional | IsActive = true Presentation Content Definition | Configuration | Bidirectional | NA Note After you create these configurations, generate a metadata cache . The metadata cache downloads the required objects so users can access their audio briefings even in areas with limited network coverage, and ensures the mobile app accesses the latest metadata definitions, including any schema changes for supported objects.

Customize your calendar by configuring these general settings as needed. First Day of Work Week | Select the first day of the calendar work week. If left empty, this defaults to Monday. Day View Fieldset for Visit | Enter the API name of a field set from the Visit or Provider Visit object. The first two fields from the fieldset appear on the visit tiles in the Day view. Assessment Task Display Name | Enter the API name of a Text or Formula field from the Assessment Task object to use as the display name. Colleague Visit Field | Enter the name of a formula field from the Visit object to show colleague's visits. Show colleague's visits in calendar grid | Select to highlight shared visits in the calendar background when a user drags an account onto the calendar grid. Hide customer address | Select to hide addresses in the account list. Hidden addresses can still be searched. Show the last visit date for an account | Select to show the last visit date when a user expands an account. Show visits to attendees | Select to show visits across all attendee territories. Enable Time Off Territory Adjustment | Select to allow resizing time off territory events on the Life Sciences Cloud Mobile app. Enable Advanced Account Search | Select to enable advanced account search in Calendar. Enable preview for denormalized visits | Select to preserve original visit data (denormalized data) in the visit preview for signed or completed visits. Work Day Start Time | Set the default start time for the calendar grid. Enter the time in hh:mm format. Hourly Slots Viewable on Calendar | Enter a value between 3 and 16 to set the default zoom level and enable calendar zoom. Leave the field blank to disable zoom. Time Format | Set the time display format for the calendar. Enter h:mm for 12-hour standard time or HH:mm for 24-hour time. Share calendar events with mirror territory users | Select to enable shared calendar functionality, allowing users to view visits from their mirror (shared) territory on the calendar. Note: This requires mirror territory configuration. For more information, see Configure Mirror Territory . Allow users to create an event by clicking on the calendar grid | Select to allow users to create events by clicking an empty time slot. Configure the general event settings. To allow users to add employees to general events, select Is Feature Enabled . Note Make sure that you add the Attendees field to the Event page layout. Manage user routines by enabling these settings as needed. Enable Routine | Select to enable the routine feature so users can save and apply predefined sets of visits for recurring schedules. Allow users to share routines | Select to let users share routines from the Account tab. Allow users to create a routine that spans across multiple days | Select to allow users to create multi-day routines. This feature is available in Day, Work Week, and Week views. Don’t rollback changes when there’s an error saving a routine | Control how schedule conflicts are handled when a routine is applied. When selected, valid visits are created while conflicting visits are skipped. When deselected, no visits are created if any schedule conflict occurs. Note Sharing is restricted to subordinate territories of a user's assigned territory. If a user is assigned to both a parent and a subordinate territory, the subordinate territory isn't available for sharing. In the Business Hours Settings section, assign business hours for each activity type. Global Business Hours | Set the organization's standard working hours for all calendar activities. Also used to calculate working days for activity plans. Business Hours for Visits | Set the working hours for scheduling visits. If left blank, this defaults to the Global Business Hours. Business Hours for General Events | Set the working hours for creating general events. If left blank, this defaults to the Global Business Hours. Managed Event Business Hours for Planner | Set the working hours for creating field events. If left blank, this defaults to the Global Business Hours. Before assigning the business hours, define your organization's business hours in Salesforce setup. If needed, you can customize the default colors of event types. In the Event Indicators section, entering a Hex color code for each event type. Planned Visit Confirmed Visit Completed Visit Time Off Territory General Event Holiday Assessment Task In the Account Record Types section, move the account record types you want to display in the calendar account list to the Selected Values list. HCP includes accounts where the IsPersonAccount field on the account object equals True . HCO includes accounts where the IsPersonAccount field equals False . Save your changes. Important Calendar settings such as Show visits to colleagues and Share calendar events with mirror territory users control only how the calendar shows visits. They aren't security controls and can't hide records that the sharing model has already granted. findings.name: Set Up Engagement Execution Features
findings.detail: Streamline scheduling, pre-visit planning, in-visit execution, and post-visit reporting processes with Visit Management. Capture, manage, and honor consent and communication preferences of healthcare professionals with Consent Management. Use Remote Engagement to host virtual meetings with customers. Use Medical Inquiries to deliver fast, compliant, and trusted responses to every HCP inquiry. Use Surveys to collect feedback from customers.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. Consent Management Capture, synchronize, and honor the communication preferences of healthcare professionals across different subscription topics and channels. Use Consent Management to limit outreach to healthcare professionals who have provided consent and stay compliant with data privacy regulations. Medical Inquiries Capture, manage, and respond to critical questions from healthcare professionals (HCPs). Help your sales representatives and medical science liaisons streamline the inquiry creation process, provide accurate and timely responses, and handle a variety of inquiry types, including general medical inquiries, adverse events, and product quality complaints. Leverage configurable workflows and robust compliance capabilities to ensure that all medical inquiries are handled quickly and in accordance with medical, legal, and regulatory standards. Medical Insights Use Medical Insights to provide field teams a structured way to capture and share insights from their engagements with HCPs and HCOs. Show relevant insight data for collaboration through customized record pages with specific field sets and related lists. Streamline the user workflow by creating quick actions and defining granular permissions to control how users interact with insights. Provider Engagement Compliance Provider engagement compliance is a regulatory support feature for the Japanese pharmaceutical market. It automates and tracks two mandatory processes: Early Post-Marketing Phase Vigilance (EPPV), which monitors new drug safety for the first few months of sales, and Medical Information Delivery (MID), which ensures the rapid delivery of urgent safety information to healthcare professionals (HCPs). Sales representatives conduct periodic visits (cycles) to healthcare organizations (HCOs) to collect safety data and deliver critical documentation. Remote Engagement Remote engagement facilitates virtual meetings by providing tools to start and manage remote visits with healthcare professionals (HCPS) and healthcare organizations (HCOs). When users schedule remote visits, healthcare professionals receive invitations with the necessary details such as the meeting link and passcode. During the meeting, users can manage participants, share screens, and capture signatures, streamlining virtual interactions and eliminating the need for in-person visits. Surveys Design and distribute structured questionnaires to gather feedback from healthcare professionals. Use the collected data to analyze behavioral trends, monitor patient-related outcomes, and strengthen provider relationships. Visit Management Use Visit Management to plan, execute, and record visit details while meeting compliance requirements. Your users can seamlessly share content, distribute samples, and capture signatures across both mobile app and desktop site. Concur Expense Sync Concur Expense Sync helps organizations to effectively and efficiently manage expense reporting for field operations by synchronizing visit-related expense data between SAP Concur and Life Sciences Cloud using a dedicated MuleSoft integration. This process ensures that field representatives can capture and manage expenses directly from the mobile app, providing them with a unified experience that maintains data accuracy. Next Best Message Next Best Message provides tailored and relevant messages for each product associated with an account. These recommendations are dynamically generated based on real-time data, allowing field sales teams to provide this information during visits with their customers.

findings.name: Provider Engagement Compliance
findings.detail: Provider engagement compliance is a regulatory support feature for the Japanese pharmaceutical market. It automates and tracks two mandatory processes: Early Post-Marketing Phase Vigilance (EPPV), which monitors new drug safety for the first few months of sales, and Medical Information Delivery (MID), which ensures the rapid delivery of urgent safety information to healthcare professionals (HCPs). Sales representatives conduct periodic visits (cycles) to healthcare organizations (HCOs) to collect safety data and deliver critical documentation.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package.

findings.name: Considerations for Using Provider Engagement Compliance
findings.detail: Product restrictions, including the ones defined at the territory level (account—territory—product combinations) doesn't apply for provider engagement compliance. Salesforce uses product restrictions for controlling sample drops, and don't define the accounts to be monitored for account compliance. Assessment tasks for account compliance must be associated with a visit. The Type field in Action Plan differentiates a provider engagement compliance action plan from a key account manager action plan. The Category field of a care program differentiates a provider engagement compliance care program from any other care program. On Mobile, a custom tab shows the Account Compliance component and related records. You can't customize the Account Compliance tab. The standard Action Plan object is used for account compliance. So, you see the standard Action Plan tab on the web and on mobile devices. You can't hide the Action Plan tab on your mobile. There's no validation to restrict manual status updates on Provider Engagement Compliance Cycle records. You can control access to these records by restricting the visibility of the Provider Engagement Compliance Cycle tab for sales representatives. We recommend you avoid migrating to Agentforce Life Sciences when a provider engagement compliance is in progress. However, if you must migrate, the ongoing provider engagement compliance data, such as care program, Care Program Product, Action Plan, are migrated from legacy systems. During the migration, system validations and trigger handlers that restrict creation of or updates to provider engagement compliance data are ignored for successful data loading. Unlocking a visit doesn't automatically update the visit status to In Progress. You can configure a record-triggered flow to update visit status when unlocked. Provider Engagement Compliance Glossary Before you dive into the configurations for Provider Engagement Compliance, familiarize yourself with the feature's nomenclature. Learn about the terms that are commonly used to describe Provider Engagement Compliance, including the terminology used throughout the feature's lifecycle. Provider Engagement Compliance Workflow Provider engagement compliance is about generating compliance cycles to monitor a newly launched product, and then using these cycles to record observations for the new launch. Set Up Provider Engagement Compliance Prepare your org for Provider Engagement Compliance by enabling and configuring the feature. Generate Provider Engagement Compliance Cycles Salesforce generates compliance cycles based on the configurations defined in the associated care program and compliance template. Conduct Provider Engagement Compliance Visits Track account compliance within your assigned territory. Use the color-coded compliance list for an account to make sure that you don't miss any required cycles.

title: Provider Engagement Compliance Glossary

findings.name: Provider Engagement Compliance Glossary
findings.detail: Before you dive into the configurations for Provider Engagement Compliance, familiarize yourself with the feature's nomenclature. Learn about the terms that are commonly used to describe Provider Engagement Compliance, including the terminology used throughout the feature's lifecycle.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package.

findings.name: Generic Terms
findings.detail: EPPV (Early Post-Marketing Phase Vigilance): A mandatory regulatory process in Japan that monitors the safety, effectiveness, and overall performance of newly launched pharmaceutical products for the first six months of sales. MID (Medical Information Delivery): A regulatory requirement in Japan mandating pharmaceutical companies to deliver promptly urgent safety documents and information to healthcare institutions where their drugs are prescribed. Provider Engagement Compliance: The Agentforce Life Sciences term for the EPPV and MID features collectively. Compliance Template: A reusable template created by using Action Plan Template. This template dictates the structure of the compliance process, including cycle length, number of cycles, and restart and last-cycle behaviors. Compliance Program: These records, created by using Care Program, contain the specific details, such as mandatory regulatory dates and associated products (Care Program Product). Account Compliance Plan: These records are created by using Action Plan for each HCO participating in a compliance program. Sales representatives use these records to monitor the required compliance activities during visits to those HCOs. Provider Engagement Compliance Cycles: The account-specific generated cycles that contain the details of when sales representatives must conduct visits for an HCO. Compliance Activity: The actual record of the Provider Engagement Compliance interaction is created by using Assessment Task. A sales representative captures the interaction during a scheduled visit to an HCO. Institution Doctor Account: A business account type that links an HCP to an HCO, which serves as the target account for scheduling compliance activities.

findings.name: Key Configurations
findings.detail: Compliance Announce Date: The date when the compliance program officially becomes visible to sales representatives. Compliance Start Date: The date when a sales representatives officially delivers a pharmaceutical product at an HCO. On this date, you can change the status of an account compliance to In Progress. Compliance End Date: The date marking the end of the compliance period beyond which Salesforce doesn't create any cycle. Extension Due Date: The latest date that the final compliance cycle can be extended to, allowing users a final window to execute their compliance activity visits. Modification End Date: The final date after which sales representatives can’t log new visits or enter or modify reasons for skipped cycles. Pre-Cycle Start Date: A compliance template setting that defines the date when sales representatives can begin optional pre-survey visits to HCO before the product is officially launched. A pre-survey visit can begin on the defined pre-cycle start date and conclude one day before the compliance start date. Restart Behavior: A compliance template setting that defines the rules to generate new cycles when sales representatives restart an interrupted compliance plan. There are four available Restart Behavior options. Not Allowed: Sales representatives can’t restart an account compliance. This is the default option. Restart: Salesforce deletes the incomplete cycles when you stop an account compliance. When you restart the account compliance, Salesforce deletes the completed cycles. Start Over: Salesforce deletes the incomplete cycles when you stop an account compliance. When you restart the account compliance, Salesforce generates a new set of cycles, by using the restart date as the start date for Cycle 1. Resume: Salesforce retains the completed cycles and deletes the incomplete ones when you stop an account compliance. When you restart the account compliance, Salesforce generates the incomplete cycles by using the restart date as the start date for the next cycle. Last Cycle Behavior: A compliance template setting that determines how Salesforce handles the final cycle if the cycle approaches the compliance end date. There are three Last Cycle Behavior options. Do Not Create: Salesforce skips generating a cycle and its subsequent ones if the cycle's calculated end date falls after the compliance end date. Create With Cycle End Date: Salesforce generates cycles with an end date based on the duration defined in the compliance template. However, if the cycle’s end date exceeds the extension due date, Salesforce adjusts a cycle's end date to match the extension due date. This is the default option. Create With Compliance End Date: Salesforce generates cycles ignoring the duration defined in the compliance template and sets a cycle's end date to match the compliance end date.

findings.name: Generate Provider Engagement Compliance Cycles
findings.detail: When a new pharmaceutical product is launched, create a compliance program (care program). Use the related list of the compliance program to associate a product with the compliance program. Based on the territories defined for the product, Salesforce automatically shares the compliance program with territories. Create a compliance template (action plan template) with the type Provider Engagement Compliance. Set the compliance cycles and how long they are. Every account compliance records created by using the template has these cycles. Associate a compliance template and a compliance program. So, now you can create account compliance records for the HCO accounts participating in the compliance program. Next, create an account compliance record (action plan) for an account using a compliance template. The care program associated with the compliance template gets associated with the account compliance. After a newly launched product is officially delivered to an account, start the account compliance. If the product is delivered to multiple accounts, bulk update the status of the account's compliance to started. When an account compliance starts and its status changes to In Progress, based on the cycles and the start date defined in the compliance template, Salesforce generates the cycle schedule. If the calculated cycle date is after the care program end date, Salesforce doesn’t create a cycle. If you've configured a pre-survey cycle in the associated compliance template, Salesforce generates a pre-survey cycle. Sales representatives can conduct and log their pre-survey visits before the account compliance period even starts.

findings.name: Conduct Provider Engagement Compliance Visits
findings.detail: Each cycle has a color-coded status, such as New, Due Soon, Upcoming, Overdue, Skipped, and Completed. You can see the color-coded compliance list in the Account Compliance tab. Based on the status, sales representatives can identify the accounts that require attention, and create a visit for the compliance cycle and associate its assessment task with a care program. Based on the visit and cycle date, Salesforce links an assessment task to the relevant provider engagement compliance cycle. During a visit, sales representatives record compliance activities by using an assessment task. After completing an assessment task, sales representatives submit the visit. Salesforce then changes the status of the corresponding provider engagement compliance cycle as completed. If a product delivery is interrupted, sales representatives can stop and then restart an account compliance. Salesforce handles the compliance cycles based on the Restart Behavior defined in the associated compliance template.

findings.name: Product Territory Alignments
findings.detail: Set up product-territory alignments to help users drive targeted product efforts, reduce errors, and comply with regulatory standards. These alignments control how products and product messages are assigned to territories, and make sure that the correct user has access to the correct product in the correct territory.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. By default, product-territory alignments are inherited downstream in the product hierarchy. But Life Sciences Cloud also provides the Parent Territory Product Alignment admin setting that enables product territory alignments to be extended all the way up in the hierarchy to all parent territories. Product-territory alignment in Life Sciences Cloud is determined through explicit (direct) alignment, parent-based inheritance, and explicit exclusion. Explicit alignment (direct alignment): A product is explicitly aligned to a specific territory. This means that the product is directly available in that territory, regardless of other hierarchy-based rules. Inherited from parent (parent alignment): A product is inherited from a parent territory. This means that it was aligned to a parent territory and is automatically made available to the child territory through inheritance. Directly excluded (exclusion): A product is explicitly excluded from a territory. This means that the product is unavailable for a child territory even when the parent territory is aligned to the product. The final product alignment consisting of only non-excluded products—whether explicitly aligned to the territory or inherited from a parent—is available to users in that territory. When you align products to territories, the system automatically creates Product Territory Availability records in the Queued status. An invocable action creates Product Territory Detailed Availability records for the queued Product Territory Availability records. Note As an alternative to using the Admin Console for product-territory alignment, admins can import product-territory alignment data from an external system and run the Publish Draft Product Territory Alignments batch job. To learn more, see Create Product Territory Alignments in Bulk . Here are the alignment types—Exclusion, Inclusion, and Territory and Subordinates Inclusion and the sharing rules. Symbol | Meaning | Product Territory Availability Alignment Type Indicates that a territory isn't aligned to a product. | No Product Territory Availability record created Indicates that a territory is directly aligned to a product. If this territory is a child territory, it means that even if the parent territory isn't aligned to the product, the child territory still has access to it. | Inclusion Indicates that a territory is excluded from the alignment, even though its parent territory is aligned to the product. | Territory Exclusion Indicates that a territory is included, because one of its parent territories is aligned. | Inclusion (Inherited) Indicates that a territory, as well as its child territories, is aligned to a product. | Territory and Subordinates Inclusion When you enable the Parent Territory Product Alignment admin settings, products assigned to a territory are automatically aligned with its parent territories as well, all the way up in the hierarchy. However, when you make changes to the admin setting, the new rules aren't applied retroactively to existing Product Territory Availability records. Align Products with or Exclude Products from Territories Configure precise and targeted product-territory alignments by using territory exclusions. When you exclude a child territory, it doesn't inherit the product alignment of its parent territory record. Create Product Territory Alignments in Bulk Import multiple product records from external systems, align them with territories, and create detailed availability records by using the Publish Draft Product Territory Alignments batch job. Assign sample quantities to sales territories for a specified period. Sales reps can only distribute or request approved samples that are allocated to their assigned territories. When to Use Territory Product Quantity Allocations and Sample Limits Both territory product quantity allocations and sample limits can help you manage sample product distribution to healthcare professionals (HCPs). Understand the difference between these options and when to use them. Set Up Territory Product Quantity Allocations Allocate sample products to a specific territory over a specified period.
