title: When to Use Territory Product Quantity Allocations and Sample Limits
summary: Both territory product quantity allocations and sample limits can help you manage sample product distribution to healthcare professionals (HCPs). Understand the difference between these options and when to use

findings.name: When to Use Territory Product Quantity Allocations and Sample Limits
findings.detail: Both territory product quantity allocations and sample limits can help you manage sample product distribution to healthcare professionals (HCPs). Understand the difference between these options and when to use them.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. Territory product quantity allocations control inventory management and strategic distribution, while sample limits control regulatory compliance and responsible sampling per account. You can configure territory product quantity allocations and sample limits separately. Or, use them together to control the quantity of samples allocated to territories and how many samples sales reps can distribute per account and visit within that territory and period. Feature | Overview | Purpose | Characteristics Territory Product Quantity Allocations | Controls how much of a sample product is allocated to a territory for distribution to HCPs. | Helps with inventory management, budgeting, and strategic distribution planning. | Set at the territory level. Determines the total quantity of a sample product available for that territory. Used for planning and managing sample stock. Managed via Territory Product Quantity Allocations records. Sample Limits | Defines the maximum number of samples that can be distributed to a specific account within a given time frame or under certain conditions. | Prevents oversampling to ensure regulatory compliance and adhere to legal restrictions | Set at the account level. Determines the maximum quantity an account can receive. Managed via sample limit templates with defined rules, such as 2 samples per visit or 5 samples per period per account. Limits can reset periodically.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. User Permissions Needed To create, edit, and delete Life Sciences Customer Engagement data: | Life Sciences Commercial Admin permission set Before you can allocate quantities: Define date ranges for allocations in the Time Period object. Create territories and products. Configure product territory alignments to control how you assign products to territories and to give the correct user access. From the App Launcher, find and select Territory Product Quantity Allocations , and then click New . Select the product and territory that you want to enforce this quantity allocation for. Define allocations at the lowest relevant level in the hierarchy where you manage samples. Select or create a period during which to enforce the quantity allocation for this product and territory. To determine how sales reps can disburse the product, select the allocation type. To distribute samples to HCPs during visits, select Drop . To ship samples directly to HCPs, select Ship . Define the quantities to enforce. Allocated Quantity : The amount of the sample product allocated to the territory for the selected time period. Adjustment Quantity : The amount to adjust the allocated quantity. Ordered Quantity : The total amount ordered and available for distribution in the territory. Max Disbursement Limit Quantity : The maximum amount that a sales rep can disburse in a given visit. Save your changes. After field reps submit or sign a visit, Salesforce updates the territory product quantity allocation records. The debited quantity shows the amount disbursed or shipped to HCPs, and Salesforce calculates the remaining quantity to reflect the disbursement. Validation and debiting for Direct to Practitioner shipments only apply to territory product quantity allocation records with the Ship allocation type. To enforce quantity limits, create a Ship allocation for each product, territory, and time period. To monitor allocations, track usage, and identify any discrepancies, we recommend setting up reports and dashboards.

title: Event Management Glossary of Terms
summary: To familiarize yourself with the industry-standard nomenclature that’s commonly used in Event Management, refer to the comprehensive list of terms used across the

findings.name: Event Management Glossary of Terms
findings.detail: To familiarize yourself with the industry-standard nomenclature that’s commonly used in Event Management, refer to the comprehensive list of terms used across the feature.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. Activity Plan | A record that organizes and tracks financial goals, spending limits, and activities for a defined time period. Activity plans of type Event Management Limit are used to enforce monetary caps across managed events. Actual Expenses | The real costs incurred for an event, recorded after the event takes place. Actual expenses are allocated to participants and reported for compliance and transparency purposes. Attendee | A healthcare professional (HCP) or account-based participant who is formally invited to and attends a managed event. Attendees are searched and added via the New Attendees window. Attendee Quota | A configurable limit that restricts the number of participants a colleague with the contributor role can invite to an event. When the quota is exceeded on mobile, a Managed Event Participant Discrepancy record is created. Business Hours | The configured working hours of an organization. Managed events must be scheduled within defined business hours, enforced by the MngEventBusinessHoursHandler trigger handler. Colleague | An internal user (such as a sales representative) who is added to a managed event as a participant. Colleagues are looked up via User Additional Info records and can hold roles such as organizer, coorganizer, coordinator, or contributor. Committed Expenses | Expenses that have been formally approved for one or more activities but not yet spent. Committed expenses factor into the total expense calculation when a managed event is still in progress. Compliance Agreement Status | A field on the Managed Event record that reflects whether all mandatory compliance statements have been accepted by the organizer. The status remains “Agreement Required” until all mandatory statements are accepted, after which it changes to “Agreed.” Compliance Statement | A regulatory policy statement embedded in the managed event workflow that requires acknowledgment from the event organizer or coorganizer before the event can proceed. Statements can be of type Compliance Note or Compliance Agreement. Compliance Statement Definition | A configuration record that defines the text, type, requirement level (mandatory or optional), and display order of a compliance statement. Only records with statement text filled in and the correct module and statement types are displayed in the Compliance Statements component. Estimated Expenses | The projected amount of money expected to be spent for one or more activities in a managed event. Entered during the planning phase and used to calculate total event expenditure before actuals are available. Event Execution | The active phase of a managed event during which the organizer captures attendee sign-ins, adds write-in participants, launches presentations, and administers surveys. Event Logistics | The resources, venues, catering, equipment, and other supplies that facilitate the smooth running of a managed event. Managed using Managed Event Resource and Managed Event Resource Preference records. Event Management | An Agentforce Life Sciences Cloud solution that provides a comprehensive framework for planning, approving, executing, and concluding field events, while supporting compliance and regulatory governance. Event Management Participant Role | A record that assigns a custom name to a standard participant role (such as, organizer, coorganizer, coordinator, contributor, approver, attendee, expert). Custom roles are mapped to standard roles to control access and actions in the event workflow. Event Management Participant Type | A record that assigns a custom name to a standard participant category (such as, expert, colleague, attendee, non-profiled attendee, write-in attendee). It allows organizations to define custom categories aligned to their business needs. Event Management Participant Type Role Mapping | A junction record that links an Event Management Participant Type, an Event Management Participant Role, and a Managed Event Type. It determines which participant roles are available for a given participant type within a specific event type. Expense | A financial record associated with a managed event that tracks the cost of an activity, such as catering, venue fees, or speaker fees. Expenses can be classified as estimated or actual. Expense Allocation | The process of distributing actual expense costs among the participants of a managed event. Allocation can be even (split equally) or uneven (manually assigned individual amounts). Expense Participant | A record that links a specific expense to a managed event participant. It captures the portion of the actual expense allocated to that participant and is used in monetary cap calculations. Expense Type | A record that defines a category of expense (such as, food and beverage, venue, audio-visual). Expense types have a classification (estimated or actual) and an Included in Cap flag that determines whether they count toward monetary cap calculations. Expert | A healthcare professional contracted by a life sciences company to present at managed events. Experts are linked to Subject records via Expert Subject records to confirm their eligibility and training for a given topic. Expert Subject | A record that associates an Expert with a Subject, confirming the expert’s training and eligibility to present on that topic. The record must be active during the dates of the managed event for the expert to be eligible. Field Event | A preplanned, regulated interaction between a life sciences company’s representatives and healthcare professionals (HCPs) that takes place outside the company’s home office. Includes speaker programs, rep-led meetings, and HCP sponsorships. HCO (Healthcare Organization) | A healthcare institution such as a hospital or clinic. In Event Management, an HCO can serve as the location (resource type) for a managed event. HCP (Healthcare Professional) | A licensed healthcare practitioner, such as a physician or nurse, who participates in managed events as an attendee, speaker, or other participant type. HCP Sponsorship Event | A type of managed event in which a pharma company provides financial support for an HCP to attend a third-party event (for example, a medical congress) that the company does not organize or control. Requires compliance review, approvals, and transparency reporting. Key Opinion Leader (KOL) | An influential healthcare professional who presents expert insights on drug efficacy or disease management to peer HCPs at company-sponsored events. KOLs are typically contracted as Speakers. Life Science Email Template | A template record (comprising a Life Science Email Template and its associated snapshot) used to configure and send email invitations and notifications to managed event participants. Managed Event | The central record in Event Management representing a field event. It captures the event’s name, dates, type, status, participants, expenses, and compliance information. The Status field drives progression through the workflow path. Managed Event Participant | A record that represents an individual’s participation in a managed event. It stores the participant’s type, role, invitation response, attendance status, and other participation details. Managed Event Participant Discrepancy | A record created to log exceptions or warnings associated with a participant’s addition to an event. Examples include monetary cap exceedances on mobile, subject compliance violations with a Warn action, and attendee quota exceedances. Managed Event Product | A record that links a product to a managed event. These records are automatically created and reconciled based on the Subject Product records associated with the subjects assigned to the event. Managed Event Resource | A record that captures the primary logistical resource for an event, such as a venue, catering service, or audio-visual equipment. The first confirmed Venue or HCO resource automatically stamps the event’s location. Managed Event Resource Preference | A child record of a Managed Event Resource that represents ranked alternative options for a resource. For example, for a venue resource, preferences might list Hotel A (rank 1) and Hotel B (rank 2). Users can select a Managed Event Resource Preference record as the event location by confirming its status. Managed Event Territory | A record created when a participant with an organizer, coorganizer, or coordinator role accepts an invitation. It links the event to the user’s active territory and triggers territory-based record sharing. Managed Event Type | A configuration record that defines the template and category for a managed event (for example, speaker meeting, rep-led meeting, HCP sponsorship). It is the basis for participant type role mappings and workflow configurations. Monetary Cap | An account-level spending limit that tracks actual, estimated, and committed expenses for a healthcare provider across all managed events. Caps can be configured with Error or Warning alert types. Non-Profiled Attendee | A participant who attends a managed event but is not profiled as a standard account or contact in Salesforce. Non-profiled attendees are linked to Party Profile records. Organizer | The primary participant role that’s assigned to the person who creates and manages a managed event. The organizer can add participants, accept compliance statements, and drive the event through the workflow stages. Participant Recruitment | The process of adding participants to a managed event. When an event is created, the system automatically adds the current user as the organizer and creates the corresponding Managed Event Participant records. Party Profile | An intermediate, non-profiled record in Salesforce that represents an individual who has not yet been fully profiled as a standard account or contact. Used for write-in and non-profiled attendees. Presentation Forum | A record associated with event presentations within the Event Management solution. Provider Activity Goal | A record that tracks spending goals and allowances for a healthcare provider account. Associated with an Activity Plan and used to calculate and enforce monetary caps. Provider Activity Goal Limit | A record that sets the maximum monetary spending amount for an account across all managed events within an activity plan’s time period. Provider Activity Goal Measure | A record that measures and tracks the utilization (estimated, committed, actual, and total expenses) against a provider activity goal. Cap data is stored as JSON in the AdditionalInformation field. Provider Activity Measure Type | A configuration record that defines the conditions and alert type (error or warn) for monetary cap calculations. Specifies the criteria JSON used to determine when expenses are included in cap utilization. Record Update Validation Notifier | A Lightning App Builder component added to the Managed Event and Managed Event Participant record pages that subscribes to the event and displays alerts and notifications when the account reaches the utilization limit. Rep-Led Event | A type of managed event hosted by a company and led directly by a sales representative, without a paid external speaker. May include meals or other items requiring transfer-of-value reporting. Restricted Party | An account or contact flagged as ineligible to participate in certain events due to a product-account restriction. Adding the associated healthcare provider as a participant is blocked or warned depending on the event’s start date. Sign-In Sheet | An electronic form launched on the day of the event to capture attendee signatures, attendance confirmation, and meal preferences. Essential for compliance reporting and transfer-of-value tracking. Speaker | An expert or key opinion leader (KOL) who delivers approved educational or promotional content at a managed event. Speakers are contracted by the pharma company and must have valid training records for the event’s subject. Speaker Bureau | A compliance type assigned to subjects that require strict expert eligibility and subject compliance validation. When a subject with this type is assigned to an event, the system enforces expert training checks and attendance history checks. Speaker Event | A company-hosted event where an HCP contracted as a speaker delivers approved educational or promotional content to other HCPs. Requires formal approvals, speaker contracts, attendance capture, and post-event reconciliation. Subject | A topic that a speaker presents at a managed event. Subject records define the content theme of an event and are linked to products, experts, and email or presentation templates. Only subjects with a usage type of Managed Event can be assigned to an event. Subject Assignment | A record that links a specific Subject to a Managed Event. When a subject is assigned, the system automatically creates related Managed Event Product records for the associated products. Subject Compliance Check | A verification process that determines whether a participant is eligible to be added to a managed event based on their recent attendance history — confirming they haven’t attended another event on the same subject within a configured number of past days. Subject Material Template | A junction record that associates a managed event subject with an email template or presentation. Subject Product | A record that links a product to a Subject. Subject Product records determine the valid product set for a managed event and are used to reconcile Managed Event Product records. Territory | A geographic or organizational region used to align accounts, users, and events for sharing and access control. Territory membership determines which records users can view and interact with in Event Management. Time Period | A record that defines the date range within which an activity plan is active. Managed event start and end dates must fall within the associated activity plan’s time period for monetary cap calculations to apply. Transfer of Value (TOV) | Any item of monetary value provided to an HCP at or in connection with an event, such as a meal, speaker fee, or sponsorship payment. TOVs must be tracked and reported for regulatory transparency and compliance. User Additional Info | A supplemental Salesforce record that stores additional profile details for internal users, such as preferred country. Required for users to appear in colleague search results in Event Management. Utilization Tracker | A Lightning App Builder component added to the Account record page and the Expert record page that displays all active monetary caps and utilization levels for that account or expert. Workflow Path | A configured sequence of stages, stage operations, and actions that defines the full lifecycle of a managed event — from draft through pending approval, approved, execution, and conclusion. Controls which roles can perform which actions at each stage. Write-In Attendee | A participant who attends a managed event on an ad hoc basis without a prior invitation. Automatically converted to an attendee (if linked to an account) or non-profiled attendee (if linked to a party profile), based on the participant party reconciliation status.

See Get Your Org Ready for Event Management . Configure Concluded Event Status in org-level admin console settings. See Configure Org-Wide Settings for Event Management . Add the Utilization Tracker Lightning App Builder component to the participant's Account record page. Set up an Activity Plan of type Event Management Limit with a defined time period. See Define the Time Period for the Activity Plan and Create Activity Plans . Create Provider Activity Goal records for participant accounts. See Set Goals for Activity Plans . Create Provider Activity Measure Type records for Error and Warning scenarios (with criteria JSON). See Monetary Cap Setup in Monetary Cap. Create Provider Activity Goal Measure records linked to the goals and measure types. See Set Goal Measures for Activity Plans . Create Provider Activity Goal Limit records with the monetary limit amount. See Create a Provider Activity Goal Limit in Monetary Cap. Change sharing settings for Provider Activity Goal and Activity Plan to Private. See Activity Plan Record Sharing Rules in Monetary Cap. Run the Share Provider Activity Goals Based on Activity Plan Type batch job. See Event Management Batch Jobs .

findings.name: Expense Management
findings.detail: Create field sets for Expense Type search and display (Expense Type Search Field Set, Expense Type Display Field Set). See Get Your Org Ready for Event Management . Configure admin console settings: Allow Partial Expense Allocation, Add Receipts to Expense Records, Toggle the System-Generated Expense Type Filter. See Configure Profile-Level Settings for Event Management . Add an Expenses tab to the Managed Event record page, and add the Expense Management custom component to the Expenses tab. See Create an Expense Tab for the Event in Expense Management. Create Expense Type records for estimated expenses (Classification: Estimated; Parent Expense Type: blank). See Create an Expense Type for Estimated Expenses in Expense Management. Create Expense Type records for actual expenses (Classification: Actual; linked to parent estimated expense type). findings.name: Integration with Email
findings.detail: Create dynamic picklist values for the Subject Material Template’s Template Type field. See Get Your Org Ready for Event Management . Add HTML and JPG files for the email template. See Email Template ZIP Files and the prerequisites for Integration with Email . Create Life Science Email Template records and Life Science Email Template Snapshot records (versions) with subject line and file identifier. Attach an HTML file (email body) and a JPG file (thumbnail) to each snapshot. See Create an Email Template in Integration with Email. Create Subject Material Template records linking each Subject to its email template. See Create a Subject Material Template for Emails in Integration with Email.

findings.name: Integration with Presentations
findings.detail: Add the Managed Event Presentations Lightning App Builder component to the Managed Event record page. See Create a Lightning Record Page for Managed Events . Create dynamic picklist values for the Subject Material Template’s Template Type field (such as, Presentation). See Get Your Org Ready for Event Management . Configure Presentation Subject Material Template Types in the admin console. See Configure Org-Wide Settings for Event Management . Create Subject Material Template records linking each Subject to its presentation. See Create a Subject Material Template for Presentations in Integration with Presentations.

findings.name: Integration with Calendar
findings.detail: Configure business hours for the organization. See Set Business Hours . Configure Managed Event business hours for Planner in the admin console (Calendar tile). See Configure Business Hours for Events . Configure calendar events using managed event metadata. See Configure Calendar Events .

findings.name: Integration with Surveys
findings.detail: Activate trigger handlers: ColleagueSurveySharingHandler, SurveyInvitationSharingHandler. See Get Your Org Ready for Event Management . Create territory records and assign users to territories (required for territory-based sharing). See Set Up Sales Territories for Life Sciences Cloud in Get Your Org Ready for the Customer Engagement Managed Package. Create a Survey record and activate it. See Create Managed Event Surveys in Integration with Surveys. Create a Survey Subject record linking the survey invitation to the managed event (via Apex script). See Create Managed Event Surveys in Integration with Surveys. For territory-based sharing: create a Survey Engagement Context record linking the survey invitation to the territory (via Apex script). See Create Managed Event Surveys in Integration with Surveys.

findings.name: Event Workflow
findings.detail: Activate trigger handlers: StagePathPermissionsHandler, ColleagueSurveySharingHandler, SurveyInvitationSharingHandler. See Get Your Org Ready for Event Management . Add the Life Sciences Event Workflow Lightning App Builder component to the Managed Event record page. See Create a Lightning Record Page for Managed Events Create picklist values for the Managed Event’s Status field. See Get Your Org Ready for Event Management . Customize the Launch Survey workflow action (add survey name and configure parameters). See Customize the Launch Survey Workflow Action in Event Management Workflow. Customize the Managed Event Email Participant workflow action (configure participant response filters). See Customize the Managed Event Email Participant Workflow Action in Event Management Workflow. Customize the workflow path: add stage operations, role-based filter conditions, and actions per stage. See Customize the Workflow Path in Event Management Workflow. Activate the workflow.

title: Create a Lightning Record Page for Managed Events
summary: Help users capture event-related information in one place by creating the Managed Event Lightning record page. Add tabs for the various Event Management components, such as expenses, logistics, and

findings.name: Create a Lightning Record Page for Managed Events
findings.detail: Help users capture event-related information in one place by creating the Managed Event Lightning record page. Add tabs for the various Event Management components, such as expenses, logistics, and presentations.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. User Permissions Needed To add a Lightning record page: | Life Sciences Commercial Admin permission set From the object management settings for Managed Events, select Lightning Record Pages . To create the Managed Event record page, click New , and make the following changes. In the Create a new Lightning page window, select Record Page , and then click Next . Enter a label, such as Managed Event. For Object, select Managed Event , and click Next . Select Header and One Region as the page template. Click Done . Drag the Highlights Panel to the header region. Drag the Tabs component to the editable part of the page. Add a tab for expenses. In the Properties pane, click Add Tab . The standard Details tab is added by default. Select the standard Details tab. In Tab Label, select the dropdown next to Details, scroll to the top of the list, and then select Custom . Enter a custom label, such as Expenses. In the builder, drag the Expense Management custom component onto the Expenses tab. Similarly, add a tab for capturing event logistics information, and drag the Related List - Single component onto the tab. In the Properties pane, make these changes. The default value for Parent Record is Use This Managed Event. Keep it as is. In Related List, select Managed Event Resources . The default value for Related List Type is Default. Keep it as is. Create a tab for presentations, and drag the Managed Event Presentations custom component onto the tab. Create a tab for event attendees, and add related lists for each participant type. See the Participant Recruitment Setup section for more information on related list setup for attendees, experts, colleagues, write-ins, and non-profiled participants. Add the Compliance Statement component on the Managed Event record page. In the builder, drag the Field Events: Compliance Statements Lightning App Builder component onto an editable part of the page. In Properties, for Compliance Statement Auto-Save Limit, enter a value, such as 5 . This setting determines the number of compliance statements that can be automatically saved in bulk. Note If the number of compliance statements for a managed event is more than the auto-save limit, the Accept button appears and you can capture acceptance in bulk. If the number of compliance statements for a managed event is less than the auto-save limit, the Accept button doesn’t appear and you can capture acceptance individually. If the auto-save limit isn’t configured, the Accept button appears by default. Add the Life Sciences Event Workflow component onto the Managed Event record page. Save your changes. Click Activation . Click Assign as Org Default , and select Desktop and Phone . Click Next and save your changes.

Configure Profile-Level Settings for Event Management To define event management configurations,...

findings.name: Event Management Admin Console Configurations
findings.detail: Set up profile-level and org-wide Admin Console settings for Event Management. Define the business hours for your org and learn about the batch jobs that support the event management processes. Configure Profile-Level Settings for Event Management To define event management configurations, compliance checks, participant search, and eligibility criteria, set up the event management Admin Console settings. You can apply the settings to a specific profile or the entire org. Configure Org-Wide Settings for Event Management Configure the Admin Console settings, such as transaction and logistics rules, that apply universally in your Salesforce org. Event Type Mappings Streamline event workflows by mapping managed event record types to managed event types. When users select a record type during Managed Event record creation, the system automatically populates the Managed Event Type lookup field, eliminating redundant data entry. Participant Type Mappings Autopopulate fields in the Managed Event Participant record when you add a participant to an event, based on the Managed Event Participant record type you specify in the custom related list for event participants. The system derives the values from the event management participant type that the record type is mapped to, and updates the Record Type, Event Management Participant Type, Event Management Participant Role, and Event Management Participant Type Role Mapping fields in the Managed Event Participant record. Configure Business Hours for Events As a prerequisite, set up business hours for your organization. You can choose to create standard business hours or custom ones that are specific to your unique requirements. Event Management Batch Jobs Run automated batch jobs to align event products with subject products, calculate expenses against monetary caps, and share provider activity goals based on activity plan type.

title: Configure Profile-Level Settings for Event Management
summary: To define event management configurations, compliance checks, participant search, and eligibility criteria, set up the event management Admin Console settings. You can apply the settings to a specific profile or the entire

findings.name: Configure Profile-Level Settings for Event Management
findings.detail: To define event management configurations, compliance checks, participant search, and eligibility criteria, set up the event management Admin Console settings. You can apply the settings to a specific profile or the entire org.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. User Permissions Needed To configure Admin Console settings: | Life Sciences Commercial Admin permission set From the App Launcher, find and select Admin Console . Select the Event Management tile. In the left navigation pane, select Field Events Profile Settings . Choose whether you want to configure the settings for the org or for a specific profile. Note These settings use the Admin Console hierarchical framework. Before you configure them, review how precedence works and the related considerations in Hierarchical Settings in the Admin Console . Configure the event settings that generally apply for the profile. For Participant Invitation Response Default Status, select the participants’ default response to managed event invitations. Choose a value from among the statuses available in the Managed Event Participant’s Participant Response field. Choose whether the system captures the attendee’s location at the time of sign-in. Choose to attach receipts to expense reports. Choose to verify that the sign-in date is within the event’s start and end dates. Enable sales reps to add write-in attendees to an event. In Default Managed Event Duration in Minutes, enter the default duration of an event in minutes. Configure compliance settings. For Attendance Statuses for Subject Compliance, select the participant’s attendance status for past events that makes them eligible for a subject compliance check. For Participant Subject Compliance Check Actions, specify the action to take if a participant fails the subject compliance check. The options you can choose from are Block, Warn, and None. For Write-In Participant Subject Compliance Check Actions, specify the action to take if a participant fails the subject compliance check. The options you can choose from are Block, Warn, and None. For Write-In Participant Restricted Product Check Actions, specify the action to take if a write-in participant is associated with a product that is restricted for the event. The options you can choose from are Block, Warn, and None. If you leave this field blank, the system uses the default Warn value. For Managed Event Colleague Restricted Roles, select the participant roles that a colleague is restricted from being assigned to. For Attendance History Subject Conflict Check in Days, enter the number of retrospective days that the system must scan for a subject conflict in the participant’s attendance history. Configure allocation settings. For Expense Allocation Eligible Participant Types, select the participant types who are eligible for allocation of expenses. The selected participant types appear while allocating expenses. For Estimated Expense Allocation Invitation Status, select the values that indicate that estimated expenses are allocated to the invited participant. For Actual Expense Allocation Attendance Status, select the values that indicate that actual expenses are allocated to the participants. Configure quota settings. For Colleague Invitation Quota Exempt Status, select the participant’s response status values that represent that the participant is excluded from the colleague’s invitation quota. Configure search settings for adding attendees. For New Attendees Display Field Set, select the field set in the Account object that represents the fields displayed as columns in the Update Attendee window’s search results. For New Attendees Search Field Set, select the field set in the Account object that consists of fields to search for at the time of adding an attendee to an event. To help users add attendees in bulk, select Show the Add All button in the New Attendees modal . To help users conduct detailed searches beyond the standard keyword search, select Enable Advanced Search to find accounts to invite . To view the hierarchical relationship between healthcare professionals and healthcare organizations in the Add Attendees modal, select Show HCP-HCO affiliation for attendees . To use advanced filtering conditions in Event Management, select Enable lists and filters in the New Attendee modal . Configure search settings for adding event experts. For New Experts Display Field Set, select the field set in the Expert object that consists of fields that are available as filter options, and are displayed at the time of adding experts. For New Experts Search Field Set, select the field set in the Expert object that consists of fields that appear in expert search. To help users find participants via account search instead of searching for experts, select Enable the Add Experts Via Account Search button in the New Experts modal . Configure search settings for adding event colleagues. For New Colleagues Display Field Set, select the field set in the User Additional Info object that consists of fields that are available as filter options, and are displayed at the time of adding colleagues. For New Colleagues Search Field Set, select the field set in the User Additional Info object that consists of fields that are available as filter options, and are displayed at the time of searching for colleagues to add to an event. To provide users with the flexibility to remove system-generated filters that show only those colleagues whose country matches the current user’s, select Toggle the system-generated Preferred Country filter . Configure search settings for the event’s expenses. For Expense Type Display Field Set, select the field set in the Expense Type object that contains the fields that are available as filter options and are displayed while adding an estimated or actual expense. For Expense Type Search Field Set, select the field set in the Expense Type object that contains the fields that are displayed while searching for expenses to be added to an event. To provide users with the flexibility to remove system-generated filters that only show expense types that match the event’s type and subtype at the time of expense search, select Toggle the system-generated expense type filter . To enable users to allocate a portion of the expense amount to the event participants rather than the whole amount, select Allow partial expense allocation . Configure search settings for the event’s subject. For Subject Display Field Set, select the field set in the Subject object that contains the fields that are available as filter options and are displayed while adding a subject to an event. For Subject Search Field Set, select the field set in the Subject object that contains the fields that are displayed while searching for subjects to add to an event. To provide users with the flexibility to remove the system-generated filter that only shows subjects whose dates overlap with or fall within the event's date range, select Toggle the system-generated subject filter . Configure eligibility settings for the event’s expert. For Expert Subject Training API Name, enter the API name of the custom Boolean field in the Expert Subject object that indicates that the expert has completed a valid training for the subject. For Subject Compliance External ID List, enter the API name of the field in the Subject object that stores the semicolon-separated list of the external IDs of compliance subjects. To enable users to only add experts who have completed the required training for a subject, select Check eligibility for subject presentation . Save your changes.

summary: Configure the Admin Console settings, such as transaction and logistics rules, that apply universally in your Salesforce

findings.name: Configure Org-Wide Settings for Event Management
findings.detail: Configure the Admin Console settings, such as transaction and logistics rules, that apply universally in your Salesforce org.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. User Permissions Needed To configure Admin Console settings: | Life Sciences Commercial Admin permission set From the App Launcher, find and select Admin Console . Select the Event Management tile. In the left navigation pane, select Field Events Org Level Settings . Configure the general settings. For Presentation Subject Material Template Types, select the template type value that represents presentations in a managed event. Admins must first create the dynamic picklist in the Subject Material Template object’s Template Type field. To determine expense amounts using the exchange rate on the day of transaction, select Use Historical Transaction Rate to calculate expenses . This setting uses the Dated Exchange Rates configured in Manage Currencies in Setup. To enable the event manager to review the event, select Include manager as event approver . When you select this setting, and if the sales rep creating the event is set as the primary owner of the event, the sales rep user's manager is automatically added as the approver of the event. When you deselect this setting, the manager is added as the coordinator of the event. For Concluded Event Status, configure the managed event’s status value or values that indicate that the event has ended. This setting is used to determine when the monetary cap calculation switches from estimated to actual expenses. Configure the participant role settings. Make sure you create event management participant types, participant roles, and mapping records between the type and role before you complete these steps. For Attendee Participant Default Role, select the custom picklist value in the Event Management Participant Role’s Role field that the attendee participant type maps to. For Expert Participant Default Role, select the custom picklist value in the Event Management Participant Role’s Role field that the expert participant type maps to. For Write-In Participant Default Role, select the custom picklist value in the Event Management Participant Role’s Role field that the write-in participant type maps to. For Non-Profiled Participant Default Role, select the custom picklist value in the Event Management Participant Role’s Role field that the non-profiled participant type maps to. Configure event logistics settings. For Venue Resource Type, select the managed event resource’s resource type picklist value that represents a designated venue for events to take place. For Healthcare Organization Resource Type, select the managed event resource’s resource type value that represents the HCO where an event can take place. For Managed Event Resource Confirmed Status, select the managed event resource’s status value that indicates that a resource has been confirmed as the location for an event. For Managed Event Resource Preference Confirmed Status, select the managed event resource preference’s status value that indicates that a resource preference has been confirmed as the location for an event. Save your changes.

findings.name: Event Type Mappings
findings.detail: Streamline event workflows by mapping managed event record types to managed event types. When users select a record type during Managed Event record creation, the system automatically populates the Managed Event Type lookup field, eliminating redundant data entry.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package.

findings.name: Considerations
findings.detail: Managed Event record types that aren’t mapped to a managed event type follow the standard event creation process, in which the Managed Event Type lookup field is manually selected. This setting doesn’t have any direct UI impact. The Managed Event Type field is populated in the backend. To prepare for this automatic population, remove the Managed Event Type field from the Managed Event’s page layout. See Customize Page Layouts with the Enhanced Page Layout Editor . The record type must be valid for the Managed Event object. Each record type maps to only one event type.

findings.name: Prerequisites for Using Event Type Mappings
findings.detail: Make sure you configure the following. Create record types for the Managed Event object. Create Managed Event Type records.

findings.name: Enable Event Type Autopopulation Settings
findings.detail: To use event type mappings to dynamically update the Managed Event Type field in a Managed Event record, turn on the Autopopulate Managed Event Type in Managed Event Records toggle.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: User Permissions Needed To enable setup toggles: | Life Sciences Commercial Admin permission set From Setup, use the Quick Find box to find and select Life Sciences for Customer Engagement Setup . In the Configure Event Management for Customer Engagement section, turn on Autopopulate Managed Event Type in Managed Event Records.

findings.name: Map a Managed Event Type to a Managed Event Record Type
findings.detail: Create mappings between managed event record types and managed event types. Each record type-event type mapping must be unique. This setting ensures that when you create a Managed Event record, the Managed Event Type field is automatically populated based on the Managed Event record type.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: User Permissions Needed To create record type-event type mappings: | Life Sciences Commercial Admin permission set Important Make sure you remove the Managed Event Type field from the page layout. From the App Launcher, find and select Admin Console . Select the Event Management tile. In the left navigation pane, select Event Type Mappings . Click New . Select a managed event record type. Select a Managed Event Type record. Select Active . Save your changes.

title: Participant Type Mappings
summary: Autopopulate fields in the Managed Event Participant record when you add a participant to an event, based on the Managed Event Participant record type you specify in the custom related list for event participants. The system derives the values from the event management participant type that the...

findings.name: Participant Type Mappings
findings.detail: Autopopulate fields in the Managed Event Participant record when you add a participant to an event, based on the Managed Event Participant record type you specify in the custom related list for event participants. The system derives the values from the event management participant type that the record type is mapped to, and updates the Record Type, Event Management Participant Type, Event Management Participant Role, and Event Management Participant Type Role Mapping fields in the Managed Event Participant record.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. Original Participant Role Settings (Deprecated) The original participant role settings help you configure default roles for the attendee, expert, write-in, and non-profiled participant types. The default role is derived from the Event Management Participant Role’s Role field, that an attendee, expert, write-in participant, and non-profiled participant type is already mapped to. Where: In the Admin Console, go to the Event Management tile. In the org-level settings, find the Participant Role Settings section. Impact: Based on the participant role setting, the Event Management Participant Type Role Mapping is automatically populated in Managed Event Participant records. Participant Type Mappings (Enhanced Approach) In the enhanced approach, participant type mappings help you map the default role-participant type combination to a Managed Event Participant record type. An Event Management Participant Type can be linked to only one Managed Event Participant record type through a single participant type mapping. If you need to support multiple record types for the same standard type (for example, two different Attendee record types), create a separate Event Management Participant Type record for each record type — each one using the same standard type (Attendee) but mapped to its own record type. In this case—where multiple Event Management Participant Type records are mapped to the same standard type to support multiple record types—make sure you specify the record type in the custom related list. Without this step, the related list button is hidden and users encounter an error. Where: In the Admin Console’s Event Management tile, go to Participant Type Mappings, and map the Event Management Participant Type record to a Managed Event Participant record type, and set a default role for this mapping. The default roles are derived from the Event Management Participant Type Role Mapping records that the Event Management Participant Type is already mapped to. Impact: When a user adds a participant to a managed event, they don’t have to go through multiple windows and steps to select the Managed Event Participant record type, the Event Management Participant Type, Event Management Participant Role, and the Event Management Participant Type Role Mapping records in the Managed Event Participant record. All these values are derived from the participant type mappings and autopopulated in the Managed Event Participant records. This participant type mapping can also be created between the event management participant type and default role, without specifying the Managed Event Participant record type. In such cases, the mapping serves as an assignment between the event management participant type and the default role from the Event Management Participant Roles that the Event Management Participant Type record is already mapped to, similar to how the original Participant Role Settings functions. Usage: When you configure the participant record type in the custom related list for attendees, colleagues, experts, write-ins and non-profiled, the mapping automatically populates the Event Management Participant Type, Event Management Participant Role, Event Management Participant Type Role Mapping and Record Type fields in the Managed Event Participant records that are created. Admins must create mappings for these 5 types of participants. For Attendees, Experts, Write-Ins, and Non-Profiled Participants, also assign a default role in the mapping — this is required for the system to auto-populate participant fields. For Colleagues, skip the default role: it's ignored by the system, since the role is assigned by the user at the time the colleague is added. Prerequisites and Validations Create active Event Management Participant Type Role Mapping records. Optionally, create active record types for Managed Event Participants. Specify only 1 record type in the related list’s properties. Each Event Management Participant Type record can be mapped to only one Managed Event Participant record type. To support more than one record type for a given standard type, create a distinct participant type record per record type. Make sure the managed event type is valid for the Managed Event record where the related list is configured.

findings.name: Considerations for Participant Type Mappings
findings.detail: Learn more about how Event Management handles scenarios where the record type is specified in the custom related list versus when it's not. Note Each event management participant type can be mapped to only one Managed Event Particiant record type via a singular participant type mapping. Default role behavior differs by standard type and is required only for attendees, experts, write-in participants, and non-profiled participants. When no record type is specified, exactly one participant type mapping (with default role set) is allowed per standard type for Attendees, Experts, Write-Ins, and Non-Profiled Participants. This restriction doesn't apply to Colleagues, where multiple mappings and roles for the same standard type are allowed since role is assigned at run time.

findings.name: Record type is specified
findings.detail: Attendees and Experts To specify a record type in the custom related list’s properties, you must create a mapping between the event management participant type and managed event participant record type. The default role must be set for the event management participant type. If the record type is specified in the custom related list’s properties, the system doesn’t check for the event management participant type’s standard type. Error Scenarios If there’s no participant type mapping specified for the record type, the related list button is hidden. If the default role is not set for the participant type-record type mapping, the users see an error in the relevant section in the Attendee tab. Colleagues To specify a record type in the custom related list’s properties, create a mapping between the event management participant type and managed event participant record type. If the record type is specified in the custom related list’s properties, the system doesn’t check for the event management participant type’s standard type. The system doesn’t check for the default role for the colleague because the role is assigned by the user at run time. If the default role is populated, the system ignores it. The system shows the roles for the mapped participant types in the New Colleague window. Event organizers see the type and role combinations of the available options. Error Scenarios If there’s no participant type mapping specified for the record type, the New Colleague button is hidden. Write-Ins and Non-Profiled Participants To specify a record type in the custom related list’s properties, you must create a mapping between the event management participant type and managed event participant record type. The default event management participant role must be configured in the mapping. When the record type is specified in the custom related list, the system fetches the event management participant type, event management participant role, and the event management participant type role mapping, and populates these values in the Managed Event Participant record. If the record type is specified in the custom related list’s properties, the system doesn’t check for the event management participant type’s standard type. Error Scenarios If there’s no participant type mapping specified for the record type, the related list button is hidden. If the default role is not set for the participant type-record type mapping, the users see an error in the relevant section of the Attendee tab.

findings.name: Record type isn't specified
findings.detail: Attendees and Experts If you don’t specify a record type in the custom related list’s properties, the system goes through the existing participant type mappings to find the event management participant type whose standard type matches the participant type of the custom related list, and for which the default role is set. For example, if you don’t specify a record type for experts, that is, the New Record Type Action field in the custom related list for experts is left blank, the system scans through the participant types whose standard type is expert and for which the default event management participant role is set. Error Scenarios If more than one participant type mapping exists, users see an error. If the participant type mapping exists but the default role is not set, users see an error. Colleagues If you don’t specify a record type in the custom related list’s properties, the system checks the Event Management Participant Type Role Mapping records for the event management participant types whose standard type is colleague, and shows all event management participant roles mapped to it. Write-Ins and Non-Profiled Participants If you don’t specify a record type in the custom related list’s properties, the system checks the existing participant type-record type mappings for event management participant types whose standard type matches the attendee type of the custom related list (write-in or non-profiled) for which the default event management participant role is set. Error Scenarios If there is more than one participant type mapping, you see an error message. If the participant type mapping doesn’t exist, you see an error message. If mapping exists but the default role is not set, you see an error message.

findings.name: Configure Participant Type Mappings
findings.detail: Configure a mapping between a participant type and a Managed Event Participant record type. Optionally, assign a default role to the participant type in the Participant Type Record Mapping.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: User Permissions Needed To create participant type mappings: | Life Sciences Commercial Admin permission set When you select the event management participant type, in the Default Event Management Participant Role field, the system shows the event management participant roles that the participant type is already mapped to. Note Once you create a participant type-record type mapping, you can’t update the record type. You have to delete the mapping and create a new one. From the App Launcher, find and select Admin Console . Select the Event Management tile. In the left navigation pane, select Participant Type Mappings . Click New . Select an Event Management Participant Type record. Set a default role for the participant type. Skip this step for participant types whose standard type is Colleague. Select a record type. Save your changes. Next, configure the record type (developer name) in the custom related list for Attendees, Experts, Colleagues, Write-Ins, and Non-Profiled participants.

findings.detail: Plan and prepare for the recruitment process of event participants. Find out more about how participant search works for each attendee type. Configure related lists for attendees, experts, colleagues, write-ins, and non-profiled attendees.

findings.name: Required Editions

It uses internal checks to verify access to fields specific to the Event Management data model.

findings.name: Considerations for Recruitment
findings.detail: When the current user creates a Managed Event record, the system automatically adds the current user as an organizer, and creates a related Managed Event Participant record. When the current user creates a Managed Event record and adds another user as the primary owner of a managed event, the system automatically adds the current user as the coordinator and the other user as the organizer, and creates two Managed Event Participant records. When the current user creates a Managed Event record and adds their manager as the primary owner of a managed event, the system automatically adds the current user as the coordinator and the other user as the approver, and creates two Managed Event Participant records.

findings.name: Prerequisites
findings.detail: Create territories. See Set Up Sales Territories for Life Sciences Cloud in Get Your Org Ready for the Customer Engagement Managed Package. Set up Account Search . Search for accounts and align accounts with the territories . To use advanced search criteria, set up search before create . Create accounts to represent the healthcare professionals and healthcare organizations you want to add as participants. Create picklist values in the Managed Event Participant’s Participant Type field to represent attendees, colleagues, experts, write-ins, and non-profiled attendees. In the org-level Admin Console settings for Event Management, select the default role for each participant type in Default Role for Attendee, Default Role for Expert, Default Role for Write-In Attendee, Default Role for Non-Profiled Attendee. Make sure you create Event Management Participant Role records, Event Management Participant Type records, and Event Management Participant Type Role Mapping records for each participant type, for a specific managed event type. Create record types for Managed Event Participants. Create participant type mappings for each participant type. As a prerequisite for the participant recruitment setup, create a Lightning record page for Managed Events and add an Attendee tab.

findings.name: Managed Event Participants
findings.detail: Users can also create Managed Event Participant records directly, either from the App Launcher or the Managed Event record page's standard related list. On the Managed Event Participant record, users select the participant's type and role. Based on the user's selection, the system fetches the active Event Management Participant Type Role Mapping records that are applicable for the managed event type, and stamps it on to the Managed Event Participant record. As a prerequisite for this advanced selection option to be visible in the Managed Event Participant record, make sure you turn on the Display Type and Role in Participant Records toggle in the Life Sciences for Customer Engagement Setup's Configure Event Management for Customer Engagement section. Attendee Participant Learn about the configurations that control the display, filtering, and advanced search options in Attendee Search. Then, configure the Attendee section related list on the Managed Event's record page. Colleague Participant Simplify colleague participant implementation by setting up configurations and related lists that streamline the colleague search. You can only add colleagues who are managed event participants where the participant is a user. Expert Participant Configure expert search and eligibility validation to ensure only qualified, compliant experts are added to an event, including training checks, attendance history conflicts, and account access verification. Write-In Participant Help users capture attendance of write-in participants who join the event in an ad hoc manner. Event Management helps users convert write-ins to attendees or non-profiled attendees based on the linked record type and reconciliation status. Non-Profiled Participant Complete the prerequisites for adding non-profiled participants. Create the participant values that correspond to non-profiled attendees and configure the related list settings.

title: Attendee Participant

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. User Permissions Needed To add a related list for attendees: | Life Sciences Commercial Admin permission set In the New Attendees window, Event Management searches for attendees to add to an event in the following ways. Aligned Accounts list: By default, the system searches for accounts aligned to your territory. Users can see all the available attendee options in the Aligned Accounts list. They can switch to a list they created to see accounts that fulfil a specific criteria, or filter the search by HCP, HCO, or all. Enable lists and filters using the Enable lists and filters in the New Attendee modal checkbox in the Event Management profile-level settings. Search filters: Enable users to filter the attendee search by specific fields by creating a field set and configuring the same in the New Attendees Search Field Set in the Admin Console. Display columns: Enable users to view specific fields in the columns of the search results by creating a field set and configuring the same in the New Attendees Display Field Set in the Admin Console. Add All button: Configure the visibility of the Add All button, which lets users invite all the attendees in the search results, using the Show the Add All button in the New Attendees modal setting in the Admin Console. HCP-HCO affiliation: Enable users to quickly find an HCP from a specific HCO. In the search results, if an HCO has any affiliated HCPs, the search result is indicated with a [affiliation] symbol. This function makes it easier to select an attendee who’s affiliated with an HCO. Configure this setting using the Show HCP-HCO affiliation for attendees field in the Admin Console. Search Before Create: Enable users to use the Search Before Create function before creating an account to add as an attendee. Configure this setting by selecting the Advanced Search using the Enable Advanced Search to find accounts to invite checkbox. Also, add the Enable Search Before Create Lightning App Builder component onto the Managed Events record page’s Related tab. To display fields of your choice in the Attendees related list on the Managed Event record page, create a field set in the Managed Event Participant object. Add the field set in the Related List-Life Sciences custom component for Attendees.

findings.name: Create the Related List for Attendees
findings.detail: To enable users to quickly add attendees to a managed event, configure the attendee's related list settings on the Managed Event record page. From the App Launcher, find and select Managed Events . Select a record. From the top-right corner of the page, click , and then select Edit Page . Go to the Attendees tab. In the searchbox, find and select the Related List-Life Sciences custom component. Move the component onto the Attendees tab. In the properties pane, add the following information for the Attendee section. In Object API Name, enter MngEventParticipant . Represents the API name of the object to fetch the data for and display in the related list. In Field Set API Name, enter the API name of the custom field set you created for adding attendees, such as, lsc4ce__Add_Attendee . Represents the field set that defines which columns to display in the related list. In Label API Name, enter Attendees . Represents the related list’s header. In Icon, enter the list header icon name, such as standard:person_account . To view the standard icon options, see Icon Library . In Action Handler API Name, enter AccountAttendeesUpdateDeleteHandler . Represents the component that handles row-level update, delete, and menu actions. In Where Clause, enter MngEventId = '{recordId}' AND EventMgmtParticipantType.StandardType = 'Attendee' AND MngEventParticipant.RecordType.DeveloperName = 'AttendeeRecordType'. Replace AttendeeRecordType with the developer name of the record type for attendee participants. Represents the clause that filters the records to show. In New Action Handler API Name, enter AddAccountAttendee . Represents the underlying component that’s used in the New Attendees button. In New Action Record Types, enter the developer name of the Managed Event Participant record type you created for the attendee participant, such as AttendeeRecordType. In Relationship Field API Name, enter MngEventId . Represents the lookup field on the child object that points to the parent record, and is used by the system to add new records. In View All Component API Name, enter StandardViewAll . Represents the underlying component that’s used for the View All action. Select Show record count . Save and activate your changes.

title: Write-In Participant
summary: Help users capture attendance of write-in participants who join the event in an ad hoc manner. Event Management helps users convert write-ins to attendees or non-profiled attendees based on the linked record type and reconciliation

findings.name: Write-In Participant
findings.detail: Help users capture attendance of write-in participants who join the event in an ad hoc manner. Event Management helps users convert write-ins to attendees or non-profiled attendees based on the linked record type and reconciliation status.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. User Permissions Needed To add a related list for write-in attendees: | Life Sciences Commercial Admin permission set A write-in can already have a record in Salesforce (as an account), or can be a party profile, which represents an intermediate, non-profiled record that isn’t profiled as a standard account or contact yet. In either case, when the user adds the write-in as a participant, the system checks for the following things: The associated record (account versus party profile) The reconciliation outcome set by the user (completed profiled versus completed non-profiled) If the write-in is linked to an Account record, and the user sets the Participant Party Reconciliation Status to Completed Profiled, the WriteInToAttendeeHandler trigger handler converts the participant’s ParticipantType from Write-In Attendee to Attendee. If the write-in is non-profiled and is linked to a Party Profile record, and the user sets the Participant Party Reconciliation Status to Completed Non-Profiled, the WriteInToAttendeeHandler trigger handler converts the participant’s ParticipantType from Write-In Attendee to Non-Profiled Attendee. The system doesn’t convert the write-in in the following cases. A write-in linked to an account and the related Managed Event Participant record has a Participant Party Reconciliation Status of Completed Non-Profiled. A write-in linked to a party profile and the related Managed Event Participant record has a Participant Party Reconciliation Status of Completed Profiled. A write-in linked to any other object, such as User. A write-in whose related Managed Event Participant record has a Participant Party Reconciliation Status of Pending Reconciliation.

title: Attendee Quota
summary: Manage the scale of an event by implementing participant invitation quotas. Define the number of managed event participants that the user, who is assigned the colleague participant role and the contributor participant type, can add to an

findings.name: Attendee Quota
findings.detail: Manage the scale of an event by implementing participant invitation quotas. Define the number of managed event participants that the user, who is assigned the colleague participant role and the contributor participant type, can add to an event.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package.

findings.name: Exemption
findings.detail: Configure the managed event participant’s responses that indicate that the invite is excluded from being counted in the colleague’s invitation quota. Select the relevant statuses in the Colleague Invitation Quota Exempt Status multi-select picklist field in Field Event’s profile-level Admin Console configurations.

findings.name: Setup
findings.detail: Make sure you add the Default Invitation Quota field to the Managed Event’s page layout.

findings.name: How Attendee Quota Works
findings.detail: When the user adds a value to the Default Invitation Quota field, the MngEventPtcpSetAttendeeQuotaHandler trigger handler automatically updates the colleague’s invitation quota accordingly. When the user adds a new Managed Event Participant record with the participant type as colleague and the participant role as contributor, or when the user updates the participant type and role of an existing Managed Event Participant record to colleague and contributor, the MngEventPtcpSetAttendeeQuotaHandler trigger handler updates the Managed Event Participant’s Invitation Quota field to reflect the Managed Event’s Default Invitation Quota value. When a colleague invites an attendee to an event, the MngEventParticipantInvitedByHandler trigger handler updates the attendee Managed Event Participant record’s Invited By field to show the colleague’s Managed Event Participant record. When a colleague invites an attendee to an event, the AttendeeQuotaCountOfAttendeesHandler trigger handler updates the Current Invitation Count in the colleague’s Managed Event Participant record. If a colleague’s Current Invitation Count exceeds the Invitation Quota assigned to them, the system flags the violation in two ways On the web: The action is blocked with an error message. On mobile: The action is allowed, but in the Managed Event Participant record of the attendee who was added after the quota was exceeded, the Invitation Quota Discrepancy Reason field is marked as “Quota Exceeded”.

findings.name: Event Management Participant Sharing Rules
findings.detail: In Event Management, Managed Event records are shared in two ways: territory-based sharing, where access is granted to all users in a participant’s territory, and user-level sharing, where access is granted to an individual user.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package.

findings.name: Territory-Based Sharing
findings.detail: When users with organizer, coorganizer, and coordinator participant roles are invited to an event and they accept the invite, the MngEventParticipantSharingHandler trigger handler fetches the active territory associated with the user and creates Managed Event Territory records. The creation of Managed Event Territory records in turn triggers the MngEventTerritorySharingHandler handler and Managed Event Share records are created for all users of the territory.

findings.name: User-Level Sharing
findings.detail: When a user with an approver or host organizer participant role is invited to an event and they accept the invite, the Managed Event Share records are created specifically for that user. Note that only colleague type participants can trigger sharing logic.

findings.name: Exception
findings.detail: No sharing records are created for attendee, expert, and contributor roles.

findings.name: Invitation Requirement
findings.detail: The record sharing criteria involves the following invitation-related clauses. On the Managed Event Participant record, the Send Invitation checkbox must be selected. On the Managed Event Participant record, the Participant Response must be “Accepted”. Invitation must be sent and accepted for organizer, coorganizer, and approver roles to get the sharing records, whereas coordinators and host organizers have no invitation requirements. Organizer | Organizer | Territory | Yes | MngEventTerritory and MngEventShare (territory users) Coorganizer | Coorganizer | Territory | Yes | MngEventTerritory and MngEventShare (territory users) Coordinator | Coordinator | Territory | No | MngEventTerritory and MngEventShare (territory users) Approver | Approver | User-Level | Yes | MngEventShare (specific user) Host Organizer | HostOrganizer | User-Level | No | MngEventShare (specific user) Attendee | Attendee | None | N/A | No sharing Expert | Expert | None | N/A | No sharing Contributor | Contributor | None | N/A | No sharing

findings.name: Subject Assignment Admin Console Configurations
findings.detail: Get to know all the Admin Console profile-level settings that control expert eligibility and subject compliance in Event Management. Also, learn more about how subject compliance works. Check eligibility for subject presentation | This setting ensures that only those experts who have undergone due training can present on the assigned subject at an event. When this setting is enabled, it prevents the addition of subjects on which the expert speaker isn’t trained to present. Attendance History Subject Conflict Check in Days | The number of days the system must check in the participant’s attendance history to confirm that the participant hasn’t already attended an event with the same subject. Attendance Statuses for Subject Compliance | The status value of a participant’s attendance of a past event that qualifies them for the subject compliance check. Participant Subject Compliance Check Actions | The action to be taken if a colleague, expert, attendee, or non-profiled participant fails subject compliance validation on account of attending an event on the same subject in the recent past. The actions you can configure are Block, Warn, and None. Write-In Participant Subject Compliance Check Actions | The action to be taken if a write-in participant fails subject compliance validation on account of attending an event on the same subject in the recent past. The actions you can configure are Block, Warn, and None. Subject Compliance External ID List | The API name of the text field on the Subject record where you add the list of external IDs of compliance subjects. How Subject Compliance Works Subject compliance prevents changing the event’s start time if an attendee has attended an event with the same subject in the new proposed time frame. If you select Block, the system rejects the date change. If you select warn, the date change is accepted but with a warning, and a participant discrepancy reason is created. This compliance check is skipped if the Attendance History Subject Conflict Check in Days and the Attendance Statuses for Subject Compliance fields are empty. If an event is associated with a restricted subject product, the system will throw an error when you try to add a healthcare provider associated with the restricted product as a participant. If the start date of the managed event has already passed, the system allows you to add the participant with a warning. It will create a Managed Event Participant Discrepancy record with a discrepancy reason, such as, Managed Event contains restricted product. If the managed event start date is in the future, the system prevents you from adding the participant.
