findings.detail: Define the assets that facilitate the smooth orchestration of an event. Event logistics includes services that ensure that participants have access to the information and tools they require to attend an event, such as event venue, conference rooms, speakers, and technicians.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. User Permissions Needed To create managed event resources and managed event resource preferences: | Life Sciences Field Sales Representative permission set AND Life Sciences Core permission set Managed event resources represent the primary choice of the logistical provider for an event resource. Resources can be of different types, such as: venue locations, like hotels or hospitals; equipment to run the event, such as projectors and audiovisual tools; supplies for the event, like notepads and markers; catering services and refreshments. Managed Event Resource Preferences is a child of the Managed Event Resource object and it represents alternate resource options. For example, for a managed event resource called Hotel Astro California, multiple managed event resource preferences can exist, such as Hotel Astro San Diego and Hotel Astro San Jose. The Status fields of a Managed Event Resource object and the Managed Event Resource Preference object indicate whether the location is confirmed for an event. When the user confirms the status of a Managed Event Resource record or a Managed Event Resource Preference record, the event’s location is stamped with the address and location of the selected resource or the resource preference. Note An event can happen either in a hospital or at a physical location, but not in both of these types of places.

findings.name: Monetary Cap
findings.detail: Track event expenses and compare the total against an account's spending limit to determine whether the account can be added to the event. Monetary caps are account-level restrictions that limit the expense amounts that are allocated to a healthcare professional account across the events they're added to, for specific expense categories and for a specific period of time. These restrictions apply when an event organizer allocates actual or estimated costs to a participant, and when they add an attendee or expert to an event.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package.

findings.name: How Monetary Cap Works
findings.detail: Monetary caps represent the spending ceiling for each participant account. Before event organizers add a participant to an event, the system automatically checks whether the account has already reached its spending limit. Based on the provider activity measure type configured, the system either allows the addition with a warning, or blocks the addition entirely. The account spending limit is stored in the Provider Activity Goal Limit record. Monetary Cap adds up the relevant expenses for an event, and compares the total to the account's limit. The expense amounts that Monetary Cap calculates are grouped into three buckets: Estimated expenses: The amount of money that’s projected to be spent for one or more activities in an event. Committed expenses: The amount of money that’s approved for one or more activities in an event. Actual expenses: The amount of money that’s already expensed for one or more activities in an event. While an event is in progress, the system takes the higher of actual expenses versus the sum of estimated and committed expenses as the running total that it checks against the account's limit. Once an event is closed, the system considers only the actual expenses for monetary cap check. Whenever an attendee or expert is added to an event, or an allocation for actual or estimated expense is created, updated, or deleted, the system automatically recalculates the cap total and checks it against that limit. Only expenses whose type is marked Included in Cap count toward the limit. When a limit is breached, the system responds in one of two ways, depending on how the cap is configured: Error: The action is blocked, with an error message, preventing the participant from being added or the expense from being recorded. Warn: The action is allowed, but a Managed Event Participant Discrepancy record is created with a warning message. Actual expenses are stored in the parent Expense record, while expenses allocated to individual participants are stored in the child Expense Participant records. Estimated expenses are stored in the parent Estimated Expenses record, while expenses allocated to individual participants are stored in the child Estimated Expense Participant Allocation records.

findings.name: Prerequisites
findings.detail: Activate the monetary cap trigger handlers. Configure Lightning App Builder components. For more information, see Add and Customize Tabs on Lightning Pages Using the Lightning App Builder . Utilization Tracker Lightning App Builder component: Shows all the active monetary caps related to a participant's account. Add this component to the Account record page. lscRecordUpdateValidationNotifier component: Provides notifications when an account reaches or exceeds the monetary limits. Add this component to the Managed Event and Managed Event Participant record pages.

findings.name: Calculation of Total Expense
findings.detail: The total expenses are calculated based on the managed event’s status. If the managed event is completed, that is, the status represents a concluded state, the total expenses equal the actual expenses. Total = Actual If the managed event is not completed, that is, the status represents a draft state, the total expenses are the maximum of actual expenses and estimated plus committed expenses. Total = MAX(Actual, Estimated + Committed) The cap data is stored in the provider activity goal measure’s additional information field in JSON format and is rolled up into Committed Expense Amount, Actual Expense Amount, Estimated Expense Amount, and Total Expense Amount fields. The following code is an example of a monetary cap. {"1POXJOO0000002L4AU":{"isFinalValue":true,"isFinal":true,"estimatedMap": {},"estimated":{},"committedMap":{},"committed": {},"actualMap": {"1Z6XJ0000000iAjOAI":{"rate": 1.0,"amount":200.0},"1Z6XJ00000001970AA": {"rate":1.0,"amount": 100.0}},"actual":{"1Z6XJ0000000iAjOAI": {"rate": 1.0,"amount":200.0},"1Z6XJ00000001970AA": {"rate": 1.0, "amount":100.077}}}} Monetary Cap is calculated throughout the event. When the event is in progress, that is, when the event hasn’t reached the final status, the total expense is the greater of actual expenses and estimated plus committed expenses. When the event reaches the final status, only actual expenses count. The final status is determined based on the Concluded Event Status field in the event management’s org-level settings. The conversion rates are automatically updated based on the currency.

findings.name: Trigger Handlers
findings.detail: Make sure the following trigger handlers are active. See Manage Trigger Handlers . ExpenseParticipantMonetaryCapsHandler When expense participants are created, the handler recalculates the monetary cap utilization of the associated Provider Activity Goal Measure record. It blocks negative amounts from being allocated. When an expense participant’s amount is updated, the handler recalculates cap totals based on the new amount. If the monetary cap’s Alert Type is set up as Error, the handler blocks amount increases that would push the total over the cap. If the Alert Type is Warn, even if the monetary limit is exceeded, the handler allows the amount to increase. Decreases are always allowed without restriction — even if the current total is already over the cap — because they reduce utilization. Changes to any field other than amount trigger no recalculation at all. When an expense participant is deleted, the handler recalculates cap totals to remove the deleted amount. Deletions are always allowed because removing a participant always reduces the cap total. MngEventPartMonetaryCapsHandler When a new participant is being added to an event, the handler checks whether that provider’s spending cap has already been reached. If the monetary cap is set up with Alert Type as Error, the handler restricts the addition. If the monetary cap is set up with Alert Type as Warn, the handler allows it but with a warning. By default, the handler blocks all participant changes. The change is allowed only during an account merge or a write-in a reconciliation scenario, in which case the handler recalculates caps for both the old and new participant. If an account is swapped with a user, the monetary cap is reduced only for the account. During a mobile sync, the handler does not block the addition — instead, it marks a discrepancy for the participant. MngEventMonetaryCapsHandler If the managed event status is updated, the trigger handler recalculates the monetary cap limit for all the participants. If the status is not one of the qualifying statuses (such as, draft or closed), the handler removes the expense entry and the event is no longer tracked. If the managed event start date is updated to outside the associated activity plan’s time period, the handler removes the expense entry. If the event dates are within the activity plan time period, the handler recalculates the expense based on the new time period. If the managed event is deleted, the handler removes all the related contributions from the monetary cap limit. ExpenseMonetaryCapsHandler If the expense date is updated, the handler recalculates cap totals based on the new date. If the new date falls outside a configured time window, the expense no longer counts toward the cap. If any of the controlling fields defined in the ProviderActivityMeasureType’s Criteria JSON is updated but still meets the criteria, the handler recalculates the cap. If any of the controlling fields defined in the ProviderActivityMeasureType’s Criteria JSON is updated but fails to meet the criteria, the handler removes the contribution from the cap total. If an expense that’s marked as Included in Cap is deleted, the handler recalculates the expense and removes the expense’s entry. Only expenses whose type is marked as Included in Cap are counted. EstimatedExpenseMonetaryCapsHandler When an estimated expense is updated, the handler monitors the fields that are referenced in the provider activity goal measure’s criteria configuration. If any of those change, it recalculates monetary cap utilization for all child Estimated Expense Participant Allocation records. When an estimated expense is deleted, it recalculates in delete context so that those child allocations’ contribution is removed from the cap totals. It does not run on insert (no child allocations yet) and does not block or validate — it only recalculates. The EstExpensePtcpAllocMonetaryCapsHandler runs when allocations are added or changed. EstExpensePtcpAllocMonetaryCapsHandler When an Estimated Expense Participation Allocation record is inserted or updated, the handler rejects negative amounts, then checks whether the allocation would push the provider past their monetary cap. With Alert Type as Error, it blocks the estimated expense allocation; with Alert Type as Warning, it allows the estimated expense allocation and stamps a discrepancy. It then recalculates the monetary cap on Provider Activity Goal Measure record. When an allocation is deleted, the handler recalculates caps in delete context so that amount is removed from the estimated totals. For mobile sync transactions that would exceed the cap, the handler does not block the record; it creates a discrepancy and still recalculates for all records. Immutability Handlers Three immutability handlers block users from changing the participant in Expense Participant, Managed Event Participant, and EstimatedExpense Participant Allocation records, thereby preventing monetary caps from being bypassed. MngEventParticipantImmutabilityHandler Stops reassigning a participant between accounts after creation. After a managed event participant is created, the Participant field (Account or Expert lookup) can’t be changed on update. The exceptions to this handler are the Account Merge scenarios, where the system re-parents the participant, and write-in conversions, where the write-in attendees are reconciled and converted to attendee or non-profiled attendees. ExpenseParticipantImmutabilityHandler Stops moving an expense between accounts after creation. After an expense participant is created, the Participant field (Account or Contact lookup) can’t be changed on update. There are no exceptions to this handler. Account Merge isn’t affected because the account is updated in the Managed Event Participant record, and this change is automatically reflected in the Expense Participant record. EstimatedExpPtcpAllocImmutabilityHandler Stops moving an estimated allocation between participants after creation. After an estimated expense allocation is created, the Participant field (lookup to MngEventParticipant) can’t be changed on update. There are no exceptions to this handler. Account Merge re-parents the parent MngEventParticipant, but doesn’t change the Estimated Expense Participant Allocation’s Participant field directly, so the merge is unaffected.

findings.name: Batch Jobs
findings.detail: Calculate Expenses Against Monetary Caps: When data is uploaded in bulk and when the trigger handlers are not active, the batch job recalculates the actual and estimated expenses based on the latest account data. Multicurrency calculation must be enabled for the job to run. If there are no expense participants and estimated expense participant allocations, the monetary cap amounts reset to zero. If only expense participants are missing but estimated expense participant allocations exist, the monetary cap amounts consider the leftover estimated amounts. The Managed Event Participant Discrepancy records are added or deleted based on the data that the job finds at the time of run. Share Provider Activity Goals Based on Activity Plan Type: Shares provider activity goals that are associated with activity plans of type Event Management Limit with the territories aligned with an account. For goals that are associated with other types of activity plans, the job shares the goals in accordance with the sharing setting of the activity plan.

findings.name: Offline Mobile Sync
findings.detail: Monetary Caps handles offline monetary cap violations in the mobile based on the latest sync configurations. On the web, when the sales rep attempts to add a participant who has exceeded the monetary cap limit, the system blocks the action. On the mobile, when the sales rep attempts the same action while offline, the system allows or blocks the action based on the latest configuration synced on the mobile device. When an addition made offline despite an exceeded limit syncs with the web, the system doesn't reject it — the addition is allowed, and a Managed Event Participant Discrepancy record is created. findings.name: Prerequisites
findings.detail: In the org-level admin console settings for event management, configure the Concluded Event Status field to denote the final value of the status. This setting is used by provider activity goal measure to confirm that the event is over and to calculate the actual expenses for each participant. Create a territory in the territory hierarchy. Add a user (sales rep) to the territory, and assign an account, representing the participant, to the territory. For more information, see Set Up Sales Territories for Life Sciences Cloud Create an Expense Type record. Make sure the Expense Availability Type is Managed Event, and the start date and the end date of the expense type fall within the time period of the activity plan. Select the Included in Cap checkbox. For more information, see Expense Management . Create a parent Estimated Expense record, and child Estimated Expense Participant Allocation records. For more information, see Post-Approval Tasks .

findings.name: Criteria Configuration Structure for Monetary Limit
findings.detail: Provide real-time validations of an account's expenses versus its defined limits by configuring provider activity measure types. Specify when an expense (expense participant or estimated expense participant allocation) counts towards the actual or estimated buckets. Use the specified JSON structure to define high-level record filtering conditions, and then classify the record into expense types. Choose how you want the system to respond to limit breaches by configuring the alert type as Warning (allow the action but flag the discrepancy) or Error (block the action). You can configure the Provider Activity Measure Type’s criteria configuration in two formats: the older format for the Expense Participant object (version 1) and the enhanced format for Event Management Expense enum (version 2), which includes Expense Participant, Estimated Expense Participant Allocation and Managed Event Participant objects. The context condition's relationship path can reference up to 5 levels from the root object. Older Criteria JSON Configuration The older JSON format is applicable only for monetary cap calculation of actual expenses. The provider activity measure type's activity object is Expense Participant. The provider activity measure type's criteria uses a JSON structure that has two sections—context criteria, which contains high-level filter conditions, and utilization types, which categorizes the expense into buckets. The utilization conditions you add for the estimated and committed buckets are not taken into account, and the system only categorizes the expense into the actual bucket. Operators must be in Pascal case (Equals, In, NotEquals, NotIn) There are no versions in the older format. In version 1, the JSON checks only for expenses. But the system must verify whether a participant has hit the monetary cap when the sales rep tries to add them to an event. The system carries out the evaluation via internal checks. In version 2, the configuration supports an explicit contextCondition evaluation on a participant block. { "contextCondition": { "conditions": [ {"field": "MngEvent.Status", "operator": "In", "value": "Draft;Approved;Closed"} ] }, "utilizationTypes": { "estimated": { "conditions": [{"field": "MngEvent.Status", "operator": "Equals", "value": "Draft"}] }, "committed": { "conditions": [{"field": "MngEvent.Status", "operator": "Equals", "value": "Approved"}] }, "actual": { "conditions": [{"field": "MngEvent.Status", "operator": "Equals", "value": "Closed"}] } } } Enhanced Criteria JSON Configuration The enhanced JSON format helps calculate monetary caps for both actual expenses and estimated and committed expenses. In the newer format, the Activity Object is Event Management Expenses, which is a categorization, rather than a Salesforce object. Since there is no object in the newer format, users have to specify the version (version 2). The JSON structure has three nodes for the Expense Participant, Estimated Expense Participant Allocation, and Managed Event Participant objects. Within the Expense Participant and the Estimated Expense Participant Allocation nodes, the structure has two sections—the context condition and the expense bucket. The context condition sets the filter criteria, while the expense bucket determines whether the expense falls into the estimated bucket, the committed bucket, or the actual bucket. The JSON structure for the Managed Event Participant node contains the context condition section that decides whether the monetary cap check runs when the event organizer tries to add a participant as an attendee or an expert to an event. If the condition matches and the account is already over the limit, the action is blocked or allowed with a warning. If the condition doesn’t match, the cap check doesn’t apply for that action. { "version": 2, "ExpenseParticipant": { "contextCondition": { "conditions": [ {"field": "MngEvent.Status", "operator": "In", "value": "Draft;Approved;Closed"} ] }, "expenseBuckets": { "actual": { "conditions": [{"field": "MngEvent.Status", "operator": "In", "value": "Closed"}] }, "committed": { "conditions": [{"field": "MngEvent.Status", "operator": "Equals", "value": "Approved"}] } } }, "EstimatedExpensePtcpAlloc": { "contextCondition": { "conditions": [ {"field": "MngEvent.Status", "operator": "In", "value": "Draft;Approved"} ] }, "expenseBuckets": { "estimated": { "conditions": [{"field": "MngEvent.Status", "operator": "Equals", "value": "Draft"}] }, "committed": { "conditions": [{"field": "MngEvent.Status", "operator": "Equals", "value": "Approved"}] } } }, "MngEventParticipant": { "contextCondition": { "conditions": [ {"field": "MngEvent.Status", "operator": "In", "value": "Draft;Approved"} ] } } } Criteria JSON Validations If you select Expense Participant as the activity object, you must specify the older structure. Similarly, if you select Event Management Expenses as the activity object, you must specify the newer structure. If you select Expense Participant as the activity object and specify version 2 in the JSON structure or use the newer JSON structure, the record will not be saved. You can use the older format to calculate actual expenses, without adding a version. In version 1, you must add a section for context condition, utilization types, and at least one bucket for actual. The field in the context condition must be valid. If you select Event Management Expenses as the Activity Object, you must specify version 2. Operators must be in Pascal case (Equals, In, NotEquals, NotIn). Lowercase or other forms fail silently or throw errors. In both version 1 and version 2, you must specify the Provider Activity Measure Type's Category as MonetaryCapLimit. In both version 1 and version 2, the field in the field path must be in the object whose section it is in. In version 1, the field in the field path must be valid and must be in the Expense Participant object. In version 2, the field in the field path must be valid and must be in the object whose section it is in (Expense Participant, Estimated Expense Participant Allocation, and Managed Event Participant).

findings.name: Monetary Cap Enforcement Behavior
findings.detail: (Version 1 and 2) Actual expense operations aren’t blocked when they’re over the cap; the amounts still update and a discrepancy is stamped. (Version 2) Estimated allocations are blocked when over the cap (Error); the record is not created. (Version 1 and 2) If context conditions don’t match, the expense is not counted toward the cap. (Version 1 and 2) For the participant cap, Error blocks insert; Warning allows create and stamps a warn discrepancy. (Version 1 and 2) Actual expenses and estimated expense allocations with IsIncludedInCap = false are not considered for monetary cap calculation. (Version 2) If the configuration has no Managed Event Participant node, participants are not blocked even when over the limit. (Version 1 and 2) If multiple provider activity measure types apply (block and warning), block takes precedence. (Version 1 and 2) A closed event drops estimates from the total calculation. (Version 2) If the event’s date and time changes or if the event's status moves to closed, the MngEventMonetaryCapsHandler trigger handler recalculates the monetary caps. (Version 2) Deleting an Expense Participant record or an Estimated Expense Participant Allocation record triggers recalculation and reduces the related amounts.

findings.name: Activity Plan Record Sharing Rules
findings.detail: Learn more about how activity plans are shared with users, such as the event organizer. By default, activity plans and provider activity goals are not shared with non-admin users, like sales reps. To share these records with sales reps, run the Share Provider Activity Goals Based on Activity Plan Type job. The system creates Provider Activity Goal Share records and Activity Plan Share records of Life Sciences Commercial Auto Share type, and shares them with the territories aligned to the participant account.

findings.name: Prerequisite
findings.detail: Before you run the Share Provider Activity Goals Based on Activity Plan Type job, change the provider activity goal sharing settings from Controlled by Parent to Private. You can find the sharing settings in Setup.

findings.name: How Sharing Works
findings.detail: If activity plans already exist, changing the sharing settings from Controlled by Parent to Private also changes the sharing access of the associated provider activity goals, goal measure, and goal limits. To ensure that access is not lost, the batch job shares the activity plans, provider activity goals and associated records based on activity plan type. If the activity plan type is Event Management Limit, the batch job shares provider activity goals and activity plans with the territories aligned with the account. If the activity plan type is anything other than Event Management Limit, the batch job shares provider activity goals, and associated goal measures and goal limits, based on the parent activity plan shares. When provider activity goals are shared, all associated activity plan objects such as provider activity goal measure, provider activity goal limit, are shared accordingly.

findings.name: How Sharing Works for Manual Shares
findings.detail: Additionally, to ensure that provider activity goals inherit the sharing settings of existing activity plans that were shared manually with users, turn on the Include Records of All Sharing Types in Workflows toggle in Life Sciences for Customer Engagement Setup. When enabled, this setting considers all sharing types, including manual shares, for all Life Sciences processes. When turned off, Life Sciences workflows only consider the Life Sciences Commercial Auto Share sharing type. When the Share Provider Activity Goals Based on Activity Plan Type batch job is run after the Include Records of All Sharing Types in Workflows toggle is turned on, the batch job replicates all sharing types, including manual shares, in the provider activity goal sharing settings. When the toggle is turned off, the batch job only replicates Life Sciences Commercial Auto Share sharing type settings for provider activity goal sharing settings. For more information, see Get Your Org Ready for the Customer Engagement Managed Package .

title: Account Utilization Limits

findings.name: Account Utilization Limits
findings.detail: Help sales reps check in real time whether an account meets the eligibility criteria for event attendance. Configure account-based participation limits to cap the number of events an account can attend in a specific time period. Provide instant notifications based on configurable alert types that block or warn the organizer when the account exceeds their limit. To support fair reporting, the system maintains a log of exceptions by automatically creating Managed Event Participant Discrepancy records.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. When a Managed Event Participant is created, updated, or deleted, Utilization Limit recalculates the utilization of the account and logs discrepancies if needed. Updating a Managed Event recalculates utilization only when a field in the criteria changes, or when the event’s start date and time changes, even if that field is not in the criteria. Moving the event into a different plan period updates the counts on both the old and new plans. Deleting a Managed Event also recalculates utilization, but creating a Managed Event by itself does not.

findings.name: How Account Utilization Works
findings.detail: To track the number of events a healthcare professional account has attended versus the total number of events the account is allowed to attend, you must create an activity plan, a provider activity goal, provider activity goal limit, and provider activity goal measures for the account. Activity plans track interactions between sales reps and healthcare professionals for a specific time period. Admins set activity targets for the sales reps to fulfill through Provider Activity Goal records. The total number of activities that a healthcare professional account can attend in a time period is established through the Provider Activity Goal Limit record’s Activity Limit field. The Provider Activity Goal Measure records store the utilization count via the Total Activity Value field, which represents the total number of events an account has attended, and the Additional Information field, which stores the Managed Event Participant’s IDs. Configure the criteria for checking the account’s utilization by creating a Provider Activity Measure Type record from the Developer Console. The criteria configuration follows a JSON format that first filters the record, and then puts the participant into a utilization type bucket (actual, committed, and estimated). For more information, see Considerations for Using Utilization Limits . When an account is added to an event, removed from an event, or when the Managed Event Participant record is updated, the system recalculates the account’s utilization count. If the account’s utilization count is exactly at limit, the account is added to the event as a participant without a warning message. If the account’s utilization count exceeds the limit, and the Provider Activity Measure Type’s Alert Type is set as Warning, the account is added to the event as a participant but with a warning message, and a Managed Event Participant Discrepancy record is created. If the account’s utilization count exceeds the limit, and the Provider Activity Measure Type’s Alert Type is set as Error, the account is not added to the event as a participant.

findings.name: Batch Jobs
findings.detail: Share Provider Activity Goals Based on Activity Plan Type: Shares the participant account's provider activity goals with the territories aligned with the account. The goals that are shared must be associated with activity plans of type Event Management Limit. For goals that are associated with other types of activity plans, the job shares the goals in accordance with the sharing setting of the activity plan.

Create a provider activity goal to link the account to the activity plan. Create event management participant type role mappings . Make sure the following trigger handlers are active. See Manage Trigger Handlers . MngEventAcctUtilLmtsHandler MngEventPartAcctUtilLmtsHandler

Use the criteria JSON to set the filter criteria and sort records into different utilization buckets. Choose how you want the system to handle accounts that are at limit or exceed limit by specifying the alert type. You must follow the JSON structure in the sample code. findings.name: Check Account Utilization By Running a Batch Job
findings.detail: To calculate the utilization count of a large number of accounts in one go, run the Recalculate Account Utilization Count batch job.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. The Recalculate Account Utilization Count batch job recalculates account utilization from scratch and is particularly useful for the following scenarios. While processing bulk data imports During initial setup of Event Management, when trigger handlers aren't activated After you make configuration changes such as modifying limit records or criteria JSON. The batch job can be invoked through the Admin Console UI settings, API, Apex code, or through custom flows, depending on your org's needs. Batch Job Through a Flow and Invocable Action To run the batch job for a specific time period, use a Salesforce flow to invoke the batch job. The Activity Plan ID input parameter is optional and controls the scope of recalculation. If you don't specify an Activity Plan ID, the batch job automatically selects activity plans based on the current time and date and recalculates utilization counts for all accounts associated with those plans. If you explicitly specify an Activity Plan ID, the batch job recalculates goal measures only for accounts related to that specific plan, even if the plan is inactive.

findings.name: Prerequisites for Email Integration
findings.detail: Make sure that the user is assigned to the same territory that the managed event is part of. The territory must also be active. Add dynamic picklist values for the Subject Material Template’s Template Type field, such as EmailTemplate. Add the Life Science Email Template Snapshot related list to the Life Science Email Template object’s page layout. Add the Files related list to the Life Science Email Template Snapshot object’s page layout. The managed event must have participants added to it. Create a Subject record. Make sure the usage type is Managed Event. Create a Subject Assignment record. Add ZIP files to the email template. Each template version must have an HTML file and a thumbnail. For more information on what you can include in the ZIP files, see Dynamic Capabilities for Email Templates . Use the following values as an example to create an HTML file. Title | index PathOnClient | index.html FileType | HTML Content | The HTML body Use the following values as an example to create a JPG file. Title | thumbnail PathOnClient | thumbnail.jpg FileType | JPG Content | Any JPG image Merge Variables in the HTML File When you send an email to a participant, the record data is populated dynamically via merge variables in the HTML file. Merge variables are stand-in tokens embedded in email templates that get replaced with actual data at run time. Learn more about merge variables and their usage in Event Management. By default, any standard or custom field on the Managed Event, Account, User, and User Additional Info objects can be used as a merge variable. For Event Management to auto-populate the record data, the user must have access to the field in the variable, and the field must have a value. The merge variable must follow the mustache token syntax (double curly braces): {{object.fieldname}} , in lower case. Use the following merge variables as examples to draft your own. Managed Event: {{mngevent.name}}, {{mngevent.status}} Account (recipient): {{recipient.firstname}}, {{recipient.lastname}} User (sender): {{sender.name}}, {{sender.email}} User Additional Info (a related object): {{sender.useradditionalinfo.fieldname}}

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. Event Participants | A participant with the same type and role can’t be added twice to the same event. The current user must be added as a colleague-type participant before they can add other participants. The Event Management Participant Type Role Mapping record must be active for participants to be added. When an attendee or non-profiled attendee is added, the Invited By field is auto-populated with the ID of the colleague sending the invite. The Invitation Sent Date and Time is automatically populated when the Invitation Sent checkbox is selected. You can’t delete a participant who has an organizer role. Participant Recruitment | When a managed event is created, the system automatically adds the creator as the organizer. If the user (event creator) adds another user as the primary owner, the creator becomes the coordinator and the other user becomes the organizer. If the user (event creator) adds their manager as the primary owner, the creator becomes the coordinator and the manager becomes the approver. Attendee Quota | Only colleagues with the contributor role have an invitation quota. When the Default Invitation Quota field is filled in, the system automatically applies it to all contributor-type colleagues. On the web: if a colleague exceeds their invitation quota, the action is blocked with an error. On mobile: if a colleague exceeds their quota while offline, the attendee is added, but a Managed Event Participant Discrepancy record is created with the reason “Quota Exceeded.” Participant Sharing Rules | A colleague with an organizer role is required for sharing records to be created. Managed Event Share and Managed Event Territory records are created only when an invitation has been sent and the participant’s response is “Accepted.” Coordinators and host organizers do not require an accepted invitation for sharing to be triggered. No sharing records are created for attendee, expert, or contributor roles. Subject Assignment | The same subject can’t be assigned to the same event twice. If an Expert participant has already been added to an event, subjects with a compliance type of Speaker Bureau won’t appear in search results. Remove the expert to see all subjects. If a subject is associated with a restricted product and the associated participant has already been added, the system throws an error (or a warning if the event start date has passed). Changing the event’s start date is blocked (or warned) if an existing participant has already attended an event on the same subject within the new proposed timeframe. If a workflow path is configured, subject assignment follows the workflow stage operations. Compliance Management | Only the organizer and coorganizer of an event can respond to compliance statements. The Compliance Agreement Status remains “Agreement Required” until all mandatory statements are accepted, after which it changes to “Agreed.” Only Compliance Statement Definition records with a statement type of Compliance Note or Compliance Agreement, a module type of Managed Event, and statement text filled in are displayed in the component. Event Logistics | A managed event can have only one location — either a Venue or an HCO, but not both. When adding a location, the address selected must correspond to the resource type chosen (for example, an HCO location must use the HCO’s address; a Venue location must use the Venue’s address). The first time a Venue or HCO resource is confirmed, the location is automatically stamped onto the Managed Event record. Monetary Caps | If the alert type is Error: adding a participant whose total expenses have reached or exceeded the monetary limit is prevented with an error. If the alert type is Warning: the participant can be added, but a Managed Event Participant Discrepancy record is created as a warning. On mobile (offline): cap limits are not enforced at the time of the action; violations are flagged via a discrepancy record when the device syncs. Only expenses with the Included in Cap checkbox selected count toward monetary cap calculations. The cap is only finalized once the managed event reaches a concluded or closed status (as configured in the Concluded Event Status Admin Console setting). Expense Management | All estimated expenses for the same expense type on the same event must be unique. For example, two “Food” estimates on the same event are not supported. If partial allocation is not enabled, the total allocated amount must exactly equal the actual expense amount. If partial allocation is enabled, underallocation is allowed, but overallocation (allocating more than the actual expense amount) is not. Integration with Email | The user sending the email must be assigned to the same active territory as the managed event. The managed event must have participants added before emails can be sent. Each email template version must include an HTML file (for the email body) and a JPG thumbnail. Integration with Presentations | Presentations are filtered by the subject assigned to the event and the current user’s territory. Integration with Calendar | Managed events created from the calendar must fall within the organization’s configured business hours. Integration with Surveys | The managed event must be in the workflow stage configured for survey launch for the survey to appear. Only the organizer or coorganizer of the event can view and launch the survey. For territory-based survey sharing, the territory switcher must match the territory associated with the survey subject. Event Workflow | The Managed Event Default Operation must remain in the workflow for each stage. Removing the operation causes an error. The workflow path is driven by the Managed Event’s Status field. The picklist values for this field must be created for the workflow to function. Each stage exposes only the actions relevant to that role — Organizers see planning actions in Draft; only the Approver sees Approve or Reject in Pending Approval. The approval process is supported only on the web. If a workflow path is configured, subject assignment is subject to the workflow stage operations defined in the path.

findings.name: Set Up Common Customer Engagement Components
findings.detail: Notify users of critical updates with App Alerts. Prevent legal and regulatory violations by making informed decisions with License Validation Checks. Manage complex business processes and guide users through their tasks with clear steps with multi-step workflows and related lists. Maximize customer engagement efficiency with Multi-Object Components and Dynamic Tree Views. Create Quick and Custom Actions for smoother workflows. Visualize Sales Data for effective customer interactions.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. App Alerts Deliver in-app notifications, recommendations, guided actions, and announcements to users in their flow of work by using App Alerts. Create and assign alerts to specific territories to make sure that notifications reach the right users. Use App Alerts to enhance in-app communication, drive user engagement, and avoid missing opportunities. Alerts appear in the Notifications experience, on record pages, or on the home page of the Life Sciences Commercial app and Life Sciences Cloud Mobile app. Dynamic Tree View Components for Life Sciences Configure a Dynamic Tree View component to show related Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement data in an expandable hierarchy. Users can easily explore related records in one place without going to multiple pages, boosting visibility and saving time. For example, show the account hierarchy within a health system, or visualize how healthcare professionals (HCPs) and healthcare organizations (HCOs) are aligned under specific territories. Error Log Management in Life Sciences Subscriber logs capture the errors and diagnostic messages that occur in Life Sciences Cloud so that you can review them and act on them. The logs give you visibility into problems that your users encounter, whether the problem happens during server-side processing or in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. Go to the Error Log Management tile in the Admin Console to view subscriber logs and control how long the log details are available. License Management in Life Sciences Help your company comply to legal and regulatory standards, and adhere to audit-tracking measures with flexible license validity evaluations. License management in Life Sciences is a critical process that makes sure that healthcare providers (HCPs) have the required license and authorization to receive pharmaceutical samples. Multi-Object Components for Life Sciences The Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement multi-object components consolidate fields from several related objects onto a single record page, making it easier for users to view and manage data. Showing fields from multiple objects together helps users avoid going to multiple pages and simplifies the workflows for accounts, inquiries, and visits. Provider Bulk Sync Provider Bulk Sync helps organizations to effectively and efficiently manage their relationships with Healthcare Organizations (HCOs) and Healthcare Providers (HCPs). It allows organizations to integrate HCP and HCO data from IQVIA OneKey directly into the Life Sciences Cloud data model. This process helps organizations get verified HCP data, which helps users have the right information for their customer engagement plans and activities. The verified data can be used for territory planning and other processes. Quick and Custom Action Management Quick Actions and Custom Actions are shortcuts that provide fast access to key features in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. These actions are available directly from record pages, the home page, and custom components. Related Lists for Life Sciences Records in Salesforce can include details and links to other related records. The Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement related list offers more customization and filtering options than standard related lists. If you create a Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement workflow, you can also control the actions that users can take on related records based on the parent record’s status, user role, and other business rules. These related lists are supported both online and offline in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. Reports and Dashboards Administration Use reports and dashboards to deliver information to your Life Sciences Cloud mobile app users in the ways that work best for them. Run Batch Jobs Automate the processing of large record volumes by running Apex batch jobs from the Admin Console. Trigger Handler Administration View and activate trigger handlers in the Life Sciences Customer Engagement Admin Console. Workflows for Life Sciences Life Sciences Customer Engagement workflows automate your business processes and guide users through their tasks with clear steps. Configure the permissions and actions for each step of the workflow based on the users' context and role. Implement custom validations to make sure that users follow business processes, and provide checklists to help users understand how to use the workflow. These workflows are supported both online and offline in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app.

findings.name: App Alerts Overview
findings.detail: Use App Alerts to create notifications, define how and when they appear, and deliver them to the correct users. App Alerts centralizes all alerts in one place and helps users to take immediate action. The alerts appear directly within the Life Sciences Commercial app and Life Sciences Cloud Mobile app, keeping users informed without disrupting their workflow.

findings.name: Types of Alerts
findings.detail: All alerts share a common framework but they’re categorized by where they appear and who they target. The two main categories are: App Alerts: Versatile notifications that are delivered via the global notification bell or specific tabs. They use territory targeting to ensure that the right messages reach the right regional teams. Record Alerts: Contextual notifications that are delivered via the notification bell icon. They appear directly on a record page to provide immediate, relevant insights while a user is actively working on that specific data point. Both app alerts and record alerts are further categorized by their purpose into Notifications, Recommendations, and Guided actions. App alert has an additional subtype called Announcements. Type | Purpose | Where It Appears | Example Notification | Used for general alerts or informational updates. Notifications surface relevant updates without elevating them to the level of recommendations. | Web and Mobile: Alerts tab | New Safety Update for Immunexis The Medical Affairs team has released updated prescribing guidance for Immunexis in patients 65+. Review before your next healthcare professional visit. Actions: View Updated Prescribing Information; Open Safety Summary Recommendation | Used to highlight important opportunities or suggested next steps. Recommendations are designed to stand out more than standard notifications and guide users toward meaningful engagement actions. | Web and Mobile: Recommendations tab | Opportunity: Dr. Morita – Low Adoption of Immunexis Dr. Morita has 15 eligible patients but prescribed Immunexis only twice in the past 60 days. Based on prescribing data, a follow-up discussion on Immunexis efficacy may be beneficial. Actions: Create Visit; Send Email Guided Action | Used to guide users through structured tasks or initiatives that should remain visible over time. Guided Actions often include multiple resources and deep links to support execution. | Web: Alerts tab Mobile: Guided Action tab | Q2 Launch Excellence Program – Immunexis Expansion Corporate initiative to increase Immunexis adoption among Tier A cardiologists. Actions: View Target HCP List; Launch Sales Aid; Review Objection Handling Guide; Update Assessment Task Announcement | Used for organization-wide communications, such as home office updates or internal announcements rather than territory-based delivery. Announcements appear on the home page for maximum visibility. Announcements are delivered via App Alerts, not Record Alerts. | Web and Mobile: Announcements Lightning component on the home page | Q2 Sales Kickoff Announcement Join the upcoming kickoff session to learn about the Immunexis expansion strategy and territory priorities for the next quarter.

findings.name: Methods for Creating Alerts
findings.detail: You can create alerts for users in three ways, depending on your business needs. Manual Creation Create App Alert and Record Alert records to configure alerts. For more information, see Create an Alert . To control alert visibility and ensure that alerts reach the correct users, map each alert to one or more territories by creating App Alert Territory records. These records determine the target users by territory and the specific time period during which the alert remains visible. For a user to see an alert, make sure the user’s active territory matches the one set in the App Alert Territory records. For more information about configuring visibility and sharing behavior, see Share App Alerts . Automated Creation Automate alert delivery by triggering record alerts based on business logic or user activity. For example, configure rules by using Business Rules Engine to send alerts when an event status changes, or use Flow to deliver alerts automatically based on real-time context. See Create Record Alerts Using Business Rules Engine . External System Integration If you have critical information stored outside of Salesforce, use this method to surface that data as an alert. See Show External System Record Alerts in Salesforce .

findings.detail: Set up alerts so your organization can send relevant and targeted notifications, recommendations, and guided actions to users across web and mobile experiences. Configure the trigger handlers, enable alert-related components, assign access to the Apex classes, and activate the Life Sciences Commercial app for the standard user profile. Proper setup ensures that alerts appear consistently and support the intended user workflows.

findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. User Permissions Needed To configure App Alerts: | Life Sciences Commercial Admin Prerequisites: Make sure that you have configured profiles and assigned permission sets to users based on their roles. See Assign Permission Sets to Life Sciences Customer Engagement Users . If you’re using territory targeting, ensure that your territory model includes territory types, active territory models, and user assignments to territories. For more information, see Set Up Territory Types and Territories . Verify that your Salesforce org uses the default sharing settings, as App Alert record sharing is based on territory assignments. In the sharing settings for the App Alert and Record Alert objects, verify that default internal access is set to Private . On each user profile, verify that the View All Records permission is disabled for the App Alert and Record Alert objects. Configure trigger handlers for App Alerts. From the App Launcher, find and select Admin Console . Click Trigger Handler Administration . Turn on NotificationTerritorySharingHandler . Verify if a record with the developer name NotificationTerritorySharingHandler exists on the LifeScienceTriggerHandler object. If not, create one. Make sure that your users have the Life Sciences Core permission set to access these required Apex classes. LWCSoqlConnector NotificationsComponentController TerritorySwitcherCmpController See Assign Permission Sets to Life Sciences Customer Engagement Users . Alternatively, you can manually provide access to these Apex classes. For more information, see Set Apex Class Access from Permission Sets and Set Apex Class Access from Profiles . Set Up App Alerts for Web Configure the web experience so users can view alerts directly within the Life Sciences Commercial app. Add the built-in Notifications List Lightning component to a record page or home page to ensure that users can access and interact with alerts within the standard web workflow. The details on the component appear based on the context and visibility rules that you configure. Set Up App Alerts for Mobile Configure the mobile experience so that app alerts appear correctly in the Life Sciences Cloud Mobile app. Set up the required mobile metadata, components, and configurations so users can receive and interact with timely alerts on their mobile devices. Set Up Home Office Announcements for Web and Mobile Configure the web and mobile experience so that announcements and messages from the home office are visible to users. Add the Announcements Lightning component to a record page or home page of the Life Sciences Commercial app and Life Sciences Cloud Mobile app.

findings.name: Create an App Alert
findings.detail: App alerts are contextual notifications that appear in the Notifications experience and in specific areas of the application. When you create an alert, select a context type to control where the alert appears: Global, Object, and Tab. You can also include an additional message to provide links, actions, or tags that guide users toward their next steps.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. User Permissions Needed To configure App Alerts: | Life Sciences Commercial Admin From the App Launcher, find and select App Alerts . Click New . Enter a subject. Select the type of alert. Notification : Provides short, contextual updates about relevant actions or statuses. Recommendation : Guides users toward the next best action or suggestion. Guided Action : Directs users through specific tasks by using predefined instructions. Announcement : Shares broad internal communication, such as home office announcements. For more information, see Create Home Office Announcements . If you set the alert type to None, the app alert is considered as a notification. Select the display context type. Object : Shows the alert on all the record pages of a specific object. After you select Object , specify the object name in the Display Context Name field. For example, enter Account so the app alert is visible on all Account pages. Note: Object type is supported only on mobile. Tab : Shows the alert on a specific tab in the app. After you select Tab , specify the tab details in the Display Context Name field. There are three distinct naming conventions for tabs and you can refer to this table for examples. Standard Tab | Prefix with “standard-" | standard-home standard-Visit Managed Package Tab | Prefix with the namespace | For Account, use lsc4ce__AccountFilter For Calendar, use lsc4ce__Planner For Intelligent Content, use lsc4ce__IntelligentContent For Sales Data, use lsc4ce__SalesData Custom Tab | No prefix | Defined by admins Note: Tab type is supported only on mobile. Global : Shows the alert across all pages. Note: Global type is supported only on mobile. Note For Display Context Type, Global is selected by default. If you the field is left blank, alerts appear only on the home page. Select the effective start date and time. Indicates the date and time from when the alert becomes visible to users. If needed, in Valid Until Date, select the effective end date and time. On mobile, notifications and recommendations are visible by default for up to 7 days from the effective start date, unless removed earlier by users. If you don't set a value in the Valid Until Date field for web, alerts are visible indefinitely until the user marks them as Read. If needed, in Additional Message, enter a JSON-formatted value that follows the supported scheme. The Additional Message field appears only on mobile. This field supports a JSON structure that enables deep links, external website links, action buttons, and tags on mobile. If the alert is actionable, define the action and mark it as Dismissed or Resolved using the actionName attribute in the JSON. For more information, see Additional Message for App Alerts on Mobile . If needed, enter a message. The Message field appears on both the web and mobile applications. Note: If you provide valid values in both the Message and Additional Message fields, only the content in the Additional Message field appears on mobile. To avoid inconsistencies between web and mobile displays, we recommend keeping the content in the Message and Additional Message fields consistent. Save your changes.

findings.name: Additional Message for App Alerts on Mobile
findings.detail: Use the Additional Message field on App Alerts and Record Alerts to enhance alerts with structured, actionable content. This field supports formatted text, navigation links, external action buttons, and categorization tags in the alert. By supporting rich messaging and contextual actions, the field enables users to understand the notification and take the next step directly from the alert interface.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package.

findings.name: JSON Structure Overview
findings.detail: The Additional Message field uses a structured JSON format consisting of three primary sections: message , notificationActions , and tags . The sections provide contextual guidance, navigation shortcuts, and classification labels for the alert. General Structure: { "message": "", "notificationActions": [], "tags": [""] } Example for a complete JSON-formatted Additional Message field: { "message": "Share the latest Immunexis efficacy message with /view\">Dr. Aaron Morita.", "notificationActions": [ { "title": "Check New Content", "action": "lsc://deeplink/lightning/n/lsc4ce__IntelligentContent" }, { "title": "Dismiss", "actionable": true, "actionName": "Dismissed", "dismissOptions": ["Acknowledged"], "dismissOptionRequired": true } ], "tags": ["Recommendation","Next Best"] } Attribute | Description message | Defines the message body of the alert. Supports formatted text and hyperlinks for using tags. notificationActions | Defines interactive actions, such as links and buttons. tags | Defines informational labels for alert categorization.

findings.name: Message
findings.detail: The message section defines the primary alert content shown to users. The section can include navigation links embedded in text by using HTML anchor () tags. Only hyperlink tags are supported inside the message content. For supported link types and deep link formats, see Navigation Links in Additional Message . Because the message value is stored as a JSON string, make sure any double quotes (") inside the message are escaped by using a backslash (\). This is required when you define hyperlinks using the href attribute. Example for a hyperlink format: Link Text Example for a deep link to a specific Account record: "message":"Share the latest efficacy message with /view\">Dr. Aaron Morita. Check the updated content, plan your next visit, and loop in your team." To open the link in the device’s default external browser, such as Safari on iOS, include the target="_blank" attribute in the hyperlink. Link Text Note External browsers require users to sign in again because authentication tokens aren't passed automatically. To ensure a seamless experience without additional prompts, we recommend that use the in-app browser. Alternatively, users can navigate to the user profile icon on the mobile app, select View Online, and then select the App Alert URL to bypass manual authentication.

findings.name: Notification Actions
findings.detail: The notificationActions section defines interactive buttons within the alert interface. You can implement two distinct types of actions: Link actions and Response actions. 1. Link Actions Link actions allow users to go to internal Life Sciences Cloud destinations, external websites, or external applications. These actions use the navigation link formats and open destinations using a URL-based action. General Structure: { "title": "Button Label", "action": "URL" } Example: { "title": "Add to Upcoming Visit", "action": "lsc://deeplink/lightning/r/Visit/<VisitRecordID>/edit" } field | description title | Specifies the label shown on the action button. action | Specifies the navigation link or URL that the action directs to. 2. Response Actions Response actions allow users to update the state of the alert directly. Users can dismiss, resolve, or acknowledge a message. Use these actions to mark notifications as handled or trigger automated workflows. These actions can collect a reason when users dismiss the alert. General Structure: { "title": "Button Label", "actionable": true, "actionName": "ResponseValue", "dismissOptions": ["Reason1", "Reason2"], "dismissOptionRequired": true } Example: { "title": "Dismiss", "actionable": true, "actionName": "Dismissed", "dismissOptions": ["Acknowledged", "Expired"], "dismissOptionRequired": true } field | Required? | Description title | Yes | Specifies the label shown on the action button. actionable | Yes | Indicates whether the action is interactive. When the actionable property is set to true, the action button becomes active, and the system records the user's response. Skip this field for actions that open a web URL or deep link. actionName | Yes | Specifies the outcome when users interact with the action. Supported values are Dismissed and Resolved. dismissOptions | No | Specifies a list of predefined dismissal reasons that the user can select from when they dismiss the alert. dismissOptionalRequired | No | Indicates whether selecting a dismissal reason is required. Note Dismissal reason text in dismissOptions isn't validated for length when you configure the alert. However, only the first 40 characters of the reason that a user selects are saved when the user dismisses the alert. Keep each dismissal reason to 40 characters or fewer so that saved records and reporting capture the full text.

findings.name: Tags
findings.detail: The tags section uses tags to categorize additional messages and visually highlight their context and purpose. Tags appear as labels in the alert and help users quickly recognize the type of message. You can assign one or more tags to a message. Tags can represent campaign names, feature highlights, or categories, such as Territory, Engagement, and Product Update. In the Additional Message JSON field, define tags by using the tags attribute. The attribute accepts an array of text values and each value represents a label displayed in the alert. General Structure: "tags": ["<tag label>", "<tag label>"] Example: "tags": ["Next Best Message", "Agentforce","Visit Prep"] Navigation Links in Additional Message The message and notificationActions sections of the Additional Message field support navigation links that allow users to interact with records, tabs, and external platforms directly from an alert. Navigation links use URL-based actions that are categorized into three distinct types: Internal application navigation, External website navigation, and External application navigation.

findings.name: Error Log Management in Life Sciences
findings.detail: Subscriber logs capture the errors and diagnostic messages that occur in Life Sciences Cloud so that you can review them and act on them. The logs give you visibility into problems that your users encounter, whether the problem happens during server-side processing or in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. Go to the Error Log Management tile in the Admin Console to view subscriber logs and control how long the log details are available.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package.

findings.name: What Subscriber Logs Capture
findings.detail: A subscriber log records a single error or diagnostic message along with details that help you investigate it, such as the message text, an error code, the date and time, the user who encountered it, and where in the process the message originated. Each log also has a log level that indicates the severity of the message: Error, Exception, Warn, Info, Debug, or Verbose. Subscriber logs are stored in your org so that you and your users can review them. You control how long they're kept by setting a retention window on the Log Settings page. Because logs accumulate over time, keep the retention window appropriate for how you monitor your org

findings.name: Where Subscriber Logs Come From
findings.detail: Subscriber logs originate in two places, shown by each log's origin type. Logs with an origin type of SFDC are created during server-side processing in your org. Logs with an origin type of Mobile are created in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app and uploaded when the app syncs. For logs that originate on a mobile device, the log also shows the device type—iPhone, iPad, or Android—so that you can isolate issues that your field reps encounter on a specific kind of device. Currently the Life Science Cloud mobile app is only available on iPad.

findings.name: Manage Subscriber Logs from the Admin Console
findings.detail: Use the Logs page to review and filter the logs that your org has recorded. Use the Log Settings page to set the retention window that governs when logs are automatically deleted. Access both pages from the Error Log Management tile in the Admin Console. Users require the Manage Life Sciences Error Logs user permission to view and manage subscriber logs. Users without that permission receive an access error. The permission is part of the Life Sciences Commercial Admin permission set. View and Filter Subscriber Logs Review the errors and diagnostic messages recorded in your org on the Logs page in the Admin Console. Filter the list by criteria such as the log level, date, user, device type, and error source to find the logs that you need. Configure Subscriber Log Retention Control how long Agentforce Life Sciences retains subscriber logs by setting the retention window on the Log Settings page in the Admin Console.

findings.name: View and Filter Subscriber Logs
findings.detail: Review the errors and diagnostic messages recorded in your org on the Logs page in the Admin Console. Filter the list by criteria such as the log level, date, user, device type, and error source to find the logs that you need.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. User Permissions Needed To view and manage subscriber logs: | Life Sciences Commercial Admin permission set, which includes the Manage Life Sciences Error Logs user permission The Logs page shows the subscriber logs recorded in your org as a scrollable list. The list loads in batches and fetches more logs as you scroll, so large log volumes stay responsive. The page is read-only; you can't edit or delete individual logs. Logs are removed automatically based on the retention window that you set on the Log Settings page. From the App Launcher, find and select Admin Console . Go to Error Log Management, and then select Logs . The page shows error logs based on the number of days set in the Keep Logs For (in Days) setting on the Log Settings page. Review the details of each log in the list. Each log shows this information. Log Name —The log's record name. Error Date —When the message was logged. Origin Type —Where the log came from, such as server-side processing or the mobile app. User —A link to the user who encountered the message. If the user can't be identified, the log shows User not found. Error Code —The code associated with the message. Message —The text of the log message. To narrow the list, set one or more filters at the top of the page. You can combine filters. View —Show all logs or only logs of a specific level: Error, Warn, Info, Debug, Exception, or Verbose. The default is Error. Log Name —Match logs by record name. Date range —Show logs from a preset period, such as Today, Yesterday, This Week, or Last Month, or set a custom start and end date. The default is the last month. Device Type —Show logs from all devices or from a specific device type: iPad, iPhone, or Android. Use this filter to isolate logs that originated in the mobile app. User —Show logs for a specific user. Error Source —Show logs from a specific location in the process. To return to the default filters, select Reset . To change how long logs are kept, see Configure Subscriber Log Retention .

findings.name: Provider Bulk Sync
findings.detail: Provider Bulk Sync helps organizations to effectively and efficiently manage their relationships with Healthcare Organizations (HCOs) and Healthcare Providers (HCPs). It allows organizations to integrate HCP and HCO data from IQVIA OneKey directly into the Life Sciences Cloud data model. This process helps organizations get verified HCP data, which helps users have the right information for their customer engagement plans and activities. The verified data can be used for territory planning and other processes.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. Set Up Provider Bulk Sync by Using Built-In MuleSoft Integration Integrate Life Sciences Cloud with IQVIA’s OneKey to import healthcare provider and organization information from an external system into Salesforce Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement. Life Sciences Cloud offers a prebuilt suite of integrations apps, such as the Provider Bulk Sync API and the Onekey System API. These apps are deployed by using MuleSoft Direct to seamlessly integrate with and import healthcare provider information from various external data sources. Create a Copy of Healthcare Provider Address Records by Using Flows and Batch Jobs Regulatory restrictions in certain countries prevent the retrieval of healthcare provider (HCP) addresses via IQVIA OneKey. To ensure data completeness, use Salesforce batch jobs and flows to trigger invocable actions that create copies of address records from the main affiliated healthcare organizations (HCOs) for all corresponding HCP records. The Process Affiliation Address Records invocable action is triggered when a healthcare professional's affiliation status changes, such as joining or leaving a healthcare organization. The Process Contact Point Address Records invocable action is triggered when a healthcare organization's address is added or updated.

findings.name: Set Up Provider Bulk Sync by Using Built-In MuleSoft Integration
findings.detail: Integrate Life Sciences Cloud with IQVIA’s OneKey to import healthcare provider and organization information from an external system into Salesforce Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement. Life Sciences Cloud offers a prebuilt suite of integrations apps, such as the Provider Bulk Sync API and the Onekey System API. These apps are deployed by using MuleSoft Direct to seamlessly integrate with and import healthcare provider information from various external data sources.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. Note Provider Bulk Sync doesn’t integrate with Data 360 by default. To import data to Data 360, you must extend the MuleSoft Connector. Provider Bulk Sync uses Anypoint MQ to process high-volume data. Make sure that you have an active Anypoint MQ license. If you don't have one, ask your Salesforce or MuleSoft account representative to add the Anypoint MQ add-on to your subscription. The Provider Bulk Sync application is a queue-decoupled, API-led MuleSoft solution designed to perform unidirectional data synchronizations of Healthcare Provider (HCP) and Healthcare Organization (HCO) data from IQVIA OneKey into Salesforce Life Sciences Cloud. By leveraging Anypoint MQ, the application ensures resilient, scalable processing for high-volume data. It automatically transforms OneKey objects such as work locations, addresses, affiliations, specialties, and awards, into the native Salesforce schema. This automation provides commercial, medical science liaison (MSL), and field teams with verified account data to support downstream processes like territory planning and customer engagement. System API (Integration & Transformation): Connects directly to IQVIA OneKey to retrieve full or delta provider datasets. It executes batch jobs that map OneKey objects to the Salesforce data model, chunks the resulting payloads, and streams them into Anypoint MQ queues. Process API (Orchestration & Data Load): Consumes payloads from the message queues and handles execution control. It orchestrates job lifecycles via REST endpoints ( /sync, /jobs/{jobId} ), tracks job state and idempotency using IntegrationJobRun records in Salesforce, and performs batch upserts into Salesforce using the Composite and Composite-Graph APIs.

findings.name: Integrate MuleSoft Direct
findings.detail: To address end-to-end business needs, integrate Salesforce apps with external systems by using Integration Solutions with MuleSoft Direct. To set up MuleSoft Direct, see Integrate Solutions with Mulesoft Direct . To set up integration for provider bulk sync, see Explore MuleSoft Direct Integration Apps . Note To deploy MuleSoft apps to CloudHub 2.0 private spaces using MuleSoft Direct, you must enable the Enable Integrations: Private Space permission set. For instructions, see Manage Permission Set Assignments . After the MuleSoft Direct integration is complete, you can sync healthcare provider and organization data. After a sync job is initiated, you can get the status of the sync job and abort the sync job. To ensure your provider data stays up to date, schedule a bulk data synchronization job from Salesforce to automatically pull information from external systems like OneKey regularly. Note If healthcare provider (HCP) address details aren’t synced, it’s likely due to regulatory restrictions in that country. Alternatively, you can use Salesforce Flows and batch jobs that trigger invocable actions. This approach allows you to copy the missing address information directly from the affiliated healthcare organizations (HCOs). See Create a Copy of Healthcare Provider Address Records by Using Flows and Batch Jobs Tip To prevent row-locking errors and record rejections during high-volume initial data loads, temporarily disable triggers, flows, and managed-package handlers on target objects. After the data load completes, re-enable all automations, validate the imported data, and reconcile any processing that was skipped. See Trigger Handler Best Practices during Data Migration .
