findings.name: Create a Copy of Healthcare Provider Address Records by Using Flows and Batch Jobs
findings.detail: Regulatory restrictions in certain countries prevent the retrieval of healthcare provider (HCP) addresses via IQVIA OneKey. To ensure data completeness, use Salesforce batch jobs and flows to trigger invocable actions that create copies of address records from the main affiliated healthcare organizations (HCOs) for all corresponding HCP records. The Process Affiliation Address Records invocable action is triggered when a healthcare professional's affiliation status changes, such as joining or leaving a healthcare organization. The Process Contact Point Address Records invocable action is triggered when a healthcare organization's address is added or updated.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. Process Contact Point Address: This invocable action synchronizes HCP address information with the affiliated HCOs. When an HCO address is created, the action creates a copy of the address for all affiliated HCPs. When an HCO address becomes inactive, the action deactivates the corresponding copied addresses for all affiliated HCPs. Process Affiliation Address: This invocable action ensures HCPs always have accurate address information based on their active affiliations with healthcare organizations (HCOs). When an HCP is affiliated with an HCO, the action copies the HCO addresses and links them to the HCP record. When the affiliation ends, the action deactivates the copied addresses to maintain up-to-date data. To copy HCP address records from affiliated HCOs, create the required batch jobs and Salesforce Flows. The batch job triggers the flow, which in turn invokes the invocable action to create the address records. Create Flows to Trigger Invocable Actions to Copy Addresses Create Salesforce Flows that are used by batch jobs to trigger invocable actions that create a copy of healthcare provider (HCP) address records from the affiliated healthcare organization (HCOs). Create Batch Jobs to Copy Healthcare Provider Addresses Create Batch Management jobs that trigger the necessary flows, which in turn call the invocable actions to create a copy of the Contact Point Addresses and Process Provider Affiliation Addresses. Sequence Address Batch Jobs by Using a Flow To make sure that address synchronization batch jobs run in the correct order, create a flow that automatically initiates the Process Provider Affiliation Addresses batch job only after the Process HCP Contact Point Addresses batch job completes.

title: Quick and Custom Action Management
summary: Quick Actions and Custom Actions are shortcuts that provide fast access to key features in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. These actions are available directly from record pages, the home page, and custom

findings.name: Quick and Custom Action Management
findings.detail: Quick Actions and Custom Actions are shortcuts that provide fast access to key features in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. These actions are available directly from record pages, the home page, and custom components.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. Life Sciences Cloud supports three types of actions: Standard Actions, Quick Actions, and Custom Actions. Configure Quick Actions and Custom Actions in the Admin Console for areas without page layouts, such as the Home page, Calendar, and Search.

findings.name: Action Types
findings.detail: Action Type | Description | Configuration Source Standard Actions | Actions that Life Sciences Cloud ships as part of its package, such as New Visit, Email, Inquiry, and Survey, as well as Salesforce platform actions such as Edit, Delete, and New. On web, they appear in the top-right of the record page. On mobile, they appear in the floating action wheel. | Salesforce page layouts or Lightning Record Pages Quick Actions | Actions designed for areas without standard layouts, such as the Home page, Calendar, and Search. | Admin Console Custom Actions | Actions used for internal or external URLs, external apps, such as Slack or Safari, Utterances, or GoTo Visit deep links. | Admin Console

findings.name: Location-Specific Action Behavior
findings.detail: The actions available depend on where they are in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. Account Search and Advanced Search Pages Account Search uses Quick Actions where the location is Search. The app filters actions by: Profile name and permission sets. These filters apply in all contexts. If both are empty, the action doesn't appear. Record type. This filter applies only when a single account context is available. In the Bulk Select flow, the app doesn't apply record type filtering. Home Page Home page actions use Quick Actions where the location is HomePage , and Custom Actions where the entity type is HomePage . To make the action appear, select a profile or permission set. If both are empty, the action doesn't appear. Supported home page actions: New Visit Inquiry Share Content Email Create Medical Insight Custom Actions (URL, App, Utterance) Record Pages Record page actions use the Account Record Type Layout Actions and Custom Actions. Record pages don't load Quick Actions. Visit Engagement Page Visit Engagement shows the actions configured on the Account object. Visit Engagement doesn't show quick actions, except the Report Compliance Activity action. Supported primary visit actions: Create Medical Insight Custom Actions (URL, App, Utterance) Email Inquiry Last Visit Next Best Customer Report Compliance Activity Schedule Next Visit Survey Visit Attendee Actions support all primary visit actions except Schedule Next Visit. Note Child visits don't show the floating action wheel.

title: Quick Actions
summary: Quick actions provide access to common tasks from areas without page layouts, such as the home page, Calendar, and

findings.name: Quick Actions
findings.detail: Quick actions provide access to common tasks from areas without page layouts, such as the home page, Calendar, and Search.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. Configure quick actions in the Admin Console. You don't need a standard action to configure a quick action. If you add actions to the Quick Actions in the Salesforce Classic Publisher section of the page layout, they appear only in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. If you add actions to the Salesforce Mobile and Lightning Experience Actions section, they appear in both the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app and on the web.

findings.name: Quick Action Locations
findings.detail: Configure quick actions to appear in these locations. Home Page . Actions appear on the mobile app home page. Next Best Customer . Actions show in the Next Best Customer window, under the account details. Calendar . Actions show in the visit preview window. Search . Actions appear in the accounts list after tapping the ellipsis button. Visit . Actions appear on the Visit Engagement page. This page currently supports only the Report Compliance Activity action.

findings.name: Home Page
findings.detail: To configure home page actions in the Admin Console, use quick actions or custom actions because they don't use a page layout. Home page actions don't require a standard action. Supported home page actions: New Visit Inquiry Share Content Email Create Medical Insight (requires turning on InsightCaptureFromAccount in Insight Settings) Custom Actions: URL, App, Utterance Note GoTo Visit Actions aren't supported on the home page. The app fetches the home page quick actions when: Set Location to Home . Set Entity to HomePage . Specify a profile or permission set. Important If both Profiles and Permission Sets are empty, the action doesn't appear on the home page. The app fetches the home page Custom Actions when: Set Location to HomePage . Set Entity Type to HomePage .

findings.name: Visit and Visit Engagement
findings.detail: To add Visit Record Page actions, use the Visit page layout or the Visit Lightning Record Page, depending on whether dynamic actions are turned on. The app gets Visit Engagement actions from the actions configured on the account object. Only a small subset of actions appear on the Visit Engagement page. See Supported Actions on Mobile for the supported actions. To configure quick actions on the Visit Engagement page, set the Location to Visit .

findings.name: How Quick Actions Are Filtered
findings.detail: The app uses these steps to filter quick actions: Gets actions based on the location from which the user opens them. Creates a list of actions by matching the mobile user's Salesforce profile name to the Profiles field. If the Profiles field is empty, the app doesn't return actions for this criteria. Keeps actions where at least one of the user's assigned permission sets matches the Permission Sets field. If the Permission Sets field is empty, the app doesn't return actions for this criteria. Combines the profile and permission set lists using OR logic, and includes the action if there's a match on either list. Removes duplicate actions. The unique key is a combination of Action Name, SObject, and Record Types. The app treats two records with the same action name and object but different record types as distinct. Applies action sorting using the Sort field in ascending order. Note The list view and floating action wheel match the action order on your page layout. If you use dynamic actions, they match the Lightning record page instead. For Quick Actions, the app follows the Sort field in ascending order, so lower numbers appear at the top of the action wheel.

findings.name: Rendering Rules
findings.detail: The rendering rules for Quick Actions differ depending on the location. Location | Rendering Rule Home page and iPad layouts not driven by a Flexipage (such as the calendar's visit preview, the account list view, and Next Best Customer) | A Quick Action isn't required on the page layout. Record Lightning page | For standard quick actions, Quick Action metadata isn't required. When you configure quick actions in the mobile page layout, the app shows the action if its name matches a supported action. Lightning Mobile Runtime (LMR) consideration: The record page shows quick actions configured in the Salesforce page layout. For inline LWC components embedded in record page tabs, define a Quick Action on the object in Object Manager with a Name field that matches the component name. Adding the action to a page layout isn't required.

findings.name: Known Considerations
findings.detail: Duplicate actions : The app filters duplicate quick actions that use the action name and object. If you leave the object field blank on an action, the system treats it as distinct from other actions with the same name, which can result in duplicate actions. Hardcoded action type variants : All actions have multiple hardcoded name variants (for example, Namespace_survey and survey ) to support both namespaced and non-namespaced orgs. Both variants open the same custom component. Inline LWC components on record pages require a matching Quick Action : For an inline LWC component to appear in a record page's tabs on the iPad app, define a Quick Action on the object in Object Manager with a Name field that matches the component name. For example, a component named lscMobileInline_HelloWorld requires a Quick Action with the name lscMobileInline_HelloWorld . Adding the action to a page layout isn't required. This applies to any object where the inline component is deployed and doesn't apply to LWC quick actions or components on the Home Page.

title: Set Up and Manage Quick Actions
summary: Set up Quick Actions in the Admin Console to control which actions appear for specific users and locations in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile

findings.name: Set Up and Manage Quick Actions
findings.detail: Set up Quick Actions in the Admin Console to control which actions appear for specific users and locations in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app.

From the dropdown, select the action. Edit: Change the location, sort order, icon, color, associated object, and record type. Or, update the profiles and permission sets that have access to the action. Activate/Deactivate: Turn the action on or off. View Assignments: See a list of profiles and permission sets assigned to the action. Save your changes.

title: GoTo Actions
summary: GoTo actions take users from a visit record page or list view to a specific section of Visit Engagement to complete tasks without

findings.name: GoTo Actions
findings.detail: GoTo actions take users from a visit record page or list view to a specific section of Visit Engagement to complete tasks without scrolling.

title: Delete Quick and Custom Actions
summary: Remove Quick Actions and Custom Actions to keep only the actions users

findings.name: Delete Quick and Custom Actions
findings.detail: Remove Quick Actions and Custom Actions to keep only the actions users need.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. User Permissions Needed To delete actions: | Life Sciences Commercial Admin From Setup, open Developer Console . In the Query Editor, select Tooling API , and then run the appropriate Salesforce Object Query Language (SOQL) query to fetch the actions you want to delete. For Quick Actions: SELECT Id, IsOrgLevel, DeveloperName, LifeSciConfigCategory.Category FROM LifeSciConfigRecord WHERE LifeSciConfigCategory.Category='QuickAction' AND IsActive = true For Custom Actions: SELECT Id, IsOrgLevel, DeveloperName, LifeSciConfigCategory.Category FROM LifeSciConfigRecord WHERE LifeSciConfigCategory.Category='CustomAction' AND IsActive = true In the query results, select the row you want to delete. Click Delete Row , and then click Yes to confirm. To turn off the action instead, set the Active field to false . Generate a new metadata cache from the Admin Console.

title: Action Labels and Custom Label Mapping
summary: Reference for how the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app retrieves action labels and maps action names to Custom

findings.name: Action Labels and Custom Label Mapping
findings.detail: Reference for how the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app retrieves action labels and maps action names to Custom Labels.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package.

findings.name: Standard Actions (Record Page)
findings.detail: The app gets Standard Action labels directly from the standard action metadata. Override these labels in the Translation Workbench.

findings.name: Configurable Actions
findings.detail: As of Summer '26, the label lookup behavior for Quick Actions and Custom Actions has changed. Action Type | Before Summer '26 | Summer '26 and Later Quick Actions | The app used the Action Name as the Custom Label key (for example, NewVisit ). | The app first looks up a custom label that uses the MasterLabel as the key. If there's no match, the app uses the built-in action name mapping for backward compatibility. If neither produces a match, the app shows the MasterLabel value. Custom Actions | The app used the MasterLabel directly from the Custom Action record. | The app looks up a Custom Label that uses the MasterLabel as the key. If there's no Custom Label, the MasterLabel value stays as-is. There's no action name fallback for Custom Actions (URL, App, Utterance). When the app shows a Custom Action on a record page via a Standard Action counterpart, it uses the Standard Action's translated label instead. Note To translate a Quick Action label on mobile, create a Custom Label in your org whose API name matches the MasterLabel of the Quick Action record. The app picks it up automatically after a metadata sync. The key used on mobile (MasterLabel) differs from the key used on the web (SObject + Action Name), so configure both labels separately.

findings.name: How Quick and Custom Action Labels Are Determined
findings.detail: The label for a Quick or Custom Action depends on whether it appears on mobile or the web. In both cases, create a custom label to control the displayed text. On Mobile The Life Sciences Cloud mobile app determines the label for a Quick or Custom Action in this order. The app first checks whether your org has a custom label whose API Name matches the value in the action's Label field. If a match exists, the custom label's translated value appears. Note To control how an action label appears on mobile, create a custom label whose API Name matches the action's Label. The mobile app picks up the label after the next metadata sync. If no custom label matches, the app checks whether the action's API name corresponds to a standard Life Sciences Cloud action, such as New Visit, Start Remote Session, or Activity Plan Adjustment Request. If a match exists, the app shows the default translated label for that standard action. If neither produces a match, the value entered in the action's Label field is shown as-is. On Web The app reads Quick Action labels on the web from the SObject's Buttons, Links, and Actions configuration. For example, if the SObject is Account and the Quick Action is Inquiry, the label shown is the one configured on the Account object under Buttons, Links, and Actions. To override a Quick Action label translation on the web, use the Translation Workbench's Import Translated Files feature. If the Quick Action doesn't exist on the corresponding object, the web follows the same lookup order described in the On Mobile section.

findings.detail: The app maps action names to custom labels for backward compatibility. This table shows what label text appears for each action in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. Action Name | Custom Label Key | Value activityplanadjustmentrequest | ActivityPlanAdjustmentRequest | Activity Plan Adjustment Request createmedicalinsight | NewInsight | New Insight email | Email | Email inquiry | Inquiry | Inquiry intelligentcontent | IntelligentContent | Intelligent Content lastvisit | LastVisit | Last Visit newvisit | NewVisit | New Visit nextbestcustomer | NextBestCustomer | Next Best Customer reportcomplianceactivity | ReportComplianceActivity | Report Compliance Activity startremotesession | StartRemoteSession | Start Remote Session survey | Survey | Survey viewconsent | ViewConsent | View Consent viewonline | ViewOnline | View Online

title: Troubleshooting Quick and Custom Actions
summary: Reference for diagnosing and resolving common Quick Action and Custom Action issues in Life Sciences

findings.name: Troubleshooting Quick and Custom Actions
findings.detail: Reference for diagnosing and resolving common Quick Action and Custom Action issues in Life Sciences Cloud.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package.

findings.name: Action Appears on the Record Page but Not on the Home Page, Calendar, or Search
findings.detail: The Admin Console controls these locations, not page layouts. Add a Quick Action or Custom Action record with the appropriate Location field set.

findings.name: Configured Actions Don't Appear on an Object
findings.detail: To turn on dynamic actions, from the Admin Console, select Mobile , then select Application Settings , then select Enable Dynamic Actions . If dynamic actions are on, only actions configured on the object's Lightning record page appear. Add actions to the Highlights Panel component on the Lightning record page. If dynamic actions are off, only actions configured in the object's page layouts appear. Generate a new metadata cache after you make configuration changes.

findings.name: Configured Custom Action Doesn't Appear on a Record Page
findings.detail: Custom actions require a corresponding standard action counterpart to appear on record pages. Create a standard action in Salesforce (Buttons, Links, and Actions), and add it to the object's page layout or Lightning record page. Custom actions on custom pages, such as the home page and Next Best Customer, don't require a standard action counterpart.

findings.name: Inline LWC Component Doesn't Appear in Record Page Tabs on iPad
findings.detail: Inline LWC components embedded in record page tabs require a Quick Action defined on the object in Object Manager. The Quick Action's Name field must match the component name exactly. For example, a component named lscMobileInline_HelloWorld requires a Quick Action with the name lscMobileInline_HelloWorld . You don't need to add the action to a page layout. This requirement applies to any object where the component is deployed and doesn't apply to LWC quick actions or components on the Home Page. To resolve this: From Setup, open Object Manager , select your object, click Buttons, Links, and Actions , and click New Action . Set Action Type to Lightning Web Component , select your component, and set the Name field to match the component name exactly (for example, lscMobileInline_HelloWorld ). From the Admin Console, generate a new metadata cache.

findings.name: Configuration Changes Don't Appear in the App
findings.detail: All configuration changes—quick actions, custom actions, and page layouts—require a new metadata cache to take effect. From the Admin Console, select Mobile , select Metadata Cache , and then select Create New Cache .

findings.name: Custom Action Label Fails to Translate
findings.detail: Custom actions that appear on custom pages, such as the home page and Next Best Customer, use the MasterLabel as a custom label key (this behavior is a Summer '26 change). Create a matching custom label to provide a translation. Custom actions that appear on record pages use the standard action's translated label instead. Configure the translation on the standard action counterpart.

findings.name: LWC Action Doesn't Go to the Record Detail After Creation
findings.detail: This behavior is a current limitation of LWC in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. Because the server creates records directly, the app requires a round-trip sync before the record appears.

findings.name: Translate a Quick Action Label for the Salesforce Mobile App
findings.detail: Create or use an existing custom label in your org whose API name matches the MasterLabel of the quick action record. The translated custom label appears automatically after a metadata sync. The key used in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app (MasterLabel) can differ from the key used on the desktop site (SObject + Action Name), so configure both separately.

If you create a Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement workflow, you can also...

findings.name: Related Lists for Life Sciences
findings.detail: Records in Salesforce can include details and links to other related records. The Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement related list offers more customization and filtering options than standard related lists. If you create a Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement workflow, you can also control the actions that users can take on related records based on the parent record’s status, user role, and other business rules. These related lists are supported both online and offline in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. When you add the Customer Engagement related list to a record page, you can: Customize the list’s header, icon, and columns. Filter the records in the list. Populate fields on new records based on the parent record's data. Specify the record types that users can create. findings.name: Workflows for Life Sciences
findings.detail: Life Sciences Customer Engagement workflows automate your business processes and guide users through their tasks with clear steps. Configure the permissions and actions for each step of the workflow based on the users' context and role. Implement custom validations to make sure that users follow business processes, and provide checklists to help users understand how to use the workflow. These workflows are supported both online and offline in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. Life Sciences workflows are purpose-built for life sciences field teams. They offer more granular control over stage-specific permissions, validations, and offline mobile support than Salesforce Flow Orchestrator and Stage Management features. Get Your Org Ready for Life Sciences Workflows Before you create a Life Sciences workflow, complete these steps. Understand Life Sciences Workflows Life Sciences Customer Engagement workflows outline the journey of an object through various stages and help you manage different statuses, actions, and record permissions. Get familiar with these terms, and understand how each part supports the overall workflow configuration. Prepare to Configure a Life Sciences Workflow Life Sciences Customer Engagement workflows are a highly customizable way to streamline work for your field teams. To make sure your workflows function as expected, review these planning steps to avoid gathering information or make decisions during setup. Manage Life Sciences Workflows To streamline your business processes, create tailored Life Sciences Customer Engagement workflows. Merge Variables for Life Sciences Workflow Actions The Life Sciences Update Record and Platform Event workflow actions support merge variables. Merge variables can set default values for target object fields and platform event parameters with data from the record on which a workflow path runs. Select the merge variable that matches the action configuration and the data that you want to use. Considerations for Life Sciences Workflows When you configure a Life Sciences workflow, keep these considerations in mind. Custom Scripts for Life Sciences Custom scripts are programmatic tools for data validation across workflow management and visit management in Life Sciences Customer Engagement. Custom scripts are supported on desktop and both online and offline in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app.

title: Understand Life Sciences Workflows
summary: Life Sciences Customer Engagement workflows outline the journey of an object through various stages and help you manage different statuses, actions, and record permissions. Get familiar with these terms, and understand how each part supports the overall workflow

findings.name: Understand Life Sciences Workflows
findings.detail: Life Sciences Customer Engagement workflows outline the journey of an object through various stages and help you manage different statuses, actions, and record permissions. Get familiar with these terms, and understand how each part supports the overall workflow configuration.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. Review the diagram to learn about the four main components of a Life Sciences workflow. For an example workflow configuration, see Set Up Workflow Actions for Medical Inquiry Management and Set Up the Workflow Stages to Manage Medical Inquiries .

findings.name: Workflow Path
findings.detail: The workflow path is the object’s overall workflow, and the path from one stage in the workflow to the next. An object can have multiple workflow paths configured that vary by record type. Life Sciences workflows show progress in a custom progress bar on the record detail page. They don’t use the standard Path component.

findings.name: Stage Object
findings.detail: The stage object is the object for which you configure a workflow path, for example, Inquiry, Managed Event, or Account. When you create and save a workflow path, stage object records are created automatically. One stage object record is created for each object that has a workflow configured.

findings.name: Workflow Actions
findings.detail: Workflow actions are the actions that users can perform as part of the workflow.

findings.name: Workflow Stage Value
findings.detail: Workflow stage values are the steps in the object’s workflow path. A controlling picklist field determines the stages. For example, if the Status field is the controlling field on a workflow for the Inquiry object, the workflow path often includes stages such as New, Working, Escalated, and Closed.

findings.name: Stage Operation
findings.detail: Stage operations are a grouping of conditions that the record must meet to grant permissions and determine the actions that are available to users. You define stage operations for each stage in the workflow.

findings.name: Stage Operation Conditions
findings.detail: Stage operation conditions are the specific conditions within the stage operation that a record must meet to grant permissions and make actions available to users. If the conditions aren’t met, the permissions and actions aren’t granted. You define stage operation conditions for each stage operation within each stage of the workflow. Note Stage operation conditions that involve UI permission prototype checks don't support custom fields. These checks determine button visibility before a record exists or user input is captured, so they can't evaluate custom field values that a user enters while creating a record.

findings.name: Stage Operation Actions
findings.detail: Stage operation actions are the actions that are available to users when the stage operation is applied to a particular stage in the workflow path. You create workflow actions separately, and then you assign them as stage operation actions for each stage in the workflow's path.

findings.name: Custom Scripts
findings.detail: Custom scripts are Lightning web components that validate user actions or provide checklists to help users understand the tasks to complete.

title: Prepare to Configure a Life Sciences Workflow
summary: Life Sciences Customer Engagement workflows are a highly customizable way to streamline work for your field teams. To make sure your workflows function as expected, review these planning steps to avoid gathering information or make decisions during

findings.name: Prepare to Configure a Life Sciences Workflow
findings.detail: Life Sciences Customer Engagement workflows are a highly customizable way to streamline work for your field teams. To make sure your workflows function as expected, review these planning steps to avoid gathering information or make decisions during setup.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package.

findings.name: Step 1: Outline the Workflow
findings.detail: Identify the business process that you want to automate and break down the workflow into logical steps or stages. For example, a common Inquiry process can include stages such as New, Working, Escalated, and Closed.

findings.name: Step 2: Define Workflow Objects and Permissions
findings.detail: Identify the parent object that you want the workflow to run on, and any related objects. Determine the permissions users need to create, edit, or delete parent or child records at each stage in the object's workflow.

findings.name: Step 3: Identify the Workflow's Controlling Picklist Field
findings.detail: Identify the picklist field on the workflow object that controls the stages in the workflow. The values assigned to this controlling picklist field determine the stages that appear in the workflow builder. If Salesforce manages the picklist values for that field, you can't add new values, which means you can't add new stages to the workflow. Tip We recommend setting the controlling picklist field to read-only on the page layout to prevent users from editing the field directly and bypassing the workflow.

findings.name: Step 4: Identify Fields for Workflow Conditions
findings.detail: Each workflow stage operation includes conditions that must be met so that users can work with records and take actions. Identify the fields on the parent object or related objects that are required to set up these conditions.

findings.name: Step 5: Plan Actions for Each Workflow Stage
findings.detail: Workflow actions can update records, launch a platform event, invoke a Lightning web component, or open a custom URL. Outline the actions that you want to make available to users at each stage in the workflow. This way, you can identify the record fields or other components that the actions use or update.

findings.name: Step 6: Consider Validation Rules and Checklists
findings.detail: Validation rules and checklists help you maintain data integrity and enforce business rules. For validation rules, consider what conditions must be met for a record to move to the next stage in the workflow. For checklists, identify any necessary steps that you want to outline for users so that they know how to move a record to the next stage.

title: Configure Life Sciences Workflow Actions
summary: Before you configure a workflow path, create the actions that users can perform on an object. When you define the workflow path, you can assign these actions at each stage in the

findings.name: Configure Life Sciences Workflow Actions
findings.detail: Before you configure a workflow path, create the actions that users can perform on an object. When you define the workflow path, you can assign these actions at each stage in the workflow.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. User Permissions Needed To create workflow actions: | Life Sciences Commercial Admin permission set You can create four types of workflow actions. Update Record actions edit records in some way, for example, by moving the record to a new status. Platform Event actions trigger real-time processes. For example, a platform event can launch a flow. Platform Event actions aren't available in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. Component actions invoke a Lightning web component. For example, you can open a component that shows a list of available document templates. Salesforce-provided components are supported in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app, but custom components that you create aren't. Custom Actions support custom functionality, such as opening an external URL. You create custom actions from the Quick and Custom Action Administration page in the Admin Console. Actions require the Stage Path entity type and the URL action type. See Quick and Custom Action Management . The Update Record or Platform Event actions also support merge variables to set default field values in the Target Object and Platform Event Parameters sections. See Merge Variables for Life Sciences Workflow Actions . From the App Launcher, find and select Admin Console . Select Workflow Configuration , and then select Workflow Actions . To see and search for available actions, select the tabs for each action type. To create an action, click New , and select the action type that you want to create. Enter the action’s basic information, such as its name, the button label, and the object on which it’s available. For an Update Record action, enter these details. Select the field on this object that the action updates, and enter the field’s default value. In the Target Object section, select an additional object. Add the fields to update, and enter the default field values as plain text or as merge variables. When this action is triggered, a window opens where users can review, update, and save changes to these fields. In the Platform Event Parameters section, select a platform event to publish as part of this action. Add the fields to include, and specify the default values as plain text or as merge variables. The platform event details are sent as parameters to workflows, Apex processes, or other asynchronous processes that are subscribed to this platform event. For a Platform Event action, enter these details. Platform Event actions aren't available in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. In the Target Object section, select an additional object. Add the fields to update, and enter the default field values as plain text or as merge variables. When this action is triggered, a window opens where users can review, update, and save changes to these fields. In the Platform Event Parameters section, select a platform event to publish as part of this action, add the fields to include, and specify the default values as plain text or as merge variables. The platform event details are sent as parameters to workflows, Apex processes, or other asynchronous processes that are subscribed to this platform event. For a Component action, enter these details. Only Salesforce-provided components are supported in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. In the Component Parameters section, enter the name of the Lightning web component to open from this action. To populate field values when the component loads, enter component parameters. For example, for an action that opens a component to capture a signature, add these parameters to set these values when the component loads: "status":"Signed","disclaimerText":"Disclaimer Text" . For a Custom Action, select a custom URL action to open an external link. Save your changes. After you create actions, you can see action details and parameters on the Workflow Actions page. You can also edit, clone, or delete actions.

findings.detail: Custom scripts help you make sure that Life Sciences records meet your business rules. Each time a user performs an action that's part of a Life Sciences workflow, validation scripts run to prevent incorrect actions or alert users about errors. See Create Lightning Web Components and Custom Scripts for Life Sciences . Then, you can deploy the custom scripts from the Admin Console in Life Sciences Customer Engagement. Custom scripts don't have an Active field. How a script becomes active depends on its type. Workflow validation and checklist scripts become active when you assign them to a workflow object. Visit action validation scripts are active when you add them to your org. From the App Launcher, find and select Admin Console . Select Workflow Configuration , and then select Custom Scripts . Select New , and give the script a name. Enter the name of the Lightning web component that you created. Select whether the script is for a checklist, for workflow validation, or for visit action validation. Save your changes. To sync changes to the custom script after you update the Lightning web component, select Refresh . After you configure validation or checklist custom scripts for Life Sciences workflows, assign them to workflow objects to make them active.

findings.name: Merge Variables for Life Sciences Workflow Actions
findings.detail: The Life Sciences Update Record and Platform Event workflow actions support merge variables. Merge variables can set default values for target object fields and platform event parameters with data from the record on which a workflow path runs. Select the merge variable that matches the action configuration and the data that you want to use.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package.

findings.name: How Merge Variables Populate Default Values
findings.detail: The Update Record and Platform Event workflow actions support merge variables for default field values in the Target Object and Platform Event Parameters sections. Merge variables work differently for target objects and platform event parameters. Target Objects: Merge variables prefill fields on the target object when the action opens the window to update the record. Users can review and change the prefilled values before saving. Platform Event Parameters: Merge variables populate the selected platform event fields when an Update Record or Platform Event action publishes the event.

findings.name: Merge Variables for Target Objects
findings.detail: Use these supported merge variables to set default values for fields on target objects. Merge Variable | Description | Example $action.NewValue | Populates the value that the Update Record action assigns to the field that it updates. | If the action changes a status from Planned to Completed, then the value is Completed . $action.OldValue | Populates the value of the field that the Update Record action updates before the action changes it. | If the action changes a status from Planned to Completed, then the value is Planned . $record.FieldName | Populates a value from a field on the current record. | $record.Id populates the current record’s ID. $record.Relationship.FieldName | Populates a value from a record that’s related to the current record. | $record.CreatedBy.Name populates the name of the user who created the record.

findings.name: Merge Variables for Platform Event Parameters
findings.detail: Use these supported merge variables to set default values for platform event parameters. Merge Variable | Description | Example $record | Populates the entire current record as a JSON string. | None $record.FieldName | Populates a value from a field on the current record. | $record.Id populates the current record’s ID.

findings.name: Target Object Considerations
findings.detail: Keep these considerations in mind for merge variables in the Target Object section. You can add only fields that exist on the selected target object. For example, if a workflow path for the account object includes an action that opens a window to update a contact record, reference a field that exists on the contact object. Field and relationship API names are case-sensitive after the variable prefix, but the $record and $action prefixes aren't case-sensitive. Match the capitalization of each API name. For target objects, merge variables support relationships to a single object only. Merge variables don't support polymorphic relationships, which can point to more than one object.

findings.name: Platform Event Parameter Considerations
findings.detail: Keep these considerations in mind for merge variables in the Platform Event Parameters section. You can use only fields that are directly on the current record. Relationship paths aren't supported. If you use a relationship path, Salesforce doesn't populate the field. Map $record to a platform event field that's large enough to contain the entire JSON string, such as a long text area field.

title: Custom Scripts for Life Sciences
summary: Custom scripts are programmatic tools for data validation across workflow management and visit management in Life Sciences Customer Engagement. Custom scripts are supported on desktop and both online and offline in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile

findings.name: Custom Scripts for Life Sciences
findings.detail: Custom scripts are programmatic tools for data validation across workflow management and visit management in Life Sciences Customer Engagement. Custom scripts are supported on desktop and both online and offline in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. Custom scripts run during Life Sciences workflow and visit actions to support more complex business scenarios than standard Salesforce validation rules. Unlike Salesforce validation rules, custom scripts consolidate validation logic and can query any accessible database data, rather than only related records. Custom scripts also offer more dynamic user feedback, providing warnings and custom error messages when users perform actions. You can create these types of custom scripts. Checklist : Use checklist scripts in Life Sciences Customer Engagement workflows. Checklist scripts help users understand all of the steps to take before they can move to the next stage in the workflow. These scripts run when a user clicks the info icon on Record Update actions. Validation : Use validation scripts in Life Sciences Customer Engagement workflows. Validation scripts make sure that business rules are met before users can move a record to the next stage in a workflow. These scripts run when a user runs any workflow action. Visit Action Validation : Visit action validation scripts validate business rules and run when a user saves, signs, or submits a visit. Validations run only for the Save, Submit, and Sign actions. Save validation also runs for child visits and for saves triggered by actions such as starting a remote session. Validations don't run for the Withdraw action. Understand the Format and Output for Life Sciences Custom Scripts Understand the format and output for custom scripts in Life Sciences Customer Engagement. Best Practices for Life Sciences Custom Scripts Follow these best practices when you create custom scripts for Life Sciences Customer Engagement. Test Custom Scripts for Life Sciences Because custom scripts aren’t typical Lightning web components, you can’t test them in the same way. Write custom Jest tests to test the Lightning web components that you create as custom scripts for Life Sciences Customer Engagement. Troubleshoot Custom Scripts for Life Sciences To troubleshoot and debug custom scripts for Life Sciences Customer Engagement, use Chrome Developer Tools. The Console tab shows log information, while the Network tab helps monitor network requests, responses, and performance. Visit Action Validation Scripts Visit action validation scripts help make sure that users follow business rules before saving, signing, or submitting a visit. These scripts run when the user selects the Save, Sign, or Submit action. Life Sciences Custom Scripts Reference Understand the available JavaScript classes, functions, and variables that you can include in a Lightning web component for custom scripts in Life Sciences Customer Engagement.

title: Understand the Format and Output for Life Sciences Custom Scripts
summary: Understand the format and output for custom scripts in Life Sciences Customer

findings.name: Understand the Format and Output for Life Sciences Custom Scripts
findings.detail: Understand the format and output for custom scripts in Life Sciences Customer Engagement.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package.

findings.name: Format
findings.detail: You create custom scripts as headless Lightning web components, meaning that the component includes only the JavaScript file and the metadata configuration file. See Create Lightning Web Components . In the LWC, contain custom script logic in a self-calling function. (() => { // Add custom script logic here. ... })();

findings.name: Output
findings.detail: Custom scripts return an array of JavaScript objects with two defined properties. Property | Type | Details title | String | The message that users see. This can be a custom label name that you can translate to match the current user's language. status | String | The type of message. Statuses are: success: Shows a success message for checklist scripts. Not displayed for validation scripts. warning: Shows a warning message for checklist scripts. For workflow and visit action validation scripts, if there are warnings but not errors, users see all warnings in one window, and they can choose to continue. error: Shows an error message for checklist scripts. Shows an error window for validation scripts. See this example output. return [ { title: "Success Message", status: "success", }, { title: "Success_Message_Custom_Label", status: "success", }, { title: "Warning Message", status: "warning", }, { title: "Warning_Message_Custom_Label", status: "warning", }, { title: "Error Message", status: "error", }, { title: "Error_Message_Custom_Label", status: "error", } ];

findings.name: Custom Scripts Support Custom Labels
findings.detail: Life Sciences Custom Scripts fully supports custom labels. The supported syntax is as follows: With arguments: env.formatCustomLabel('XIsRestrictedForY' '{0} is restricted for {1}' ['Immunexis' accountName]) - supports {0} {1} placeholders. Without arguments: env.formatCustomLabel('PleaseCorrectErrors' 'Please correct errors' []) Simple labels: directly use the label name as the title in return: return { title: 'CustomLabelName' status: 'error' } - the system resolves the label automatically.

title: Best Practices for Life Sciences Custom Scripts
summary: Follow these best practices when you create custom scripts for Life Sciences Customer

findings.name: Best Practices for Life Sciences Custom Scripts
findings.detail: Follow these best practices when you create custom scripts for Life Sciences Customer Engagement.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package.

findings.name: Asynchronous Calls
findings.detail: Database queries are synchronous on the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app but asynchronous on desktop (web). To support asynchronous calls, enclose each validation in an async function. (() => { async function inquiryQuestionsValidation() { try { let inquiryQuestions = await db.query( "InquiryQuestion", await new ConditionBuilder( "InquiryQuestion", new FieldCondition("InquiryId", "=", getRecordId(record)) ).build(), ["Id", "Name"] ); if ( inquiryQuestions === null || inquiryQuestions === undefined || inquiryQuestions.length === 0 ) { return { title: "No Inquiry Questions Found", status: "error", }; } return { title: "Inquiry Questions Added", status: "success", } } catch(error) { return { title: "Caught Exception During Inquiry Questions Validation", status: "error" } } } function getRecordId(record) { let recordId = record.stringValue("Id"); return recordId ? recordId : record.stringValue("uid"); } return [inquiryQuestionsValidation()]; })();

findings.name: Database Queries
findings.detail: To improve performance, always specify fields in database queries. Rather than making multiple WHERE clause queries to the database, filter queries in the JavaScript instead.

findings.name: Error Handling
findings.detail: To make sure that you “catch” JavaScript errors, use a Try-Catch block in all validation functions in custom scripts. Otherwise, when JavaScript errors occur, validation rules don’t show in the UI. If enableAccessErrors() is called before running a function to retrieve field values, the function returns a JavaScript error for the inaccessible field. If an error occurs but a Try-Catch block doesn't catch it: On desktop, users see only a field access error for checklist and validation scripts. On the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app, users see a field access error for checklist scripts, but validation scripts fail.

findings.name: Testing
findings.detail: Because errors can sometimes occur in only one environment, we recommend testing custom scripts on desktop and in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app.

findings.name: Custom Settings
findings.detail: Custom Settings created from Setup aren’t downloaded or evaluated on the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. Therefore: Validation bypass logic using Custom Settings works on the web but fails silently on mobile with no error message. Custom Permissions in validation formulas don't trigger on mobile. Server-side validation rules on the Visit object aren't enforced during iPad record submission. To resolve these issues, enforce all validation and bypass logic with a client-side Visit Validation Script using only data available on-device at run time. For related records, use record.getContextData instead of queries. Field names can be lower case on mobile; therefore, normalize casing in custom scripts.

findings.name: Test Custom Scripts for Life Sciences
findings.detail: Because custom scripts aren’t typical Lightning web components, you can’t test them in the same way. Write custom Jest tests to test the Lightning web components that you create as custom scripts for Life Sciences Customer Engagement.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. See Test Lightning Web Components . Load the script. Read the script's contents from the file system. Create a new function that accepts all necessary parameters for the script and includes the script's content as the final parameter. The parameters that you pass into the function should be mocked versions of the classes and variables that are used in the script. The last parameter should be return , followed by the content of your script file. // Load the script const scriptContent = fs.readFileSync(path.resolve(__dirname, '../inquiryQuestionsValidation.js')); const scriptFunction = new Function('env', 'record', 'db', 'ConditionBuilder', 'FieldCondition', `return ${scriptContent.toString()}`); Mock custom script classes and variables. To create custom script tests, you must create mocked versions of any out-of-the-box classes and variables and pass them in during testing. If you don’t pass in mocked classes and variables, test failures occur. // Mock the classes and variables that are used in the script const mockEnv = { getOption: jest.fn(), }; const mockDb = { query: jest.fn(), }; const mockRecord = { stringValue: jest.fn(), }; const mockConditionBuilder = jest.fn().mockImplementation(() => ({ build: jest.fn().mockResolvedValue({}), })); const mockFieldCondition = jest.fn(); Set up a test using this structure. Mock the data that’s necessary for your test scenario. Invoke your script's function, and provide mocked classes and variables. To make sure that the complete result is available, allow all validation functions to resolve. Verify the results. // Mock the db.query method to return the desired value mockDb.query.mockResolvedValue([{ Id: '1', Name: 'Question 1' }]); // The scriptFunction returns an array containing a Promise const promiseArray = scriptFunction(mockEnv, mockRecord, mockDb, mockConditionBuilder, mockFieldCondition); // Wait for the Promise in the array to resolve const result = await Promise.all(promiseArray); // Assert the result is as expected expect(result).toEqual([{ title: 'Inquiry Questions Added', status: 'success', }]); Example Test Suite for Life Sciences Custom Scripts This example provides a test suite for a custom script in Life Sciences Customer Engagement.

const scriptFunction = new Function('env', 'record', 'db', 'ConditionBuilder', 'FieldCondition', `return ${scriptContent.toString()}`); // Mock the classes and variables that are used in the script const mockEnv = { getOption: jest.fn(), }; const mockDb = { query: jest.fn(), }; const mockRecord = { stringValue: jest.fn(), }; const mockConditionBuilder = jest.fn().mockImplementation(() => ({ build: jest.fn().mockResolvedValue({}), })); const mockFieldCondition = jest.fn();
