findings.name: Start Presentations
findings.detail: Start a presentation for healthcare professionals (HCPs) directly from the content library, from an account, or from a visit. Presentation metrics are saved in presentation click stream entry records. Or, preview content and practice giving presentations without tracking metrics.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package.

findings.name: Start Presentations from the Content Library
findings.detail: In the Intelligent Content tab, search or filter to find the content that you want to present. Tap a presentation to open it and start presenting the content immediately, or preview the content without tracking engagement metrics. During the presentation, add accounts as attendees, and then tap the Visit button to create a visit directly from the presentation player.

findings.name: Start Presentations from an Account
findings.detail: In the Accounts tab, you can open the content library from each account record to preview or start a presentation for that account. The presentations in the content library can vary based on the account. During the presentation, add accounts as attendees, and then tap the Visit button to create a visit directly from the presentation player. If the account has any product restrictions, you don’t see presentations associated with that product. The Recommended filter shows any presentations that are recommended for that account and territory. Changing the account or territory context updates the list of recommended presentations accordingly. The Next Best Message tag indicates the presentations that are most appropriate for the account.

findings.name: Start Presentations from a Visit
findings.detail: Deliver relevant content efficiently during visits with HCPs. On the Visit Engagement page, add presentations to the visit and tap presentation thumbnails to start presentations. From the Presentations section, you can also preview recent presentations without tracking presentation metrics or open the content library to find the presentation you need. Information and warnings about product restrictions and targeted presentations for your territories help you select the right content and add the right accounts to your visit. During or after the presentation, you can return to the Visit Engagement page to see an overview of the presented content, including the page thumbnails and the time spent on each page. You can also see the product messages presented and the reactions that you captured from HCPs.

title: Present Content to Your Customers
summary: Present slides, PDFs, embedded videos, and dynamic content to enhance your interactions with healthcare professionals (HCPs). In the presentation player, leverage engagement tools, capture feedback and survey responses, add participants, and send follow-up emails for more effective HCP...

findings.name: Present Content to Your Customers
findings.detail: Present slides, PDFs, embedded videos, and dynamic content to enhance your interactions with healthcare professionals (HCPs). In the presentation player, leverage engagement tools, capture feedback and survey responses, add participants, and send follow-up emails for more effective HCP interactions. Content tracking offers detailed insights into the content presented and the feedback from HCPs.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. Note The presentation player requires a modern internet browser with access to IndexedDB. IndexedDB is enabled by default on modern browsers but can be limited or disabled by corporate network settings. The options that are available in the presentation player depend on your platform, your admin’s configuration, and your permissions. When you start a presentation, the player opens to the presentation’s first page or to the page where you last left off. In the presentation player window, you can interact with some content on the page depending on your admin’s configuration. For example, play an embedded video, or use links within the slide to go to other pages.

findings.name: Open the Presentation Player Menu
findings.detail: You access the presentation tools from the player menu. To open the presentation player menu, use the arrow icon on the top-left or bottom-left corner of the page. If you don’t see an icon, use one of these gestures to open the menu in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. Swipe down Swipe up Or, use one of these options to open the menu in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app or on the desktop site. Tap or click the top of the page Tap or click the bottom of the page

findings.name: Navigate and Add Presentations
findings.detail: When you open the player menu, the Pages tab shows the thumbnails and page names for each page. Select and add other presentations from the content library in the Presentations, Favorites, and Pages tabs, or by using the Presentations icon on the desktop site. Apply filters to quickly find the presentation you want, or see the presentations that are recommended for that account and territory. If a product is restricted for an account that’s added to the presentation session, you can’t see or select presentations associated with the restricted product.

findings.name: Present Mandatory Pages
findings.detail: Some presentations include mandatory pages. Required pages are denoted with an asterisk, and you must present them to continue the presentation or to create a visit. If you try to close or switch presentations before you share required content, the presentation player shows you a message and highlights mandatory pages.

findings.name: Capture Feedback and Rate Content
findings.detail: To record positive or negative HCP feedback at the page or presentation level, turn on Rate Content. Capturing reactions helps you customize content for future engagements. Depending on your admin’s configuration, you can rate content in these ways. Use the thumbs up and thumbs down icons for each page or presentation in the player menu. You can use these icons to capture feedback without opening the page or the presentation. In the presentation player window, tap or click each page to capture feedback without opening the player menu. To capture positive feedback, tap or click on the top of the page. To capture negative feedback, tap or click on the bottom of the page. A flash on the page indicates that your feedback was captured.

findings.name: Use Drawing Tools and the Laser Pointer
findings.detail: To open the drawing tools menu to highlight or annotate content on the slides, use the paintbrush icon. From the drawing tools menu: Drag the drawing tools menu to another location on the screen. Select the laser pointer to highlight content. Select the pen and the pen color to annotate on the page. Undo or clear what you’ve drawn on the page. Close or open the drawing tools menu. Drawing tools aren’t available when a presentation is locked. When you use drawing tools, you can navigate slides but you can’t interact with the slide content in other ways, such as clicking links or playing embedded videos.

findings.name: Lock Presentations on Your iPad
findings.detail: To lock a presentation when you hand your iPad over to HCPs during a face-to-face visit and prevent them from accessing other parts of the app, use the lock icon. To unlock the presentation, select the Lock button again, and enter your PIN code or use Face ID. Some presentations are locked by default when the presentation starts. When presentations are locked, other options in the player menu aren’t available.

findings.name: Pause Tracking
findings.detail: The pause icon stops tracking metrics for a presentation session during a training session or when you want to preview content without recording an interaction. When tracking is paused, you see a reminder each time you go to a new page or presentation. For some presentations, session tracking is paused by default when the presentation starts. To start or resume tracking metrics, use the play icon. When tracking is paused, in-content interactions captured by the trackInteraction function aren't recorded. For information about the captured metrics, see Presentation Metrics .

findings.name: Add Attendees
findings.detail: To add HCPs as attendees so that you can capture interactions with multiple stakeholders in real time, use the account icon. The first account that you select is the main account, and others are participants. If a product that's associated with the presentation is restricted for an account, you can't add the account as an attendee.

findings.name: Add and Update Visits
findings.detail: To create a visit or to return to the Visit Engagement page during a presentation, use the Visit button. On the Visit Engagement page, you can: Update the visit information View presentation metrics, including the presentations and pages viewed, and the time spent on each page View and update the shared products and messages and capture the HCP’s sentiment Add discussions or next visit objectives Return to the presentation player by using the Return to Presentation link at the top of the page Save changes to the visit Submit the visit You can’t open visits when you preview a presentation.

findings.name: Share Presentations
findings.detail: To send the presentation to the HCP during or after a visit, use the email icon and select an email template. The presentation is added to the email as an attachment or as a link in the email content, and the accounts that are added to the presentation become email recipients. Sharing a presentation as an email attachment is supported only in the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app. You can’t email a custom presentation that contains pages that aren’t approved for email distribution. To share the custom presentation by email, remove any restricted pages. See Customize and Send Emails .

findings.name: Respond to Surveys for Accounts
findings.detail: Capture responses to account-specific surveys on behalf of the HCP. Use the account icon to see attendees, and then from the account's quick actions, select Survey . You can also use the quick action in the presentation player menu to respond to a survey for the main account. If needed, close a survey and resume it later. Responses are saved automatically and associated with the relevant account.

findings.name: Create Medical Inquiries
findings.detail: Create medical inquiries directly from the presentation player. Use the account icon to see attendees, and then from the account's quick actions, select Inquiry . You can also use the quick action in the presentation player menu to start an inquiry for the main account.

findings.name: Capture Reactions to Product Messages
findings.detail: Depending on the presentation HTML file's configuration, capture the HCP’s sentiment and reaction to products messages directly on each presentation page. The reactions that you capture are saved on the related provider visit detailing product message records.

findings.name: Capture Page-Level Survey Responses
findings.detail: Depending on the presentation HTML file's configuration, capture responses to surveys that are embedded in presentation pages.

findings.name: Cancel Presentations
findings.detail: To end the presentation without capturing metrics or saving presentation data to associated visits or accounts, use the Cancel button.

findings.name: End Presentations
findings.detail: To end a presentation, use the Visit button to return to the visit and save it or submit it. Ending the presentation saves presentation metrics and data to associated visits or accounts.

findings.name: See Also
findings.detail: Presentations

title: Manage Events
summary: Event Management gives you a structured, end-to-end workflow to plan, execute, and conclude your field events. From creating an event and planning the logistics, to submitting for approval, an event can encompass multiple phases and

findings.name: Manage Events
findings.detail: Event Management gives you a structured, end-to-end workflow to plan, execute, and conclude your field events. From creating an event and planning the logistics, to submitting for approval, an event can encompass multiple phases and steps.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. Pre-approval planning phase: As the organizer, the planning phase is of utmost importance. The event’s draft phase is the foundation of an event. You determine the subject that will be presented at the event, and then you move on to the complex task of recruiting the attendees. In case of speaker meetings, attendee recruitment involves selecting the right speaker who is trained to deliver a lecture at the event and is also compliant with event rules. Next, you figure out the logistics of when and where the event will take place, and calculate the estimated costs for the event. After all the setup is ready, you submit the draft plan for your manager’s approval. The approval process is customizable as per your org’s requirements. Post-approval planning phase: After your event plan is approved, you start sending out email invites to the attendees, collaborators, experts. Track participants’ responses and finalize the logistical service providers, like vendors and caterers. Execution phase: This is the day of the event. As attendees arrive, capture their attendance by launching the sign-in sheet. Record all types of attendees, including write-ins. Confirm the attendance of the speaker, and update their status to “Attended”. During the event, facilitate the supporting processes by launching presentations. Close-out phase: Conclude the event by launching a survey to provide feedback for the event logistics. Record actual costs to reconcile differences between estimates and actuals. Capture and reconcile write-in and non-profiled attendees with the system records. Pre-Approval Event Planning Plan your managed event by creating the event record, accepting compliance statements, assigning subjects, and adding attendees. Select the location where the event will be hosted and calculate event expenditure by adding estimated expenses. Submit the plan for approval as per your organization’s rules. After the approval comes through, send out the email invites and monitor responses. Post-Approval Tasks After your manager approves your plan, add the estimated expense for the event and finalize the logistics provider. Then, send out invites to attendees. Monitor their responses and update their record statuses accordingly. Event Execution Launch the electronic sign-in sheet on the day of the event to capture attendee signatures and meal preferences. Post-Event Tasks After the event has concluded, it’s time to complete the close-out tasks. Record the actual expenses incurred during the event, and allocate the expenses to the participants. Enter the details of the attendees who don’t have an existing record in the system. Finally, launch a survey to provide your feedback for the event. Mobile and Offline Event Execution Event Management supports mobile and offline execution from within the mobile app, helping field representatives manage sign-in, participants, presentations, and surveys even when connectivity is unavailable.

Add Event Participants Add the participants of a managed event, including regular attendees, colleagues and coorganizers, experts who are trained on the event topic, and ad hoc participants.

title: Set Up an Event
summary: Draft an event plan, along with its associated records, such as compliance requirements, subject assignment rules, and event

findings.name: Set Up an Event
findings.detail: Draft an event plan, along with its associated records, such as compliance requirements, subject assignment rules, and event resources.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. User Permissions Needed To create an event, accept compliance statements, and assign a subject: | Life Sciences Field Sales Representative permission set AND Life Sciences Core permission set

findings.name: Create a Managed Event
findings.detail: Create a managed event from the Managed Events tab or directly from your calendar. When users create the managed event, the compliance statements get added to the event automatically. Only the organizer and coordinator of an event can select the compliance statements added to the event. Create a managed event. From the iPad's homepage, go to the Managed Event tab in the top scroll bar, and tap New . Select a record type. Enter the event name. The Managed Event Type field is automatically populated in the backend, based on the record type-event type mappings configured by your admin. See Configure Event Type-Record Type Mappings . Select a managed event type, such as a speaker event. Add the start and end dates of the event. Select the managed event status, such as, Draft. Select yourself as the primary owner. If your admin selects Include manager as event approver in the org-wide Admin Console settings, your manager is automatically added as the approver of the event. If the setting is turned off, your manager is added as the coordinator for the event. Save your changes. Alternatively, create managed events from the calendar. Make sure that the event is within the business hours of the organization. From the homepage of your mobile device, go to the Planner tab in the top scroll bar. In the top-right corner of the calendar, click , and then select Managed Events . Alternatively, tap a time slot in the calendar to create the event. Enter a name for the event. Select a managed event type. Select the start and end times for the event. The start and end times are preselected for you if you’re creating the event from the calendar timeslot. This setting calculates the event end time based on the value defined in the Default Managed Event Duration in Minutes field in the profile-level Admin Console settings. Select a status. Save your changes.

findings.name: Accept Compliance Statements
findings.detail: Review and accept the compliance statements added to your event before proceeding. Note Only the organizer or coordinator can accept the compliance statements. From the Managed Event tab in your iPad, select the record for which you want to acknowledge the compliance statements. In the Compliance Statements section, select the checkboxes that require your acknowledgment.

findings.name: Assign a Subject to the Event
findings.detail: You can search for and filter the Subject records by using specific Subject fields, defined by your admin in the Admin Console. The product gets auto-assigned based on the subjects or topics assigned to an event. On your iPad, go to the Related tab of the Managed Event record for which you want to add a subject. In the Subject Assignment section, tap New . Enter a name for the record. The Assignment field is automatically populated with the managed event's name. For Subject, in the search bar, enter keywords for the subject you want to assign to an event. To refine your search, tap Advanced Search . To filter the search results, tap Filters . Select the field and the corresponding value that you want to filter the results with. For example, in Field, select Compliance Type. In Operator, select In. In Value, select Speaker Bureau. This configuration filters the Subject records to show only the records whose compliance type is Speaker Bureau. Tap Save . Tap the record you want to assign as the event’s subject. Save your changes.

findings.name: Create a Managed Event Resource
findings.detail: Capture information about the primary choice for a logistics provider, such as a venue, technical equipment, catering services, and supplies needed for the event. Only resource types that represent the venue and the healthcare (HCO) require location and address information. For resource types like catering services or refreshments, adding location and address information is optional. The first time a venue or HCO resource is confirmed, the location is stamped onto the Managed Event record. On your iPad, go to the Logistics tab of the Managed Event record for which you want to add a resource. In the Managed Event Resources section, tap New . Add a name for the event resource. Select a resource type, such as venue or HCO. To add a venue, do the following steps in the Location and Address section. In the Selected Location field, tap to select a record for the Account object. In the Selected Address field, tap to select a record for the Address object. Alternatively, to add an HCO resource type, do the following steps in the Location and Address section. In the Selected Location field, tap the dropdown to select Location , and then select a corresponding Location record. In the Selected Address field, tap the dropdown to select Contact Point Address , and then select a corresponding Contact Point Address record. Save your changes.

findings.name: Create a Managed Event Resource Preference
findings.detail: Provide users with the flexibility to choose from a variety of resource options. Configure managed event resource preferences to present options to the user. Associate the managed event resource preference with the parent managed event resource to indicate which resource type the options are for. On your iPad, from the Logistics tab of the Managed Event record, tap the Managed Event Resource record. Go to the Managed Event Resource record's Related tab. In the Managed Event Resource Preference section, tap New . Add a name for the resource preference. If needed, add the rank of preference. In Requested Resource, select the ID of the related resource. To add a venue, do the following steps in the Location and Address section. In the Selected Location field, tap to select a record for the Account object. In the Selected Address field, tap to select a record for the Address object. Alternatively, to add an HCO resource type, do the following steps in the Location and Address section. In the Selected Location field, tap the dropdown to select Location , and then select a corresponding Location record. In the Selected Address field, tap the dropdown to select Contact Point Address , and then select a corresponding Contact Point Address record. Save your changes.

summary: Add the participants of a managed event, including regular attendees, colleagues and coorganizers, experts who are trained on the event topic, and ad hoc

findings.name: Add Event Participants
findings.detail: Add the participants of a managed event, including regular attendees, colleagues and coorganizers, experts who are trained on the event topic, and ad hoc participants.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. User Permissions Needed To add attendees, colleagues, and experts: | Life Sciences Field Sales Representative permission set AND Life Sciences Core permission set

findings.name: Considerations for Attendee Search
findings.detail: In the New Attendees window, Event Management searches for attendees to add to an event in the following ways. Aligned accounts list: By default, the system searches for accounts aligned to your territory. You can see all the available attendee options in the Aligned Accounts list. You can switch to a list you created to see accounts that fulfill a specific criteria, or filter the search by healthcare professional (HCP), healthcare organization (HCO), or all. Your admin can turn on lists and filters by selecting the Enable lists and filters in the New Attendee modal checkbox in the Event Management profile-level settings. Use specific fields to filter the search by. Your admin enables this setting by creating a field set and configuring the same in the New Attendees Search Field Set in the Admin Console. View specific fields in the columns of the search results. Your admin enables this setting by creating a field set and configuring the same in the New Attendees Display Field Set in the Admin Console. Use the Add All button to invite all the attendees in the search results. Your admin configures this button’s visibility by selecting the Show the Add All button in the New Attendees modal checkbox in the Event Management profile-level settings. Quickly find an HCP from a specific HCO. In the search results, if an HCO has any affiliated HCPs, the search result is indicated with a symbol. This function makes it easier to select an attendee who’s affiliated with an HCO. Your admin configures this setting using the Show HCP-HCO affiliation for attendees field in the Admin Console. Use the Search Before Create function before creating an account to add as an attendee. Your admin configures this setting by selecting the Enable Advanced Search to find accounts to invite checkbox in the Event Management profile-level settings.

findings.name: Add an Attendee Type Participant
findings.detail: Search for healthcare professionals and healthcare organizations to add to an event. From the iPad's homepage, go to the Managed Event tab in the top scroll bar, and select the record for which you want to add an attendee. Go to the Attendees tab of the Managed Event record. Flick to scroll to the section that represents attendees, and tap New . Select a list or filter to search for attendees. Alternatively, use Advanced Search to search for an account before creating and adding it. Tap Invite next to an account that you want to add to an event. If needed, click Add All to add all the accounts in the search results in bulk. Save your changes. The attendee is added to the attendee related list. Note You can upload consent documents only from the Web. To add consent documents, click next to the attendee record, and tap Upload Consent Documents . In the consent window, select the consent type for which you’re uploading the consent document. Tap Next . Select a file to upload. Save your changes.

findings.name: Considerations for Colleague Search
findings.detail: In the New Colleagues window, Event Management searches for colleagues to add to an event in the following ways. Use specific fields to filter the search by. Your admin enables this setting by creating a field set and configuring the same in the New Colleagues Search Field Set in the Admin Console. View specific fields in the columns of the search results. Your admin enables this setting by creating a field set and configuring the same in the New Colleagues Display Field Set in the Admin Console. The New Colleagues window uses system-generated filters to only display colleagues whose preferred country matches the current user’s preferred country. However, the system-generated preferred-country filter only works if the following conditions are met. Advanced Search is enabled. Your admin configures preferred country picklist values for User Additional Info’s Preferred Country field. Your admin can remove the filter by unselecting the Toggle the system-generated Preferred Country filter field in the Admin Console.

findings.name: Add a Colleague to an Event
findings.detail: Choose a user to add as a colleague to an event. The user details must be defined in a User Additional Info record. After you select a user, you choose the event management participant type role mapping between colleague participant types and participant roles of any kind. In the New Colleagues window, the mapping options show the custom picklist values for the participant types and roles. Note After you select an organizer-type colleague, you can’t edit or remove the record. On your iPad, from the Attendees tab of the Managed Event record, flick to scroll to the section that represents colleagues. Tap New . The New Colleagues window shows all the managed event participants of type User. Select a user to add them as a colleague. This action shows all the event management participant type role mappings values where the type is colleague, while the role can be of any type. Save your changes.

findings.name: Considerations for Expert Search
findings.detail: Before you add experts to a managed event, make sure that your admin has set up the expert search field sets and configurations in the Admin Console. Also make sure that your org has an Event Management participant type with the Expert standard type, a participant role with the Expert standard role, and a mapping record between the two. Your admin must also create Expert records, Subject records, and Expert Subject records, with event dates falling within the Expert Subject record’s start and end dates.

findings.name: Expert Eligibility
findings.detail: When you search for experts to add to an event, the system may run eligibility checks depending on your org’s configuration. Eligibility checks are active when the event is assigned a subject with the compliance type as Speaker Bureau and you have field-level access to the Compliance Type field on the Subject object. When eligibility checks are active: The search results show only experts who are trained on the subject associated with the event. The system verifies that the expert has completed the required training for the subject. The Add Experts via Advanced Search button is not available.

findings.name: Account Search for Experts
findings.detail: When eligibility checks aren’t active, you can use the Add Experts via Advanced Search button to search through person accounts aligned to your territory and add an associated expert.

findings.name: Account Access
findings.detail: The system checks whether you have record-level access to the account linked to an expert before adding the expert to the event.

findings.name: Compliance Checks for Experts
findings.detail: The system checks whether an expert has recently attended another event on the same subject within a defined period. Depending on how your admin has configured the compliance settings: Block — the expert cannot be added to the event. Warn — the expert is added, but you see a warning. This applies both when adding experts during event planning and when adding them to an event that’s already in progress. The system also checks whether the expert’s linked account has an active product restriction for any product associated with the event. If a restriction exists and override is not enabled, the expert cannot be added to the event.

findings.name: Add an Expert Type Participant
findings.detail: Add a speaker or an expert to an event. On the iPad, from the Managed Event record, go to the Attendees tab. Flick to scroll to the section that represents experts. In the Expert section, tap New . In the search results, tap Invite next to the account you want to add as an expert. Save your changes.

findings.name: Add an Expert via Account Search
findings.detail: When the expert eligibility search criteria are not met, you can add experts by first running an account search. The search shows the person accounts aligned to your territory. The expert eligibility search criteria is not met when you lose field-level access to Subject’s Compliance Type field or if the event doesn’t have a subject assignment where the subject’s compliance type is Speaker Bureau. On the mobile, from the Managed Event record, go to the Attendees tab. Flick to scroll to the section that represents experts, and tap New . In the New Experts window, tap Add Experts Via Account Search . In the search results, select the account you want to add as an expert. This action creates an Expert record and a Managed Event Participant record for the managed event you want to add the expert to. The system assigns the Nominated status to the Expert record, and also selects the Speaker checkbox in the Healthcare Provider record. If the Healthcare Provider record has a parent organization account, the record is added as the primary organization in the Expert record. Save your changes. After adding the attendees, from the workflow path on the Managed Event record, submit the record for approval.

title: Post-Approval Tasks
summary: After your manager approves your plan, add the estimated expense for the event and finalize the logistics provider. Then, send out invites to attendees. Monitor their responses and update their record statuses

findings.name: Post-Approval Tasks
findings.detail: After your manager approves your plan, add the estimated expense for the event and finalize the logistics provider. Then, send out invites to attendees. Monitor their responses and update their record statuses accordingly.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. User Permissions Needed To add event location, estimated expenses, and send an email: | Life Sciences Field Sales Representative permission set AND Life Sciences Core permission set

findings.name: Finalize the Event Location
findings.detail: Confirm the event resources before sending out email invites. After the resource is confirmed, the event location is automatically updated in the Managed Event’s Event Location Address field. Note At the first instance when the status of the Managed Event Resource record or Managed Event Resource Preference record is changed to Confirmed, the system stamps the resource’s SelectedLocationId and SelectedAddressId onto the parent Managed Event record’s EventLocationId and EventLocationAddressId fields. From the iPad's homepage, go to the Managed Event tab in the top scroll bar. Select the Managed Event record for which you want to finalize the location. Go to the Logistics tab's Managed Event Resources section. Tap next to the record of your choice, and then click Edit . In Status, select the value that represents that the resource is confirmed. Alternatively, confirm a resource preference. Select the Managed Event Resource record that's associated with the Managed Event record. Go to the Related tab's Managed Event Resource Preference section. To select a Managed Event Resource Preference record for an event, edit the record and change its status to Confirmed. Save your changes.

findings.name: Send Emails to Participants
findings.detail: Invite participants to attend the event by sending out email invites. On the iPad, go to the Managed Event record. From the event workflow path, tap Actions , and then tap Email Participants . In the Send Email window, select a template to send to the event participants. To check the email you want to send, tap Preview Email . Tap Next . Select an attachment, and tap Next . Verify the mail body and tap Next . Verify the email in preview mode, and tap Next . Review the list of recipients and their email addresses. For participants whose email addresses aren’t added or aren't updated, in the email field for the recipient, enter the email addresses. Tap Send .

findings.name: Add Estimated Expenses
findings.detail: Help your organization monitor their financial planning and budgeting processes by capturing the estimated costs of an event. In the advanced search mode, you can use system-generated filters or create filters of your choice. The filter is turned on by default and shows only the expense types that match the event’s type and subtype at the time of expense search. If system-generated filters are enabled, the Add Expense Type window shows only those expense types that have no start and end dates configured, or those that have start and end dates that overlap with the event’s dates. Deselect the system-generated filter to see all expense types. You can search for and filter the Expense records by using specific fields, defined in the Admin Console configurations. The Expense list view shows the estimated costs for each expense category at the top level, while the actual expense appears as a dropdown. The total actual expense rolls up to the top row of the expense category, next to the estimated expense. If you add an actual expense without an associated estimate, the system adds a line item with its own parent expense category. The total cost of all the expenses is shown at the bottom row. If an expense item is added in another currency, the list shows the actual currency ISO for the actual estimate, but the system converts it to USD in the estimated expense row and in the total cost. Turn on the advanced currency code that uses historic transaction rates for accurate results. Add estimated expenses for an event. On the iPad, go to the Managed Event record for which you want to add the estimated expenses, and navigate to its Expenses tab. Tap Add Estimated Expenses . In Expense Type, select the parent estimated expense type created by your admin. For more information, see Expense Management . Select a category for the expense type you want to add. Enter a name for the expense. Add the expense amount. Save your changes.

findings.name: Allocate Estimated Expenses to Participants
findings.detail: Distribute the estimated expenses evenly or unevenly among the event participants. This action creates Estimated Expense Participant Allocation records, which are child records of the parent Estimated Expense record. On the iPad, go to the Managed Event record for which you want to allocate the estimated expenses, and navigate to its Expenses tab. Next to the estimated expense you want to allocate to participants, tap , and then tap Allocate . To distribute the estimated expense amount uniformly among the event participants, follow these steps. In the Allocate Estimated Expense window, select the participants you want to allocate the expenses to Save your changes. Alternatively, to allocate different expense amounts to the event participants, do these steps. . In the Allocate Estimated Expense window, turn on Uneven Allocation. Select the participants you want to allocate the amount to. Manually enter the expense amount against each participant. Save your changes.

title: Event Execution
summary: Launch the electronic sign-in sheet on the day of the event to capture attendee signatures and meal

findings.name: Event Execution
findings.detail: Launch the electronic sign-in sheet on the day of the event to capture attendee signatures and meal preferences.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. User Permissions Needed To capture attendance, add write-in attendees, and launch a presentation: | Life Sciences Field Sales Representative permission set AND Life Sciences Core permission set

findings.name: Manage Event Attendance
findings.detail: On the day of the event, capture participant sign-in information and meal preferences, if any. The sign-in sheet is available only on the iPad. Meal preferences denote transfer of value, and must be recorded for compliance purposes. From the iPad's homepage, go to the Managed Event tab in the top scroll bar, and select the event for which you want to record the attendance. On the bottom-right corner of the page, tap , and tap Sign In Sheet . Tap Sign In next to an attendee and capture their signature. Select the meal preference. Save your changes.

findings.name: Add Write-In Attendees
findings.detail: Capture attendance details for ad hoc participants in an event. For example, if a provider brings a colleague or a spouse to the event who wasn’t invited, create write-in type participant records that are automatically converted to an account or a non-profiled attendee, based on record type and reconciliation status. As a prerequisite, record ad hoc attendees who don’t have an account in Salesforce by creating a Party Profile record. Conversion to Attendee Records If the attendee has an account in the system, the write-in attendee is reconciled with the account and converted into an attendee. If the attendee doesn’t have an account in the system, the write-in attendee is converted into a non-profiled attendee. For information on how write-ins are converted to accounts and non-profiled attendees, see Write-In Participants . On the iPad, from the Managed Event record, go to the Attendee tab. Flick to scroll to the section that represents write-ins, and tap New . The managed event type, participant role, and participant type are preselected. Keep them as is. Enter a name for the write-in. In Participant, tap to add a write-in participant. If the participant has an account associated with it, select Account and then select the record. Use Advanced Search, if needed. If the participant isn’t linked to an account or contact in Salesforce, select PartyProfile, and then select the corresponding record. Flick to scroll to the Participant Party Reconciliation Status field, and select a value, such as, Completed Profiled. For a participant that has an account, choose Completed Profiled. For a participant that isn't linked to an account or contact in Salesforce, choose Completed Non-Profiled. Save your changes.

findings.name: Launch a Managed Event Presentation
findings.detail: Launch the presentation for the speaker by using the approved slide assigned to the topic. The presentations are filtered by the topic or subject aligned with the event and the user’s territory. On the iPad, go to the Managed Event record for which you want to launch a presentation, and navigate to its Presentation tab. In the Recommended section, view the list of recommended presentations that are related to the event’s subject. To preview individual presentations, tap next to the recommended presentation. In the Intelligent Content Player, the Recommended section’s preview function shows all the recommended presentations. Tap next to the presentation that you want to add to the event. The presentation is added to the Selected section. In the Selected section, do the following steps. Tap Preview to see the presentation. In the Intelligent Content Player, the Selected section’s preview function shows only the selected presentation and its pages. To remove the selected presentation, tap next to the presentation in the Selected section, or tap next to the presentation in the Recommended section.

findings.name: Post-Event Tasks
findings.detail: After the event has concluded, it’s time to complete the close-out tasks. Record the actual expenses incurred during the event, and allocate the expenses to the participants. Enter the details of the attendees who don’t have an existing record in the system. Finally, launch a survey to provide your feedback for the event.

findings.name: Allocate Actual Expenses
findings.detail: Capture the actual costs that are incurred for the event. Allocate actual costs, such as food and beverage expenses, audiovisual fees, speaker fees, and venue fees. For compliance purposes, each transfer of value, such as a meal, must be recorded in the event’s costs. Allocate costs equally or partially, as needed.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. User Permissions Needed To allocate expenses, add non-profiled attendees, and launch a survey: | Life Sciences Field Sales Representative permission set AND Life Sciences Core permission set

findings.name: Add Actual Expenses
findings.detail: Record the actual costs incurred during a managed event's execution. Go to the Expenses tab of the managed event whose actual expense you’re adding. Tap Add Actual Expenses . Select the expense item that you want to add the actual expenses for. In the New Actual Expense window, make the following changes. Add the expense amount. In Related Expense type, select the child actual expense type created by your admin. The related expense type field groups an actual expense with an estimated expense via the referenced expense type's Parent Expense Type field. If an actual expense is associated with an expense type that has no parent (that is, if the referenced expense type's Parent Expense Type field is left blank), the actual expense appears in its own category and is not mapped to an estimated expense. For more information, see Expense Management . Enter the transaction date. Save your changes. The actual expense shows up against the estimated expense amount that was added for the expense item.

findings.name: Add Receipts
findings.detail: Attach notes and receipts to substantiate the incurred costs. In the Expense tab, go to the expense item for which you want to attach a receipt. Tap , and then select Notes & Attachments . Select an attachment to add to the expense. Tap Add. The receipt is added to the Files related list of the Expense record.

findings.name: Allocate Actual Expenses
findings.detail: To record the real costs incurred per participant, distribute the actual expense across attendees, by either splitting the amount equally or assigning uneven amounts per participant. On the Web, the Uneven Allocation toggle is in the Allocate Expense window. On the mobile, the option to allocate unevenly is in the Actual Expense window. In the Expense tab, go to the expense item for which you want to allocate expenses. Tap , and then select Allocate . In the Allocate Expense window, select participants to allocate the expense to. To make partial allocations, turn on Uneven Allocation and allocate each amount as needed. The total expense amount is distributed based on the expense type's allocation type. If the allocation type is Group Allocation or Multiple Allocation, the amount is distributed evenly across the number of participants selected. If the allocation type is Individual Allocation, you can select only one participant to allocate the amount to. Save your changes.

findings.name: Add Non-Profiled Attendees
findings.detail: Capture details for ad hoc participants who have no record in the system.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: User Permissions Needed To add non-profiled attendees: | Life Sciences Field Sales Representative permission set AND Life Sciences Core permission set As a prerequisite, make sure that you create a Party Profile record for write-ins who don’t have an account in Salesforce. On the iPad, go to the Managed Event record for which you want to add the non-profiled attendee, and navigate to its Attendees tab. In the section that represents non-profiled attendees, tap New . The managed event type, participant role, and participant type are preselected. Keep them as is. Enter a name for the non-profiled attendee. In Participant, tap to select the Party Profile object, and then select the corresponding record. Save your changes.

findings.detail: Provide feedback for the event by launching a survey.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: User Permissions Needed To launch a survey: | Life Sciences Field Sales Representative permission set AND Life Sciences Core permission set On the iPad, go to the Managed Event record for which you want to launch the survey. From the event workflow path, tap Actions , and then tap Launch Survey . Select the survey that you want to take. Fill out the details as needed. Tap Finish .

title: Mobile and Offline Event Execution
summary: Event Management supports mobile and offline execution from within the mobile app, helping field representatives manage sign-in, participants, presentations, and surveys even when connectivity is

findings.name: Mobile and Offline Event Execution
findings.detail: Event Management supports mobile and offline execution from within the mobile app, helping field representatives manage sign-in, participants, presentations, and surveys even when connectivity is unavailable.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. Event Management supports full mobile and offline execution through the Life Sciences Cloud mobile app, allowing field representatives to manage core event activities, such as attendee sign-ins, write-in additions, presentations, and survey launches, even without a network connection. Actions performed offline are queued locally and synced to Salesforce when connectivity is restored. But, because validations such as attendee quota checks, monetary cap enforcement, and expert eligibility checks require a server connection, any violations detected at sync time result in a Managed Event Participant Discrepancy record rather than a real-time block, and the organizer or admin must resolve these manually. Write-in attendees added offline are reconciled with existing account records after sync and converted to non-profiled attendees if no match is found. Certain actions — including actual expense allocation, workflow stage transitions, email invitations, and calendar event creation — require connectivity and can’t be performed in offline mode.

summary: Review Salesforce Platform best practices gathered by Salesforce from partners, clients, and professional services. Adopt these insights for your own

findings.name: Salesforce Platform Best Practices for Life Sciences Cloud
findings.detail: Review Salesforce Platform best practices gathered by Salesforce from partners, clients, and professional services. Adopt these insights for your own implementation.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package.

findings.name: API Best Practices
findings.detail: No apex triggers or workflows on firing of APEX REST Reads/Inserts. Operation choice (Insert (fastest) -> Update -> Upsert). Record sizes matter (3 MB limit). Optimize sharing (Use less sharing models). To learn more, see API Best Practices and Use Cases .

findings.name: Indexes
findings.detail: To make queries faster, ensure there are proper indexes and external IDs for fields that are in the 'where' clause. Indexes must be below these thresholds to be useful: Custom Indexes: Lower of (10% of 1M + 5% over 1M) or 333,333. Standard Indexes: Lower of (30% of 1M + 15% over 1M) or 1M. Indexes modified by “AND” and “OR": AND – Below 20% of total records or 666K for custom index. OR – Below 10% of total records or 333K in summation of all indexes. Predicates that won’t use indexes: Not equal to (i.e. “!=“). NOT (i.e. NOT IN). To learn more, see Indexes .

findings.name: Page Layout Section Header Translations
findings.detail: You cannot custom translate standard section headers. The Salesforce Platform automatically translates them based on the user's language settings. They are not configurable via the Translation Workbench. If you want custom translation, hide the standard section header and create a new custom section header. You can translate this custom section header using Translation Workbench. Avoid using standard sections in the layouts. Always use custom sections.

findings.name: Reports
findings.detail: Use report filters Pre-aggregate data De-normalize data Use a data warehouse To learn more, see Reporting .

findings.name: Sharing Best Practices
findings.detail: Avoid over protection. Follow a pattern of least-privilege. Don't nest groups deeply. To learn more, see Best Practices for Optimizing Sharing Performance .

findings.name: Skinny Tables
findings.detail: Salesforce can create skinny tables to contain frequently used fields and to avoid joins. This can improve the performance of certain read-only operations. Skinny tables are kept in sync with their source tables when the source tables are modified. If you want to use skinny tables, contact Salesforce Customer Support. Advantages of skinny tables include: Better Cache Utilization Reduced Joins Invisible to End users Supported in reports, list views and SOQL queries To learn more, see Skinny Tables .

findings.name: Web Browser Considerations
findings.detail: Use separate browser contexts when you access different Salesforce environments such as sandboxes or multiple production instances. Otherwise, cookies and session info can get mixed up and cause problems such as corruption issues with the organization and Life Sciences Cloud functionality. Examples of separate browser contexts include using different Chrome users/people, Firefox profiles, or browser extensions that create separate contexts. All incognito/private browser windows share a common set of cookies. You can use an incognito/private window to separate from an org logged into a non-incognito/private window. However, it may cross cookies when using multiple incognito/private windows for multiple org logins.

findings.name: Field Types
findings.detail: There are two types of fields on an object: Salesforce standard fields are delivered by Salesforce.com Customer custom fields are created for the customer implementation.

findings.name: API Naming Convention
findings.detail: Always implement the API naming convention agreed upon at the start of the project. The convention depends on the strategy chosen by the system architect. Keep it universal by adding the organization’s prefix or suffix to differentiate between Salesforce custom fields and customer-built custom fields. Examples: OneEducation_<client name>__c License_<client name>__c In the description section, identify the: Group that requested the field ISO codes of the countries Business Units Integrations using the field

findings.name: Organize Fields
findings.detail: Organize your fields by prefixing any unused custom field labels with “dep_[fieldname] (Dep for 'Deprecated') Examples: dep_fax dep_website Salesforce sorts the fields by label name. Prefixing them moves them to the bottom of the list and out of your way. This makes it easier for you to manage the environment.

findings.name: Field Limitations
findings.detail: Understand the field limitations per object: The number of custom fields allowed per object varies according to your Salesforce edition. The Unlimited edition allows a maximum of 800 custom fields. To learn more, see Custom Fields Allowed Per Object . You can designate up to 25 External ID fields per object. To learn more, see Maximum number of External Ids per object or entity . 25 roll-up summary fields are allowed. To learn more, see Increase the maximum limit of a roll-up summary field . Two master-detail and 40 relationship fields (master-detail plus lookup) are allowed per object To learn more, see Increase the maximum relationships allowed per object .

title: Profile and Page Layout Best Practices for Life Sciences
summary: Agentforce Life Sciences provides standard security profiles such as the Salesforce admin and the Standard User profiles as a template to customize security profiles for your

findings.name: Profile and Page Layout Best Practices for Life Sciences
findings.detail: Agentforce Life Sciences provides standard security profiles such as the Salesforce admin and the Standard User profiles as a template to customize security profiles for your organization.

findings.name: Required Editions
findings.detail: Available in: Lightning Experience Available in: Enterprise and Unlimited Editions with Life Sciences Cloud, Life Sciences Cloud for Customer Engagement Add-on license, and the Life Sciences Customer Engagement managed package. Here are the recommended security best practices for profiles and page layouts. Use Field Level Security rather than page layouts to hide fields from users. Field-level security is a safer method for restricting accessibility to data due to compliance regulations. This also helps minimize the number of page layouts. Page layouts prevent a user from seeing fields but does not prevent them from seeing fields in Salesforce reports. Only field level security completely prevents access to fields. Always use the least possible number of profiles. Minimizing the number of profiles reduces the number of security profile field level security settings you must update when you add a new field to an object. Rename unused profiles to include ‘dep_’ to move them out of your way. Always use the least possible number of page layouts. This decreases the likelihood of inconsistencies for different record types. Consider using Dynamic forms instead for ease of maintenance. If you consider adding Security Exclusion to bypass enforcement of user access permissions in triggers, you must evaluate this decision very carefully before implementation. While the Salesforce Platform allows you to bypass user permissions, Salesforce doesn't recommend it because CRM is a point in time system, and audits of the system can sometimes lead to inaccurate assessments. Use only letters, digits, spaces, hyphens, and underscores in profile names. Profile names that contain special characters, such as & / \ : * ? " < > | # % @ ! ( ) or non-ASCII glyphs, aren't supported by the metadata service and can cause metadata cache generation to fail or the mobile bundle not to download. For the failure behavior and workarounds, see Generate Metadata Cache . To create profiles by cloning standard profiles, see Create Custom Profiles for Customer Engagement Users .

In the Permission Set License Assignments for the user, click Edit Assignments, and then grant the Salesforce API Integration permission set license, which includes the Skip Life Sciences Trigger Handlers permission to bypass all trigger handlers. This only bypasses the trigger handlers for integration users. For all other users, these handlers continue to run. This can significantly increase the data load performance. However, this places the responsibility on customers to ensure data sanity during data migration. This approach is most suitable for environments that are live with active users. findings.name: Code Sets and Code Set Bundles
findings.detail: Having accurate information and standardized definitions is vital for the life sciences industry. Serious consequences can occur if organizations differ in their interpretation of a patient’s data. To avoid this scenario, the life sciences industry uses terminology systems that standardize the definitions of various situations and clinical data. These systems consist of subunits that the industry terms Coding, Codeable Concept, and Value Set. In the Life Sciences Cloud implementation of the Clinical data model, coding is termed code set and codeable concept is termed code set bundle. Code Set and Code Set Bundle are generic objects designed to store a wider variety of standardized codes required by the industry. They are aligned with FHIR R4. Codings, Codeable Concepts, and Value Sets To work effectively with these entities, it’s important to know what they are first. These entities are related to each other by way of hierarchies, concepts, or contexts. Recommendations for Using Code Sets and Code Set Bundles The type and range of codes required vary across organizations. The code requirements also depend on the type of care and services organizations provide and on the terminology systems they prefer. As such, Life Sciences Cloud doesn’t pre-populate these objects with any codes from terminology systems.

title: Codings, Codeable Concepts, and Value Sets
summary: To work effectively with these entities, it’s important to know what they are first. These entities are related to each other by way of hierarchies, concepts, or contexts. Codings relate to codeable concepts as a hierarchy. Basically, a codeable concept is a set of codings that represent the same...

findings.name: Codings, Codeable Concepts, and Value Sets
findings.detail: To work effectively with these entities, it’s important to know what they are first. These entities are related to each other by way of hierarchies, concepts, or contexts. Codings relate to codeable concepts as a hierarchy. Basically, a codeable concept is a set of codings that represent the same concept. However, a value set groups codings more loosely based on their context. Let’s take a closer look at what these entities are and how they’re structured.

findings.name: Coding
findings.detail: A coding, or code set in Life Sciences Cloud, represents a specific concept in the context of the terminology system that defines that concept. Multiple codings can represent the same real-world concept. However, their form depends on the terminology systems that define them and the versions of those systems. Codings consist of five components: Code, Display, System, Version, and User Selected. Code : The symbol that represents the concept. This code can be a string of numbers or characters, and not necessarily a word. If this attribute is absent in a coding, the terminology system has no defined code to represent that coding’s concept. Consider a code as the form of a coding. Display : The text that represents the meaning of the code and its concept. System : The URI of the terminology system that defines the concept of a coding. There are many terminology systems that the industry uses, like LOINC, SNOMED, RxNorm, ICD, and so on. Version : The version of the terminology system that defines the coding. As mentioned earlier, the form a coding takes can change across versions of the terminology system. User Selected : The boolean value that specifies whether the code is explicitly chosen by a user, as opposed to being selected by an automated algorithm. The expectation is that codings marked true for this attribute are more likely to be more accurate. If there are multiple codings that represent the same concept, codings marked true for this attribute tend to be more accurate. The Life Sciences Cloud implementation calls this attribute Primary. Here’s what a JSON sample for a coding looks like: <coding> <system value="http://snomed.info/id"/> <version value="International Release – 20130731"/> <code value="389145006"/> <display value="Allergic Asthma"/> <primary value="true"/> </coding> The Life Sciences Cloud implementation of coding doesn't support hierarchies because the FHIR definition of a coding doesn’t specify hierarchies. However, if your organization requires recording hierarchies, you can do that by adding a self-reference field to the Code Set object.

findings.name: Codeable Concept
findings.detail: A codeable concept represents a unique real-world concept that’s represented by codings. Codeable concepts bind together codings from across systems and versions, with the binding factor being the shared concept that those codings represent. For instance, let’s say that system 1 represents COVID-19 as C19 in version 2.31 and as CVD2019 in version 1.13, and system 2 represents COVID-19 as C204. The codeable concept that represents the real-world concept of COVID-19 binds all three codings together. The Life Sciences Cloud implementation of codeable concepts, called code set bundles, allow only 15 codings to be bound together while FHIR places no such constraint on codeable concepts. Here’s a JSON sample for a codeable concept: <codeableConcept> <!-- SNOMED code --> <coding> <system value="http://snomed.info/id"/> <version value="International Release – 20130731"/> <code value="389145006"/> <display value="Allergic Asthma"/> <primary value="true"/> </coding> <!-- ICD code --> <coding> <system value="urn:oid:2.16.840.1.113883.6.42"/> <version value="9"/> <code value="493.00"/> <display value="Extrinsic asthma - unspecified"/> <primary value="false"/> </coding> <text value="Atopic Asthma"/> </codeableConcept>

findings.name: Value Set
findings.detail: A value set, like a codeable concept, binds together different codings. However, a value set is grouped by the context of the codings that are bound together and isn’t a shared concept that aligns across terminology systems. For instance, while a codeable concept binds together codes representing a specific illness, a value set binds together code sets representing multiple illnesses. Life Sciences Cloud hasn’t explicitly implemented value sets using any object or component. However, to achieve a basic degree of grouping, you can group together code set records that have the same values for the Code Set Type field.

title: Recommendations for Using Code Sets and Code Set Bundles
summary: The type and range of codes required vary across organizations. The code requirements also depend on the type of care and services organizations provide and on the terminology systems they prefer. As such, Life Sciences Cloud doesn’t pre-populate these objects with any codes from terminology...

findings.name: Recommendations for Using Code Sets and Code Set Bundles
findings.detail: The type and range of codes required vary across organizations. The code requirements also depend on the type of care and services organizations provide and on the terminology systems they prefer. As such, Life Sciences Cloud doesn’t pre-populate these objects with any codes from terminology systems. As an admin, it’s up to you to populate these objects with the codes your organization needs. As the volume of required codes can be immense, we recommend that you use the Salesforce Data Loader to import code data into your orgs. Data Loader is a client application for the bulk import or export of data. Use it to insert, update, delete, or export Salesforce records. When importing data, Data Loader reads, extracts, and loads data from comma-separated values (CSV) files or from a database connection. When exporting data, it outputs CSV files. Check Considerations for Installing Data Loader for system requirements and other prerequisites to using Data Loader. Data integrity in your code database is vital to the smooth functioning of your organization. It’s likely that you don’t want your users to modify codes or add new ones. Such code changes can interfere with the automated approval processes you’ve set up and result in unintended authorizations. Therefore, we recommend modifying the access permissions on these objects after you populate these objects with the data your organization needs. You can give your users Read-Only access to these objects, or even prevent new record creation in them after your initial data loading.

findings.name: Set Up Healthcare Providers
findings.detail: Set up records for healthcare providers such as the practitioners (people) who take care of patients and the facilities (organizations) where patients are cared for. Practitioners include doctors, nurses, physical therapists, and other clinical staff. Facilities include hospitals, clinics, labs, and other organizations. When you set up healthcare provider data, create a record to represent the provider as a person or an organization, and then create a record to represent what the provider does. For organizations, create accounts with a Business record type. For people, create person accounts or contacts, but we strongly recommend person accounts. A person account combines an account and a contact. Person accounts are a better fit for healthcare providers who are their own independent entity with practicing rights at a number of locations. These individuals have their own unique identification number, such as a National Provider Identifier (NPI), which follows them regardless of where they work. If you map individual providers as contacts, there are limited capabilities for these records. To represent providers in terms of what they do, create healthcare provider records. These records store business-level details about the healthcare organization or person, such as the provider type. A person account record and a healthcare provider record combine to represent the FHIR Practitioner resource in Salesforce. The healthcare provider record is the base, and it references the person account record using the AccountId field. Note Model providers using both the Healthcare Provider object and person accounts to ensure they’re aligned to the FHIR Practitioner resource and they can appear in features such as provider search. If you model providers only as person accounts, you may not be able to use features such as provider search. To define the relationship between a practitioner and a facility, create a healthcare practitioner facility record that specifies the facility’s account record and the practitioner’s person account or contact record. Healthcare practitioner facility records represent the set of services that a practitioner provides at a specific location. Create additional records to store provider care specialties, certifications, education, and licenses, and for the payer network that a healthcare provider is affiliated with. Create Records for Healthcare Practitioners Create a person account record to represent a healthcare practitioner as a person and create a healthcare provider record to represent what the practitioner does. Create Records for Healthcare Organizations Create a business account record to represent a healthcare facility as an organization and create a healthcare provider record to represent what the organization does. Create Healthcare Facilities Create a healthcare facility record to represent the facility's physical, geographic, or functional details. A healthcare organization’s local branches or facilities need healthcare facility records that reference a business account and a healthcare provider record for that specific branch or facility. Connect Healthcare Practitioners with Facilities Define the relationship between a practitioner and a facility or organization by creating a healthcare practitioner facility record to represent the set of services that a practitioner provides at that facility or for that organization. Create Healthcare Facility and Payer Networks Create healthcare payer network records for insurance network groups, and then create healthcare facility network records to identify the payer network that a facility or organization is a part of. Create Care Specialty Records Healthcare providers can have multiple specialties and subspecialties. Create care specialty and healthcare provider specialty records to represent them. You can also classify specialties and subspecialties using taxonomy records. Create Care Provider Facility Specialty Records Create care provider facility specialty records to represent all the specialties that the practitioner provides at a specific facility or for a specific organization. These records help patients find a provider by the specialties they offer at a facility. Add Healthcare Provider Credentials Create records to store healthcare provider credentials such as accreditations, awards, board certifications, business licenses, and education.

findings.name: Set Up Participant Management
findings.detail: Participant Management streamlines the process of recruiting and enrolling participants in clinical trials by orchestrating each stage, from initial recruitment to enrollment. With this feature, you can provide a unified clinical trial portal experience for potential participants and clinical trial coordinators. Using Participant Management, users can gather critical participant information and support the evaluation of the effectiveness and safety of new medical treatments. Participant Management enables you to: Reduce the cost per eligible participant Reduce the cost per conversion of consenting participants Reduce the average time between registration and enrollment Improve participant registration and enrollment experience Lower your participant attrition rate The key components of Participant Management include:

findings.name: For Recruitment
findings.detail: During the recruitment phase, potential participants are referred to as Candidates. The following features support trial discovery, candidate matching, prescreening, and the application process. Criteria-Based Search and Filter feature to help users search for and find suitable clinical trials on an experience cloud site Omnistudio components to digitize initial prescreening and candidate registration processes Einstein Candidate Matching feature to automatically match candidates to clinical trials

findings.name: For Enrollment
findings.detail: After enrollment, Candidates become Participants and proceed to the next phase of the clinical trial. Build enrollment journey using Salesforce orchestration capabilities Flows to digitize the consent management process Invocable actions and flows to digitize the basic randomization process Participant Management Data Model and Permissions Participant Management uses a data model that’s FHIR R4 and USCDI-aligned to store its data and make it interoperable. Enable Participant Management Give users access to participant management features by enabling org preferences in your Salesforce org. By enabling Participant Management, you can streamline the recruitment and enrollment processes in clinical trials. Assign Permission Sets for Participant Management Users Participant Management offers five permission sets: Clinical Trial Manager, Clinical Trial Coordinator, Clinical Trial Participant, Clinical Trial Guest, and Clinical Trial Site Coordinator in Experience Cloud. Assign the necessary permission sets to users according to their roles. Add Data for Participant Recruitment and Enrollment Quickly create a record from an object’s home page. Clinical trial managers can create records that are necessary to use the features within Participant Management. Clinical trials are represented using care programs and research studies. Participant Recruitment Participant Management digitizes and optimizes candidate recruitment in clinical trials. With Participant Management, you can help users overcome recruitment challenges, save time, and improve trial efficiency. Participant Enrollment Participant Enrollment features help your clinical trial managers, coordinators, and participants to prepare, send, and view consent forms. It includes consent management and randomization features that can be combined to create a participant enrollment journey using Salesforce orchestration capabilities. Use Participant Management Participant Management helps organizations that conduct clinical research studies to make their recruitment and enrollment processes more efficient. Clinical trial coordinators or recruiters can use the Clinical Excellence Console app to track and monitor participant recruitment and enrollment progress. Clinical trial coordinators can use the Research Study Candidate page to add new Medication Requests, Health Conditions, Allergies, and Immunization records directly from the patient card.

findings.name: Participant Management
findings.detail: Here’s the summary of objects used in Participant Management. Use these objects to set up features that assist users in the recruitment and enrollment processes. Object | Purpose Research Study | Represents the details of a research study that include its design, execution, and oversight. Care Program | Represents the extended or additional details of a research study. Care Program Eligibility Rule | Represents a rule defining the inclusion and exclusion criteria for a research study or care program. This entity creates an association between Care Program and an Enrollment Eligibility Criteria. Care Program Enrollee | Represents a participant enrolled in a care program. Enrollment Eligibility Criteria | Represents criteria that define patient enrollment eligibility for one or more care programs. Care Program Status Period | Represents the historical changes to the status of a care program. Care Program Site | Represents the location details of the care program site. Research Study Candidate | Represents the details of the associated account and the status of the research participant or candidate. Care Program Detail | Represents the detail records related to the care program. Research Study Candidate Status Period | Represents the duration of time that a research participant or candidate is assigned a particular status. Research Study Relation | Represents the different related research studies. For example, a cardiac drug research study can be a part of a larger study encompassing cardiac diseases and diabetic diseases. Research Study Searchable Field | Represents a common dataset that includes multiple fields and values from multiple objects, and is used as the basis for searches related to research studies. Research Study Protocol Information | Represents details of the research study protocol document. Data Use Purpose | Represents the reason for contacting a prospect or customer, such as for consent verification. Authorization Form Data Use | Represents the data use consented to in an authorization form. Authorization Form | Represents the specific version and effective dates of a form that is associated with consent, such as consent forms. Authorization Form Text | Represents an authorization form’s text and language settings. findings.detail: Quickly create a record from an object’s home page. Clinical trial managers can create records that are necessary to use the features within Participant Management. Clinical trials are represented using care programs and research studies. Create a Care Program You can define a care program and associate it with the research study. To create a care program, define the program and the relationships and activities within it. Create a Care Program Detail Stores the keywords, focus, and condition, including other details of the care program of the study. You can use these details to manage and track specific details of the care programs within clinical trials. Create Care Program Sites Stores the name, related care program, and healthcare facility of the care program site. Use this information to manage and track specific details of the care program site within clinical trials. Create a Research Study Stores the name, title, and all the necessary essential details of the research study. You can use these details to manage and track specific details of the research studies within clinical trials. Add Consent Documents for Clinical Trials You can add consent documents to clinical trials by associating those documents with the related care program and defining their data use purpose. Add Clinical Data to View Patient Details Use the object’s homepage to create records for adding clinical data. This data helps site coordinators track a candidate’s medical information at a glance in the research study candidate’s lightening page.
